title: fix(js): unbind manufactured output div before detaching it in cleanup
description:
## Summary

Hook-based outputs (`useShinyOutputValue` and friends) bind into manufactured `<div class="shiny-react-output">` elements inside the registry's hidden container. `scheduleCleanup` removed that div from the container **before** the container-scoped `unbindAll(container)` ran (a `requestAnimationFrame` later), so Shiny's unbind — which finds bound elements with `$(scope).find(".shiny-bound-output")` — could never reach the detached div.

Consequences of the leak, verified against shiny's `srcts/src/shiny/bind.ts`:

- Shiny keeps a global, cumulative `bindingsRegistry`: `addBinding(id, "output")` on every bind, `removeBinding` only on unbind. A never-unbound element leaves its entry behind, so every subscribe/unsubscribe cycle added one stale registration, and Shiny's "Duplicate output IDs were found" warning counted one more output per visit (observed in a downstream app as counts matching tab-visit counts).
- The stale binding kept receiving server values for the deleted registry entry, logging `Output <id> not found` in the console until the next subscribe re-bound the id.

The fix unbinds the div explicitly (`Shiny.unbindAll(el, true)`) while it is still attached, then detaches it. A re-subscribe within the same frame is unaffected (the entry is kept and reused, as before).

## Verification

Regression test in `pkg-js/src/shiny-react/__tests__/output-registry.test.ts` emulates Shiny's bind bookkeeping faithfully — bind marks `.shiny-bound-output` and increments a per-id count; unbind decrements only elements it can still find. After three subscribe/unsubscribe cycles plus a fresh subscribe, the count must be exactly 1. Without the fix the in-loop assertion fails on the second cycle at 2 registrations (the leaked first cycle plus the live one); with the fix all 31 tests in the file pass.

title: fix(ci): build the wasm image directly instead of via the r-wasm reusable workflow
description:
Follow-up to #318. The reusable workflow failed on `r/v0.1.0`: its `rwasm::add_pkg()` call leaves `remotes = NA`, which resolves rwasm's built-in list of webR package forks (`r-wasm/shiny@webr` and friends) from GitHub with no PAT — `docker run` does not forward `GITHUB_TOKEN` into the container. The container's older pkgdepends reports the failure as an opaque `res_one_row_df(): nrow(out) must equal 1` (r-lib/pkgdepends#462 masks the real error).

We build only shinyreact (`dependencies = FALSE`, same as the reusable workflow), so the fork preferences are irrelevant and `remotes = NULL` skips that resolution entirely. Dependencies come from repo.r-wasm.org at runtime.

Verified on a scratch branch: the build produces `library.data.gz` (113 KB) + `library.js.metadata`, both now attached to https://github.com/posit-dev/shinyreact/releases/tag/r/v0.1.0.

title: ci(r): attach webR wasm assets to r/v* GitHub releases
description:
Closes #268.

`shinylive:::get_github_wasm_assets()` is the only path shinylive has for a
GitHub-installed R package: it looks up
`/repos/posit-dev/shinyreact/releases/tags/<RemoteRef>` and wants
`library.data*` + `library.js.metadata` assets on it. This repo has no R
release, so any `{shinylive-r}` block using shinyreact aborts at render.

`release-r-wasm.yaml` calls r-wasm/actions' `release-file-system-image`
reusable workflow on every published `r/v*` release. It builds a webR
filesystem image of `pkg-r/` plus dependencies and uploads the two assets.

Two repo-specific details:

- The package is in `pkg-r/`, so `packages: local::./pkg-r`.
- The release tag and the ref users install must be the same string:
  `pak::pak("posit-dev/shinyreact/pkg-r@r/v0.1.0")` records
  `RemoteRef: r/v0.1.0`. Verified that pak parses a slashed ref and that
  `gh::gh()` resolves `releases/tags/py/v0.1.0` against this repo, so the
  existing `r/v` prefix convention holds.
- `webr-image` is pinned to `ghcr.io/r-wasm/webr:v0.6.0` — the webR shinylive
  ships (R 4.6.0). An image built against another R version won't load.

`release` events only run workflows from the default branch, so this has to
merge before the `r/v0.1.0` tag and release are created. That unblocks
schloerke/presentation-2026-09-15-posit-conf-shinyreact#7.

If this turns out to need more work, the tag and release can be deleted and
re-cut.

title: docs: compare shinyreact with shiny.react and friends; explain reactive_output
description:
## Summary

Adds a website article, `articles/comparison.qmd`, contrasting shinyreact with Appsilon's `shiny.react` (the one-dot name collision), `reactR`/`reactable`, `shiny.fluent`/`shiny.blueprint`, `shiny-bindings`, and the whole-frontend templates. It has three parts: a side-by-side table against `shiny.react`; a "what travels the wire: markup or data" section that writes the same filter+table+caption task with `renderReact()`, `renderReactable()`, and `reactive_output`; and a "can they be combined" section documenting how to host a `shiny.react` tree and a `reactable` inside a shinyreact client via `ShinyOutput`.

Expands the Getting Started page (`index.qmd`) with "The power of `reactive_output`" and a one-output-drives-three-components example in Python, R, and `ui.tsx`. Links the README's related-work list to the article and adds `reactable` and `shiny.blueprint`.

The two interop paths were verified in a browser (chromote) against an R `page_react()` server with the current bundle: a shiny.fluent tree rendered through `renderReact()` re-renders on input change and its `*.shinyInput` components set Shiny inputs; a `reactable` renders, re-renders, and reports row selection to `getReactableState()`. Two gotchas are documented: `renderReact()` is not a `shiny.render.function`, so `reactDependency()` and `shinyReactDependency()` must be added to the page by hand; reactable needs the `data-reactable-output` attribute on the `ShinyOutput` element or its state never reaches the server.

## Verification

```sh
cd pkg-py/docs && quarto render index.qmd && quarto render articles/comparison.qmd
```

Both render. The `py/index.qmd` link warning is pre-existing (quartodoc output not generated locally). No code changes; docs only.

title: docs(skills): two silent failure modes of the hosted-widget recipe
description:
## What

`shiny-outputs.md`'s hosted-input recipe (#294) teaches the mechanism but not the two ways it silently fails. Both produce no error, no warning, and nothing in the console — the widget just doesn't update, or doesn't appear.

1. **An `update_slider()` / `updateSliderInput()` sent before the holder has rendered is dropped.** The section previously said updates "keep working against the id" with no qualifier — which is exactly the sentence that walks a reader in. Guidance: put the value in the widget's own constructor call; reach for `update_*` only for a value you don't know until after the widget exists.
2. **A holder that isn't visible on first paint is suspended**, so its render function never runs. `[py]` `suspend_when_hidden=False` / `[r]` `suspendWhenHidden = FALSE` is the opt-out.

Neither is a shinyreact bug — a plain `output_ui()` / `uiOutput()` app with no React anywhere loses the same update and suspends the same output. But the holder recipe makes both easy to walk into, which is why they belong in the skill.

## Where this came from

[samuelbharti/shinyreact-apps `docs/upstream`](https://github.com/samuelbharti/shinyreact-apps/tree/a43634883c47104326705065b33ea304707a2a05/docs/upstream) — a gap report from a downstream repo doing pixel-identical bslib→shinyreact ports, plus a draft patch. Their report verified both in R and explicitly flagged the Python side as unverified guesswork. This PR verifies Python.

Four other findings in that report I deliberately left out: `useShinyOutputValue`'s auto-prefixing vs. a user-written namespace helper (the only genuinely shinyreact-specific one, but only bites if you wrap the module hooks yourself); `bs_global_theme()`'s first arg being `version`; `loadSupport()` sourcing `R/` before `app.R`'s `library()` calls; `page_navbar()` markup varying with `getCurrentTheme()`. The last three are bslib/Shiny trivia, and the fourth only bites if you hand-write navbar TSX instead of hosting it.

## Verification

Two new e2e tests in `pkg-py/tests/playwright/test_hosted_input_timing.py`, each with a built-in control so neither can pass vacuously:

- `test_update_before_the_holder_renders_is_dropped` — startup `update_slider(value=30)`, holder renders on click, slider arrives at `9`. Then `#bump` fires the *identical* call once the widget exists and it lands at `30`. The first assertion fails if the update had been applied; the second fails if updates never work at all.
- `test_hosted_widget_hidden_on_first_paint_never_renders` — two identical holders in one `display: none` panel, differing only by `session.output(suspend_when_hidden=False)`. Only the opted-out one exists in the DOM. **Confirmed it fails when that one line is applied to both** (i.e. the test triggers unless the gotcha is real).

```
make py-test-e2e     # 30 passed (was 28)
make py-check        # All checks passed
R testthat           # pass, incl. the skills drift check
```

`make update-skills` run; `FEATURES.md` updated with both leaves marked `(e2e)` and noted as Shiny's behavior rather than ours.

## Not done

R halves of both claims rest on the upstream report's R verification plus the shared Shiny mechanism, not a test here — R has no e2e suite yet (#194).

title: refactor(examples): depend on the published @posit-dev/shinyreact
description:
Now that [`@posit-dev/shinyreact`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@posit-dev/shinyreact) is on npm, the two npm-tier examples drop the `file:../../pkg-js` placeholder they carried until the first publish. Both take `"^0.1.1"` from the registry.

**Net −16 lines**, because the placeholder needed scaffolding that a registry dependency does not:

- **`app.py` × 2** — the build-on-first-run block no longer pre-builds `pkg-js`. That existed because the `file:` dep's `exports` point into the uncommitted `dist-npm/`, so this app's own build could not resolve the package until someone built it. Now it is `npm install` + `npm run build`, nothing else.
- **`09-hmr/vite.config.js`** — removes `resolve.dedupe: ["react", "react-dom"]` and `server.fs.allow: [repoRoot]`. Both existed only because a `file:` dep is symlinked and brings its own `node_modules`. The published package ships no nested `node_modules` and takes React as a peer, so `npm ls react` shows one deduped copy without either setting.

Each example directory now installs and builds **outside a checkout of this repo** — copy it anywhere and it works.

## Verified, not assumed

Both examples wiped to nothing (`rm -rf node_modules www`) and rebuilt from the registry:

- `npm ls @posit-dev/shinyreact` → `0.1.1`; no nested `node_modules`; `react@19.3.0` deduped to one copy.
- `npm run build` → `www/ui.js` in both.
- **Vite dev server** for 09-hmr, since `fs.allow` only mattered in dev: `App.tsx` resolves `import { useShinyInput, ... } from "/node_modules/.vite/deps/@posit-dev_shinyreact.js"` and the Fast Refresh runtime is wired.
- **`shiny run app.py` from a clean state** for 11-npm-local: it printed `www/ui.js not found -- building the client bundle...`, installed, built, served HTTP 200, and the page carries `ui.js` with no `shinyreact.js` and no `#shinyreact-config` — this example's whole point.
- `make py-check-tests` 197 passed, `make js-test` 289 passed.

## Docs

Both `FEATURES.md` trees, both example READMEs, `examples/README.md`, and the status line of `decisions/2026-08-17-js-distribution.md` (whose "Remaining: first npm publish" is now done).

09-hmr's README gains the reverse recipe — `npm install ../../pkg-js` — for developing against uncommitted library changes, since `^0.1.1` otherwise means example builds no longer pick up `pkg-js/src` edits.

## No workflow changes needed

No workflow installs example `node_modules`: `R_EXAMPLES` in the Makefile is `01-hello` and `07-plotly` (neither npm-tier), and the example tests deliberately do not import `app.py` (`test_page.py` rebuilds the two-line ui instead, precisely to avoid triggering the build). Worth naming the gap that implies: **nothing in CI builds these two examples**, before or after this change. Pre-existing, not introduced here — filing it separately if you want it covered.

title: fix: version the shinyreact HTMLDependency by the JS package version
description:
The shinyreact dependency was versioned by the bundle file's **mtime**, so a page loaded:

```
/lib/shinyreact-1789252719/shinyreact.js
```

A number that says nothing about which `@posit-dev/shinyreact` release is on the page. Now that the package is published, use its version:

```
/lib/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js
```

Beyond being readable, this is checkable: an npm-tier app bundles its own copy of the runtime, and the page source now says which release the server is serving, so a version skew between the two is visible rather than inferred.

## How the version gets there

`make update-dist` writes `pkg-js/package.json`'s version to a one-line `version.txt` beside the bundle, in both packages — same committed-copy flow as the bundle itself. `_bundle_version()` (Python) and `.bundle_version()` (R) read it.

## The fallback chain, and why it kept the mtime

`version.txt` → **bundle mtime** → per-language last resort.

The mtime is demoted rather than deleted on purpose. It existed to cache-bust the browser after a `make update-dist`, and in a dev checkout that still matters: several `update-dist` runs share one npm version, so a pure-version scheme would serve a stale cached bundle after a rebuild. Keeping mtime as the fallback covers the partially-built case, but **note the tradeoff this PR does accept** — in a normal checkout `version.txt` is present, so between releases repeated `make update-dist` runs now produce the same URL and a browser may serve a cached bundle until a hard refresh. If that bites, `0.1.1+<mtime>` is a one-line change that restores busting while keeping the release legible; say the word.

A blank `version.txt` is treated as absent, not as an empty version — otherwise htmltools would build `/lib/shinyreact-/`.

The last-resort fallbacks are untouched, including their deliberate divergence: `[py]` the literal `"0.1.0"`, `[r]` `packageVersion("shinyreact")`.

## Not touched

`page_react_dep()` — the *app's* bundle — still versions by `ui.js`'s mtime. That is the cache-busting-during-development case the mtime scheme was designed for, and an app author's bundle has no npm version to use.

## Tests

Six new/rewritten, three per language, mirrored and cross-referenced by name per the both-languages rule:

| Claim | Python | R |
|---|---|---|
| version is the JS package version | `test_dep_version_is_the_js_package_version` | "versions by the JS package version" |
| missing `version.txt` → mtime | `test_dep_version_falls_back_to_mtime_without_version_file` | "version falls back to the bundle mtime" |
| blank `version.txt` → mtime | `test_dep_version_ignores_an_empty_version_file` | "ignores an empty version.txt" |

`make py-check-tests` 199 passed · `pyright` 0 errors · full testthat suite passes · wheel build confirms `shinyreact/www/version.txt` ships (it is inside the hatchling package dir; `inst/lib/shiny/` covers R).

`FEATURES.md`'s "Asset delivery" leaves updated, with `(test)` markers on the three pinned claims.

title: fix(py): type-check tests and examples; enforce the formatter
description:
Follow-up to #305, which turned up four gaps in the Python tooling. Closing them surfaced two annotations that were unusable from user code — which is the argument for closing them. One is ours; one is upstream.

## Ours: `page_react_html()` was not accepted by `App(ui=)`

It declared `HTMLTextDocument`, but `App(ui=)` accepts only py-shiny's `PageHtmlDocument` **subclass**. `shiny.App(page_react_html(...), server)` — a documented path — failed to type-check while working fine at runtime. The class is imported from `shiny.ui._page` because py-shiny exports `page_html()` but not its return class.

Pinned by `pkg-py/tests/test_typing.py`, which asserts nothing at runtime — **pyright failing is the test**, the only thing that can catch an over-narrow annotation.

## Upstream: `Jsonifiable` rejects the `dict` every app returns → posit-dev/py-shiny#2497

`Jsonifiable` spells its container arms as `List` and `Dict`. Both are **invariant** in their element types, so a render function returning `dict[str, int]` is not assignable to it, even though every element is itself `Jsonifiable`:

```
error: Argument of type "() -> dict[str, int]" cannot be assigned to parameter "_fn"
  of type "(() -> Jsonifiable) | (() -> Awaitable[Jsonifiable]) | None"
```

The single most ordinary thing a `reactive_output` does was a type error in five example apps.

I first fixed this locally with a covariant `Mapping`/`Sequence` alias, then **reverted that** in favor of filing [posit-dev/py-shiny#2497](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/issues/2497), with a reproducer that uses only py-shiny's documented custom-renderer extension point — no shinyreact involved. A local alias would have fixed our five call sites and left the same trap for everyone else writing a `Renderer[Jsonifiable]`.

So each site carries a suppression naming the issue instead:

```python
# py-shiny#2497: `Jsonifiable`'s `dict`/`list` arms are invariant, so a
# `dict` return is not assignable to it. Drop the ignore when that lands.
@reactive_output  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
def dist_data():
    return histogram(waiting, input.bins())
```

`grep 2497` finds all seven when it lands. Runtime behavior is unaffected — it is an annotation bug only.

## The four tooling gaps

| | Gap | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `py-check-format` ran `ruff check` only, never `ruff format --check` — the formatter's output was unenforced, and `test_output_error.py` had already drifted | added `ruff format --check`; reformatted the drifted file |
| 2 | Both ruff targets scoped to `pkg-py`, leaving `examples/` unlinted and unformatted — despite being shipped, read as documentation, and run by the default pytest invocation | both now cover `$(PATHS_PY) = pkg-py examples` |
| 3 | `[tool.pyright] include` was only `pkg-py/src/shinyreact`, so no test or example was type-checked | added `pkg-py/tests` and `examples`, and fixed the 50 pre-existing errors |
| 4 | `tests-e2e` asked for a `shiny[playwright]` extra py-shiny does not have (`theme, otel, test, dev, doc, add-test`) — uv reports this as a *warning*, not an error, on every sync | dropped the extra; `pytest-playwright` already pulls in `playwright` |

## The pre-existing errors, fixed in place

- **`test_input_handler.py` / `test_dep_discovery.py`** — `NO_NAME` / `NO_SESSION` / `ANY_NAME` casts, because these tests deliberately pass `None` for arguments the handlers ignore, which is part of what they assert.
- **`test_dep.py`** — `dep_source()` / `first_script()` / `first_stylesheet()` helpers. `HTMLDependency` normalizes these attributes in `__init__` but keeps them declared as the wider argument types; narrowing once lets the assertions read as assertions instead of type gymnastics.
- **`test_bookmark_restore.py`** — local `_config_html()` helper takes `Mapping`, same invariance root cause as #2497.
- **`test_set_react_page.py`** — `RenderedHTML`, the TypedDict `render()` actually returns.
- **`04-shadcn/app.py`** — `.loc[:, [...]]` instead of `[[...]]`; pandas types the latter as `Series | Unknown`, and `Series.to_dict()` takes no `orient=`.

## Verification

- `make py-check` — ruff lint + format clean, pyright **0 errors** over package + tests + examples, **198 passed**
- `make py-test-e2e` (chromium) — **28 passed**
- `uv sync --all-extras --all-groups` — no extras warning
- `FEATURES.md` updated for both the `page_react_html` return type and the #2497 suppression

title: chore(js): npm README + staged publishing, 0.1.1
description:
Follows the manual `0.1.0` bootstrap publish. Three changes.

**1. `pkg-js/README.md`** — 0.1.0 landed on npm with a bare package page. The README covers which tier needs this package at all (bundler vs. no-build), the `shinyreact_js="client"` pairing that stops the page loading React twice, the hook surface, and links to the site. Also adds `homepage` and `bugs` to `package.json` so the npm sidebar links somewhere.

**2. `pkg-js/package.json` 0.1.0 → 0.1.1.** Tarball goes 24 → 25 files as the README joins it.

**3. `release-js.yaml` stages instead of publishing.** `npm publish` → [`npm stage publish`](https://docs.npmjs.com/staged-publishing). CI uploads a pending version that nobody can install; a maintainer runs `npm stage approve <stage-id> --otp <code>` to publish it or `npm stage reject <stage-id>` to throw it away. Approval needs proof of presence, so CI cannot do it.

Auth is [trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers) (OIDC), now configured on the package against `posit-dev/shinyreact` + `release-js.yaml` with `npm stage publish` as the only permission. So:

- **no `NPM_TOKEN` secret** — and the package is set to "require two-factor authentication and disallow bypass 2fa tokens"
- provenance is automatic; the `--provenance` flag is gone
- the workflow cannot publish directly even if someone edits it

Also: job renamed `publish` → `stage`, and npm is upgraded to 11.x because `npm stage` and OIDC need 11.15+ while `.nvmrc`'s Node 22 bundles npm 10.x.

## Merging this releases nothing

`0.1.1` goes out by pushing `js/v0.1.1` after merge, which stages it for approval. That tag push is the first real exercise of this workflow — 0.1.0 could not use it, since npm cannot stage a package that does not exist yet and a trusted publisher cannot be configured until it does.

## Skill

`.claude/skills/release-shinyreact/SKILL.md` gets the approval handoff, the `npm stage` commands, the trusted-publishing setup, and the bootstrap exception. It says explicitly that a green `release-js` run means *staged*, not released, so a future agent doesn't report a JS release as done off a green check.

## Not in scope

Python and R versions are untouched. `make update-dist update-skills update-examples` is clean against main.

title: test(py): drive servers with shiny's `local_server` fixture
description:
py-shiny main ships a built-in `local_server` pytest fixture — an already-started `test_server()` session — so a test needs neither the `with` block nor its own `APP = Path(...)` constant.

## What changed

Every Python `test_server()` call site now uses the fixture: `pkg-py/tests/test_in_memory_server.py` and the seven example suites (`01`, `02`, `05`, `06`, `07`, `08`, `10`).

The fixture defaults to `app.py` beside the test file; ours live in `tests/`, so each file carries a one-line mark pointing it a directory up:

```python
pytestmark = pytest.mark.parametrize("local_server", ["../app.py"], indirect=True)
```

`01-hello` uses the same mark to cover both `../app.py` and `../app-core.py`, replacing its hand-rolled `APPS` parametrize. `test_in_memory_server.py` uses per-test marks instead, since its apps are the Playwright fixture apps under `playwright/apps/`.

## Two py-shiny API changes surfaced

- **`make_scope()` is no longer a context manager** — `a = local_server.make_scope("a")`.
- **A `req()` failure now reports `status == "silent"`** rather than leaving the previous value in place (posit-dev/py-shiny#2492). `test_output_error_statuses` asserted the old behavior; it now asserts the blank, matching what the browser shows. `pkg-r/tests/testthat/test-render.R` called this out as a deliberate R/Python divergence in a comment — it is not one anymore, so the comment is updated.

## Docs

`shinyreact-build-app`'s `references/testing.md` + `SKILL.md`, `shinyreact-convert-app/SKILL.md`, `examples/README.md`, `pkg-py/README.md`, `pkg-py/docs/articles/testing.qmd`, and three `examples/*/FEATURES.md` leaves. `make update-skills` run for the shipped copies.

## Verification

- `make py-check` — ruff clean, pyright 0 errors, **197 passed**
- `make py-test-e2e` (chromium) — **28 passed**
- `devtools::test()` in `pkg-r` — **323 passed**, 0 failures

title: test: drive servers in memory with test_server() / testServer()
description:
[py-shiny#2470](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/pull/2470) added `shiny.testserver.test_server()`, the Python counterpart to R's `testServer()`: it runs an app's server against a mock connection, no browser and no subprocess.

That suits shinyreact unusually well. A `ui.tsx` server contains *only* reactive computation, so "input X produces output Y" **is** the server, and the JSON a test asserts is exactly what `useShinyOutputValue()` receives:

```python
with test_server(APP) as ts:
    ts.set_inputs(bins=9)
    assert ts.get_output("dist_caption") == "272 eruptions in 9 bins"
```

## Package tests

- **`pkg-py/tests/test_in_memory_server.py`** — three tests, reusing the Playwright fixture apps as-is:
  - `reactive_output` publishing through a real session. `test_reactive_output.py` only reaches `Renderer.transform()`, so nothing pinned the wire path.
  - module namespace isolation via `ts.make_scope("a")` — the in-memory twin of `playwright/test_module_namespaces.py`, which spends a browser on a purely server-side claim.
  - output error statuses and messages — the server half of `playwright/test_output_error.py`.

  It needs no `tests-e2e` extras, so it belongs in the unit suite rather than the Playwright subtree.
- **`pkg-r/tests/testthat/test-render.R`** — the R mirrors of the last two, cross-referenced by name, with the divergence stated where it exists: R's `testServer()` **raises** (`expect_error(output$answer, class = "shiny.silent.error")`) where Python's reports `.status`.

## Example tests

One Python test file per example with a server (01, 02, 05, 06, 07, 08, 10), plus R counterparts for the two that ship an `app.R` — 07-plotly had no R test directory at all, so it gains `tests/testthat.R` too.

**Two `FEATURES.md` leaves turned out to be wrong**, and are now corrected and pinned: 05-temperature and 08-input-handler both claimed `input.x()` is `None` before the client's first message, so the server returns `None` / `"—"`. It raises a silent exception — those branches are unreachable from a real client, and the outputs never render. That is the kind of claim only a test that drives the app can falsify, which is the argument for this whole PR in one leaf.

`(test)` markers added across seven example trees for what these pin: wire shapes, zone thresholds, pluralization, the two-step event handling, the `AsIs` wrapping that makes a one-bin R result a JSON array, and the plotly payload's `plotly-main`-but-not-`plotly-binding` dependency split.

`examples/01-hello/tests/test_faithful.py` opened with "`app.py` calls `set_react_page()` at module scope, so the two outputs' logic cannot be unit tested". No longer true anywhere in the tree.

## Docs and skills

- `pkg-py/docs/articles/testing.qmd` and its R mirror `pkg-r/vignettes/articles/testing.Rmd` are retitled **Testing** and gain a server-testing half ahead of the wire-tap material, tabbed py/R. Both render; headings and tabsets verified in the built HTML.
- **The shipped skills were actively wrong.** `shinyreact-build-app/references/testing.md` said *"`[py]` has no `testServer()` equivalent … This is a real gap, not an oversight in your app."* It now documents `test_server()` alongside R's, and `shinyreact-convert-app`'s verify phase goes from three layers to four. `make update-skills` run.
- Four things are documented because each cost time to find: pass an **absolute `Path`** (a relative one resolves against the test file's directory); an **untyped** id needs no `:shinyreact.default` suffix (both Python handlers are no-ops) but a **typed** id does, since the suffix is what runs the handler; an **event** input needs two `set_inputs` calls, mirroring the client's register-at-mount then send; and an **unset** input means `status == "silent"`, not a `None` value.

`test_server()` is newer than shiny 1.7.0 — which this repo already depends on via the py-shiny `main` git dep — and the docs and skills say so explicitly.

## Two upstream issues filed from this work

- [posit-dev/py-shiny#2492](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/issues/2492) — a silent `req()` failure is invisible in memory: `get_output()` keeps the previous value with `status="ok"` while the browser blanks the output, so a test can pass asserting a value the user cannot see. Includes R evidence that `testServer()` does *not* retain the stale value, which is the parity rationale the current behavior cites.
- [posit-dev/py-shiny#2493](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/issues/2493) — `status == "silent"` means "never rendered", the exact inversion of what Shiny already taught `req()`/silent to mean. Suggests `"never-rendered"`, which also frees the name for #2492.

Neither blocks this PR; the one leaf that would have asserted the missing behavior is written as a comment naming the issue instead.

## Drive-by

`pkg-r/tests/testthat/test-examples.R` read every file in an example directory and *then* filtered to `app.R` + `www/`, so the new `__pycache__` produced 208 `readLines()` warnings. It filters first now.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest` — 195 passed; `tox` py310 and py314 — 195 each
- `Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local()'` — 320 pass, 0 warn (was 208 warn)
- `make r-check` — 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
- each example's tests pass **from the app directory**: `pytest`, `shiny::runTests()`
- both doc sites render

title: feat: npm-tier example with no server JS and no config tag (#261)
description:
`examples/11-npm-local` is the Old Faithful app (`app.py` + `app.R` over one client) at the npm tier with **nothing else on the page**.

#264 gave npm-tier apps `shinyreact_js="client"`, which omits `shinyreact.js` but still emits the `#shinyreact-config` tag. This app needs neither, so its whole page is:

```python
ui = page_bare(page_react_dep(src_dir=_APP_DIR / "www", name="npm-local"))
```

- **no `shinyreact.js`** — one React and one hook registry on the page
- **no config tag, so no protocol handshake** — nothing on the page is versioned separately from the app that shipped it

The client imports `@posit/shinyreact` from the repo-relative `file:../../pkg-js` placeholder, same as `examples/09-hmr`, until the first npm publish.

## The deletion

The config-tag strict mode is gone. It made a missing tag — or a tag with no `protocolVersion` — throw rather than log, but only in the npm build, on the reasoning that an independently installed client meeting a tagless page means the server predates the protocol. It also banned the simplest page there is. With nothing opting in, `requireShinyReactConfigTag()`, `isShinyReactConfigTagRequired()`, the flag and the test-only reset are removed, along with the two branches in `bookmark.ts` and `examples/testing/mount.ts`'s reset call.

Unchanged: a major-version mismatch still throws visibly in both builds, and a tag with no `protocolVersion` still logs an error. #264's double-load warning is untouched.

Docs corrected where they justified the tag by the old behavior — `page_react()` / `page_react_html()` / `set_react_page()` / `ReactApp()` (py + R + `page_react.Rd`), `_dep.py` / `dep.R`, `FEATURES.md`: the tag is still emitted under `shinyreact_js="client"`, but because it carries the protocol version and any bookmark restore payload, not because the client hard-errors without it.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| vitest | 277 passed |
| pytest | 161 passed |
| testthat | 270 passed |
| pyright / tsc / ruff / prettier | clean |

Plus the app itself, driven in a browser on the Python server: page carries no `shinyreact.js` and no config tag, slider → server → SVG round-trips, no console errors.

## Note on scope

An earlier revision of this PR shipped `pkg-js/dist-npm/` inside the wheel and `inst/` so an app could install `@posit/shinyreact` from `.venv` / `renv` (#261's actual proposal). That worked — portable lockfile, one symlink resolving for both languages — but it is not in this PR; the example uses the repo-relative placeholder instead, and #261 keeps the question. The evidence is recorded in a comment there.

title: fix(js): don't console.error() a silent req()/validate() error
fix(js): queue ShinyOutput's bindAll() behind overlapping nested scopes
description:
Follow-up to #299, which closed #298 by deduping `bindAll()` calls per scope element.

## The finding

Deduping per scope element covers siblings that share one parent. It does not cover nested parents, which are two different elements. Each `ShinyOutput` passes its own parent as scope, so an output inside a container and another inside a container nested within it look up two different keys in `pendingBindAll`, are never related to each other, and both scans run. `bindAll` is descendants-only, so the outer scan walks the inner element too.

That matters because Shiny's own guard is not atomic. In `bindOutputs` (`shiny.js`, 1.14.0):

```js
if ($el.hasClass("shiny-bound-output")) { continue; }   // 5822
await shinyAppBindOutput(id, bindingAdapter);           // 5826
$el.addClass("shiny-bound-output");                     // 5828
bindingsRegistry.addBinding(id, "output");              // 5833
```

Two scans overlapping the window between 5822 and 5828 both pass the check and both reach 5833. Shiny then reports the id as "2 outputs" though one element exists. Instrumenting `addBinding` in a real app showed exactly that: every remaining duplicate had two registrations, 0 to 1 ms apart, from two nested scopes (a `<details>` and the `<div>` containing it; a card body and a `<div>` inside it).

## The fix

Finding the overlap needs the in-flight scopes to be walkable, and a `WeakMap` is not. A `Set` now sits alongside it, and `dedupedBindAll` queues a scan behind every in-flight scan whose scope contains, or is contained by, its own. Every one rather than the first: one scan can be running while another is already queued behind it, and queueing behind only the first leaves the same overlap in a narrower window.

The `Set` holds a strong reference where the map's is weak. Its comment says so, including the case it cannot survive: a `bindAll` that never settles would pin its scope element for good. The window is one bind pass, and the entry count is the number of concurrently scanning scopes, not the number of outputs.

## Changes

- **`pkg-js/src/shiny-output.tsx`**: `inFlightScopes` next to `pendingBindAll`, `overlappingPasses()`, and the queue-behind-all branch in `dedupedBindAll`. `queueBindAll` now takes a promise rather than a pass, so `refreshBindAll` and the exact-scope path are unchanged in behavior.
- **`pkg-js/src/__tests__/shiny-output.test.tsx`**: three tests. Nested scopes serialize; a scope overlapping two outstanding passes waits for both; two unrelated sibling scopes still scan concurrently.
- **Bundles**: `pkg-js/dist`, `pkg-r/inst/lib/shiny`, `pkg-py/src/shinyreact/www` rebuilt, the same set #299 touched.

## Deliberately not done

- **No change to Shiny's guard.** The non-atomic check is Shiny's; this only stops shinyreact from handing it overlapping scans.
- **No serializing of unrelated scopes.** Two parents side by side share no elements. The third test pins that, so this cannot quietly become "one scan at a time".
- **No Playwright test.** Six standalone pages built to reproduce the overlap stayed clean, likely because React runs child effects before parent ones, so in a small tree the inner scan settles before the outer starts. The unit test reaches the overlap deterministically by controlling when each `bindAll` promise settles, and fails without the fix.

## Verification

```
npm test              ->  289 passed (29 files)
npm run lint          ->  clean
npm run format-check  ->  clean
```

Two of the three new tests were each confirmed to fail on `main`: the nested-scope test, and the wait-for-all test when `Promise.allSettled` is weakened to the first pass only.

Against `3ff0648` in a real app: seven reported ids dropped to one, and the one left comes from that app's own code calling `Shiny.bindAll` directly, outside this path. Binding time unchanged: median 2.17s before and 2.18s after, three runs each, timed from navigation until every output carried `.shiny-bound-output`.

title: fix(js): dedupe ShinyOutput's bindAll() calls to the same scope
description:
Closes #298.

## The finding

#298 found that two or more `ShinyOutput` siblings sharing one parent make the browser log a "Duplicate output IDs" warning naming each of them, even though there is really only one DOM element per id. Confirmed with a minimal repro (no bslib, no theme, nothing but shinyreact) and with a real app hosting four `renderUI()` widgets in one sidebar.

`ShinyOutput`'s mount effect calls `Shiny.bindAll(el.parentElement)`, since `bindAll`'s own `find()` only looks at descendants (`pkg-js/src/shiny-output.tsx`'s own comment explains why). When several `ShinyOutput` siblings share one parent, React fires all their mount effects in the same commit, so several `bindAll()` calls start scanning that same parent close together.

Shiny's own `bindOutputs()` is `async`, and marks a matched element `.shiny-bound-output` only *after* an `await` for that element resolves. So several overlapping calls each see the others' not-yet-marked elements as unbound, and each one binds them. Every element does end up correctly bound once the race settles, but Shiny's own "Duplicate output IDs" check reads a separate, module-level registry that records one entry every time an element gets bound and never clears it. The count settles at the number of siblings that raced (two for two, four for four) and stays there for the life of the page.

## The fix

Stays entirely inside `ShinyOutput`, no change to Shiny core. One `bindAll()` pass per parent element at a time:

- A `ShinyOutput` whose mount effect runs while another one's pass for the same parent is still in flight reuses that pass, instead of starting a second, overlapping scan of the same DOM.
- An unbind under that parent (an id or `tagName` change, an unmount, or React StrictMode's synthetic mount-cleanup-mount double invoke) queues a fresh pass for after the in-flight one settles, rather than starting one at once. Starting one at once, while an earlier pass for the same parent is still unsettled, is exactly the overlap this fixes, whichever `ShinyOutput` triggers it.
- Once a pass settles it is forgotten, so a later mount under the same parent starts a fresh one. A `bindAll` that throws synchronously is never shared; the next `ShinyOutput` under that parent makes its own attempt.

One observable consequence: the re-bind after an id or `tagName` change now lands a microtask later, queued behind whatever pass is in flight, instead of synchronously.

The first commit on this branch dropped the cached pass on every unbind instead of queuing it, which reopened the overlap for a sibling unmounting early and for StrictMode's double invoke; ec7df62 replaced that with the queue. Details in the comment below.

## Changes

- **`pkg-js/src/shiny-output.tsx`**: `runBindAll()`, `dedupedBindAll()`, and `refreshBindAll()`, keyed by the mount effect's own parent element in a module-level `WeakMap`. No change to `ShinyOutput`'s public props, rendered markup, or the `unbindAll` side.
- **`pkg-js/src/__tests__/shiny-output.test.tsx`**: three tests asserted the old behavior directly (three siblings under one parent producing three independent `bindAll()` calls); jsdom's synchronous mock `bindAll` can never reproduce the real, async-only race, so this suite could not have caught the bug on its own. Those three now assert the deduped behavior. Five tests that checked the re-bind after an id or `tagName` change now await it. One new test renders a single `ShinyOutput` under `React.StrictMode` with a controlled, not-yet-settled first call and asserts `bindAll` is called exactly once while that call is pending. 43 tests in this file, 282 in the package.
- **`FEATURES.md`**: the `ShinyOutput` leaves updated to match; the "several `ShinyOutput`s bind independently" leaf replaced by the one-pass-per-parent leaves; one leaf added under the #286 recipe.
- **`pkg-js/dist/shinyreact.js`, `pkg-py/src/shinyreact/www/`, `pkg-r/inst/lib/shiny/`**: rebuilt and synced (`make update-dist`).
- **`pkg-py/tests/playwright/test_bind_dedupe.py` + `apps/bind_dedupe/`** (added in review, see below): the e2e coverage this PR originally deferred.

## Verified directly, in a browser

Built the IIFE bundle and swapped it into a real running app (four `renderUI()`-hosted inputs in one sidebar, the shape #298 found this in), before the fix and after each revision of it:

- Before: 10 "Duplicate output IDs" warnings in the console, each naming all four inputs as "4 outputs".
- After: 0 warnings, and `bound: 4 inputs, 5 outputs` reported correctly (four hosted inputs, one plot).
- Values still arrive at the server on connect, and a server-side `updateSelectizeInput()` still drives a dependent hosted widget correctly.

The two-sibling minimal repro from #298: 4 warnings before, 0 after.

## Deliberately not done

- **No change to Shiny core's `bindOutputs()`.** A fix there (marking an element bound before its async work starts, not after) would also work, and might be the more fundamental place for it, but that is a different package with different maintainers. This PR only changes what shinyreact itself controls.
- **No change to how `ShinyOutput` picks its scope.** Passing something other than `el.parentElement` (a private wrapper element, say) was ruled out: `ShinyOutput` deliberately renders no wrapper, for CSS reasons settled in #61.

## Review follow-ups

Two commits added after the first review pass.

### `16215e0` — only share a pass that actually scanned the element

Code review found three holes in the dedupe above.

- **A silently unbound output.** `Shiny.bindAll(scope)` scans `scope`'s children when it starts, so a `ShinyOutput` mounting under that parent *after* a pass started could not be bound by it — but it reused it anyway, and Shiny says nothing about an element it never saw. The element stayed dead, with no warning and no error. A pass now records the children it scanned (`BindAllPass.covers`); an element it does not cover queues its own pass behind it. A pass that is queued but has not started yet is still shared: it scans when it runs, so it will see the new element.
- **A poisoned parent.** A *queued* pass whose `bindAll` threw synchronously threw before the `WeakMap` was updated, leaving its rejected promise cached as that parent's pending pass forever — every later `ShinyOutput` under it reused that rejection and never bound. Map bookkeeping now lives in one `track()` helper, so every pass cleans up after itself.
- **An unhandled rejection.** The queued chain had no `.catch`, so an unmount-queued pass that rejected surfaced as an unhandled rejection with nothing logged; and it re-dereferenced `window.Shiny.bindAll` unguarded when it ran later. A queued pass now re-reads `window.Shiny?.bindAll` (no-op if Shiny is gone), and logs `[shinyreact] ShinyOutput bindAll failed:` when no mounted `ShinyOutput` is left waiting to log it with an id.

Four unit tests added for these (39 in the file, 286 in the package).

### `ff2bdcc` — the Playwright test this PR had deferred

`pkg-py/tests/playwright/apps/bind_dedupe/` hosts two `@render.ui` holders side by side under one parent, plus a third that mounts one React commit later. The fixture wraps `Shiny.bindAll` to hold each pass open for 250ms *after* its own scan — the scan keeps its real timing, only the settling is delayed — so the late mount reliably lands while a pass is in flight rather than in a sub-millisecond window.

- `test_sibling_shiny_outputs_log_no_duplicate_id_warning` captures `page.on("console")` and asserts nothing matching `Duplicate` / `Shared` after all binding has settled. Against `main`'s bundle it fails with 7 warnings, the first being `- "widgets_a": 2 outputs` / `- "widgets_b": 2 outputs`.
- `test_shiny_output_mounting_during_a_pass_is_still_bound` asserts the late holder gains `shiny-bound-output`, renders its selectize, and its value reaches the server. Against `7e1aa81`'s bundle (dedupe without the coverage check) it fails with the element stuck at `shiny-html-output` and the echo line empty.

Both were run against the pre-fix bundles to confirm they fail, which is the point — the jsdom unit tests assert call counts against a synchronous mock that marks nothing bound, so they could never have caught either symptom.

`FEATURES.md` leaves updated for all of the above, with `(e2e)` markers on the two now-pinned browser claims.

## Verification

```
cd pkg-js
npm run lint          -> tsc --noEmit, clean
npm run format-check  -> prettier --check ., clean
npm test              -> 286 passed
npm run build         -> both targets build clean
make update-dist      -> no diff (CI's build job)
make py-check-tests   -> 159 passed
make py-check-types   -> pyright, 0 errors
make py-test-e2e      -> 26 passed
```

Please check whether this makes sense before merging. Feel free to extend this PR (a different scoping strategy, more tests, anything else) if you'd rather take a different approach, or if #298 turns out to need more than this.

title: docs: host real Shiny input widgets via a dynamic-UI holder (#286)
description:
Closes #286.

## The finding

#286 asks for a `ShinyInput` component so a real `sliderInput()` / `selectizeInput()` can live in a `ui.tsx` client. A hosted input widget needs three things:

1. the widget's own JS/CSS dependency on the page (ion-rangeslider, selectize),
2. the input binding's `initialize()` pass,
3. `bindAll()`.

`ShinyOutput` does only (3), which is why it can't host an input — the issue is right about that. But the proposed component only adds (2); with client-authored markup, (1) never happens, so the binding doesn't exist to be initialized.

Shiny's own dynamic-UI output does all three: the html-output binding calls `renderContent()`, which loads the dependencies and then runs `initializeInputs()` **and** `bindAll()`. `ShinyOutput` already hosts that path (it's how the dynamic-plotly e2e test works), so the recipe needs no new code:

```python
@render.ui                        # [r] output$widgets <- renderUI({ ... })
def widgets():
    return ui.input_slider("bins", "Bins", min=1, max=50, value=9)
```

```jsx
<ShinyOutput id="widgets" className="shiny-html-output" />
```

`input.bins()` / `input$bins` then arrives exactly as in a classic app, and `update_slider()` / `updateSliderInput()` keeps working against the id.

## Changes

- **`pkg-py/tests/playwright/apps/dynamic_input/` + `test_hosted_input.py`** — browser-verified, not just reasoned about: `input_slider` becomes a real ionRangeSlider (`.irs--shiny`, `#bins` gains `shiny-bound-input`) and `input_selectize` a real selectize control; `input.bins()` is `9` and `input.letter()` is `"a"` on the server; dragging the slider to its max pushes `50`; `ui.update_slider()` / `ui.update_selectize()` still target the hosted widgets by id.
- **`.claude/skills/shinyreact-build-app/`** — the recipe in `references/shiny-outputs.md` plus a pointer in `SKILL.md`, framed as the deliberate exception to React-owned input state rather than a new default. `make update-skills` run; drift tests pass.
- **`FEATURES.md`** — new "Traditional Shiny *input* widgets inside a React tree (#286)" section under Traditional Shiny interop, `(e2e)` marked, including the explicit "there is no `ShinyInput`, and none is needed" leaf so the next reader doesn't re-derive this.

## Deliberately not done

- **No `ShinyInput` component.** It would be a second way to spell a path Shiny already owns, and the shape in the issue silently skips dependency delivery.
- **No R code or R test.** The recipe is pure interop with Shiny's own path; R needs only `renderUI()`, which is documented in the skill. Untested there because R has no e2e suite (#194).

## Verification

```
uv run pytest pkg-py/tests/playwright/test_hosted_input.py --browser chromium -o addopts=  ->  3 passed
uv run pytest pkg-py -q                                                                    ->  149 passed
```

title: ci: run py-test-e2e when a PR leaves draft
description:
## Summary

`py-test-e2e` in `check-py.yaml` is gated on `github.event.pull_request.draft != true`, and `pull_request`'s **default event types** are `opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened` — no `ready_for_review`. Those two facts combine badly: a PR opened as a draft never runs the e2e suite before merge. The `opened` event skips the job, and clicking "Ready for review" delivers an event this workflow ignores, so nothing re-evaluates the gate. The suite only ran afterwards, from the `push` to `main` (where there is no `pull_request` payload, so `null != true` is true and it runs).

Concretely, on #290: `py-check: success`, `py-test-e2e: skipped`, and `gh pr checks` reported a cheerful "15 passed". The e2e suite had not run. It ran on the merge commit and passed, so nothing was broken — but pre-merge that PR was reviewed and merged with the browser suite silently sitting out.

Fix is `types:` on both workflows:

- **check-py** — add `ready_for_review` so undrafting re-evaluates the gate and runs the job.
- **pr-done** — same list. It is the one required status check, so it has to re-run and wait for the newly started e2e job. Without it, undrafting kicks off a job nothing gates on, and a red e2e run can sit behind a green `pr-done`.

Listing the three defaults explicitly alongside `ready_for_review` is required — naming `types:` at all replaces the default set rather than adding to it.

`check-py` is the only workflow with a draft gate (`grep -n draft .github/workflows/*.yaml`), so nothing else needs the same treatment.

## Verification

Both files still parse, with the intended trigger:

```console
$ python -c "import yaml; print(yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/check-py.yaml'))[True]['pull_request']['types'])"
['opened', 'synchronize', 'reopened', 'ready_for_review']
```

The real check is this PR itself. It is opened as a draft, so `py-test-e2e` should skip on `opened` and then **run when I mark it ready** — which is exactly what does not happen on `main` today. I will confirm that transition before taking it out of draft for review.

Found while working on #291. Related: #288, #290.

title: fix: no Bootstrap on a themeless page (#285)
description:
Fixes #285. Closes #287.

Shiny's `theme = NULL` default attaches Bootstrap — 3.4.1 plus its accessibility plugin in R, which errors against a newer jQuery and can stop Shiny from finishing its connection. A `ui.tsx` page never asked for it: the client owns styling.

`page_bare()` — and so `page_react()` / `set_react_page()` — now attaches **no Bootstrap** when no `theme` is passed: jQuery, Shiny's own JS/CSS, and a viewport meta tag, nothing else. Passing a `theme` keeps the old passthrough, Bootstrap included.

The issue's own repro, served:

```
jquery[3.7.1];shiny-css;shiny-busy-indicators;shiny-javascript;bootstrap[9999];shinyreact;brtest
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"/>
```

No `bootstrap-3.4.1` CSS, no accessibility plugin. Python — which was loading Bootstrap **5** CSS/JS plus ionrangeslider, selectize and bootstrap-datepicker — is now down to jQuery, `shiny.min.css`, `shiny.js` and the busy indicators.

## How

- **R:** `htmltools::suppressDependencies("bootstrap")`, the fix from the issue, applied *only* on the themeless path so a real bslib Bootstrap 5 (same dependency name) is never stripped. The suppressed dependency is still *named* `bootstrap` — an empty one at version `9999`, which is how `suppressDependencies()` works — and emits no tags.
- **Python:** builds the page tag directly instead of calling `page_bootstrap()`, because that omits Shiny's own CSS on the assumption the Bootstrap CSS bundles it; `shiny_deps()` brings it back. Uses the public `shiny.html_dependencies`.
- **The viewport meta is kept** — the one thing worth having from the Bootstrap dependency; without it a phone renders the page at 980px. Emitted via `tags$head()` / `head_content()` so it reaches the document's real `<head>` rather than the nested body tag Shiny wraps a page in.

## Shape

No new argument: Bootstrap is opt-in via `theme=` (`bslib::bs_theme(version = 3)` for the classic stack, `shiny.ui.Theme()` in Python), and `theme = NULL` reads the same as omitting it. That answers the issue's "an argument name, where it lives?" — a knob every `ui.tsx` app would have to set is worse than the right default.

**This changes a default, so it belongs in release notes:** an app relying on the accidental Bootstrap for styling loses it.

## Tests

Three per language, cross-referenced by name: no Bootstrap without a theme (`page_bare` and `page_react`), and Bootstrap still attached when themed — the half that catches the suppression leaking into a real theme. R: 277 pass / 0 fail. Python: 155 pass. `FEATURES.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `page_bare.Rd` updated.

## Closes #287

#287 asked whether two conversion-checking R scripts belonged in this repo. The answer was no — the *questions* they ask went into `shinyreact-convert-app` Phase 5 in #289 — and the issue stayed open on one condition: re-check whether that recipe still earns its place once #285 is fixed.

It does. The Bootstrap 3 finding was one field of five; `connected`, `errors` and the console-first rule catch the failure mode that made #285 *fatal* rather than merely heavy, and that mode is untouched by this PR. So is the render-time dependency schedule.

But the recipe went subtly wrong *because* of this fix: it reads `assets` by library, which implies Bootstrap should match on both sides. Now the port loads none, so the check fires on every conversion. The second commit names that as expected — and as the to-do it really is: every `btn` / `form-control` / `container` the original's markup leaned on is unstyled in the port until the components supply it. `make update-skills` run; `test_skills.py` 8 passed, R skills tests pass.

Credit to @samuelbharti, whose gist in #287 found the Bootstrap 3 this PR removes.

title: test(py): move test_wire_tap.py into the Playwright suite
description:
## Summary

`pkg-py/tests/test_wire_tap.py` unit-tests `WireTap` against a `FakePage` and never launches a browser, so it looked like a plain unit test and lived with them. But it imports `shinyreact.playwright`, which imports `playwright.sync_api` — a `tests-e2e` dependency. In an environment without that group it failed at *collection*, taking the entire unit suite down with it:

```
ERROR pkg-py/tests/test_wire_tap.py
ImportError: shinyreact.playwright requires the `playwright` package, which is a test-only dependency.
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Interrupted: 1 error during collection !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
```

That is precisely the run `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` excludes `pkg-py/tests/playwright` in order to keep dependency-free. CI never saw it because `check-py.yaml` syncs `--all-extras --all-groups`, so `playwright` is always present there; it only bites a contributor whose env is narrower than the documented setup.

So: move the file beside the suite whose dependencies it needs. The membership rule for `pkg-py/tests/playwright/` is **"needs the `tests-e2e` group"**, not "drives a browser" — written down in `pyproject.toml`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `.claude/references/playwright-e2e-tests.md`, since the next test like this will look equally unit-ish. Cross-references in `test_wire_frames.py`, `pkg-r/tests/testthat/test-wire-tap.R`, and `docs/2026-08-27-verifying-shinyreact-apps.md` follow the file.

No test bodies change; this is a move plus comments.

## Verification

In a venv with the package, `pytest`, and **no** `playwright` — the case that used to fail at collection:

```console
$ /tmp/pwcheck/bin/python -m pytest pkg-py/tests -q
146 passed, 2 warnings in 0.35s
```

The tests are still collected and still browser-free in the e2e run — note no `[chromium]` parameterization, so they add no browser time:

```console
$ uv run pytest pkg-py/tests/playwright -o addopts= --collect-only -q
...
pkg-py/tests/playwright/test_wire_frames.py::test_histogram_wire_payload_uses_waiting_column[chromium]
pkg-py/tests/playwright/test_wire_tap.py::test_all_output_values_in_order_per_output
pkg-py/tests/playwright/test_wire_tap.py::test_all_input_values_matches_bare_and_typed_wire_ids
...
21 tests collected
```

Full env: `uv run pytest` → 156 passed (was 163; the 7 that moved now run under `make py-test-e2e`, which this PR's CI exercises).

title: fix: error clearly when page_react_dep()'s src_dir does not exist
description:
Follow-up to #288, which worked around this in two examples rather than fixing the message. Keeping the failure loud was the explicit call — this only makes it say something useful.

## Summary

Shiny serves a dependency's source directory as static files, so a `src_dir` that does not exist cannot work. Both packages said so badly, and differently:

- **Python** warned about a missing `ui.js`, then let Starlette raise `RuntimeError: Directory '...' does not exist` from inside `App.__init__` — naming neither shinyreact nor the argument that chose the path.
- **R** warned the same, then built the app happily and 404'd every asset at runtime. Its docs called a missing `src_dir` "not an error — the bundle may not be built yet".

`page_react_dep()` now checks the directory first, in both packages, and raises a message naming the resolved path, why the directory has to exist, and the two fixes. Python raises `NotADirectoryError`; R uses `cli::cli_abort()`. Two details worth noting: the check is `is_dir()` / `dir.exists()` rather than `exists()`, so a file passed as `src_dir` is rejected the same way; and it runs before the `js_file` check, so a missing directory never also warns about a file inside it.

A missing `js_file` still only warns. An existing directory with no bundle in it yet is a state a build is about to fix; a directory that is not there cannot be served at all.

R's `shinyreact-app` naming fallback (#242) stays — it is still reachable for a `src_dir` that exists but whose resolved parent has no basename, e.g. `/` — and its test now goes through `/` instead of a missing directory. The two `#242` tests that asserted the old tolerance (one per language) are rewritten to assert the error.

`FEATURES.md` is updated: the `page_react()` leaf that claimed "a missing `src_dir` does not error", and the `page_react_dep()` subtree, which now states the error and why it differs from the `js_file` warning.

## Verification

```python
>>> from shinyreact import page_react_dep
>>> page_react_dep(src_dir="/tmp/not-built")
NotADirectoryError: React asset directory not found: /tmp/not-built. Shiny
serves this directory's files, so it must exist by the time the page is built.
Build the bundle first (its output directory is created by the build), or pass
a different src_dir=.
```

```r
> shinyreact::page_react_dep("/tmp/not-built")
Error:
! React asset directory not found: '/tmp/not-built'
i Shiny serves this directory's files, so it must exist by the time the page is built.
i Build the bundle first (its output directory is created by the build), or pass a different `src_dir`.
```

Full suites pass in both languages: `pytest` 156 passed, `testthat::test_local()` all green.

title: fix(examples): build the bundle on first run in 04-shadcn and 09-hmr
description:
## Summary

`examples/04-shadcn` and `examples/09-hmr` gitignore their Vite output, so a fresh clone has no `www/` directory at all. `shiny run` on either one dies at startup with `RuntimeError: Directory '.../www' does not exist` — raised by Shiny's static mount, before `page_react_dep()`'s "JS entry point not found: … Build the bundle first?" warning gets a chance to say anything useful. (`03-columns-shadcn` escapes this only because its committed `index.html` keeps `www/` on disk.)

Both `app.py` files now check for `www/ui.js` before `set_react_page()` and run `npm install` + `npm run build` when it is absent. `09-hmr` builds `pkg-js` first when `pkg-js/dist-npm` is missing: its `file:../../pkg-js` dep resolves through `exports` into `dist-npm/`, which is not committed, so its own build fails with `Failed to resolve entry for package "@posit/shinyreact"` until that exists.

The check keys on the file existing, not on freshness — it never rebuilds a stale bundle, and never clobbers the dev stub `npm run dev` writes, which is the whole point of 09-hmr.

Also fixes 04-shadcn's Vite `build.lib.name`, which was `ColumnsShadcn`, copy-pasted from 03.

Both `FEATURES.md` trees and the three affected READMEs are updated in the same commit.

This deliberately does not change `page_react_dep()`. A missing asset directory *should* crash loudly — the follow-up is a friendlier error message, in a separate PR.

## Verification

From a state with no bundles at all:

```bash
rm -rf examples/04-shadcn/www examples/09-hmr/www pkg-js/dist-npm
uv run shiny run examples/04-shadcn/app.py
uv run shiny run examples/09-hmr/app.py
```

Each prints `www/ui.js not found -- building the client bundle...` to stderr, builds, and serves. Rendering the page confirms 04 emits `shinyreact.js` + `04-shadcn/ui.js` + `ui.css`, and 09 emits `09-hmr/ui.js` and **no** `shinyreact.js` (correct for `shinyreact_js="client"`), both with the `#shinyreact-config` tag.

title: docs(skill): add two side-by-side conversion checks
description:
Addresses #287, which proposed contributing two R scripts (`deps-diff.R`, `peek.R`) for comparing a Shiny app to its shinyreact conversion.

The scripts themselves are ~26 KB of R behind `chromote`/`callr`/`curl`/`xml2`/`httpuv`; a `tools/` folder for them means owning their maintenance and tests for a check that only runs during a conversion. The two *questions* they ask are the valuable part, and the convert skill already has both apps open in a browser by Phase 2 — so the recipe goes in the skill instead.

Adds a "Two cheap side-by-side checks" step to `shinyreact-convert-app` Phase 5: one JS snippet, evaluated on the original and on the port, reporting `connected`, bound input/output counts, `.shiny-output-error` ids, and the stylesheet/script list — plus the notes from #287 that make the readout usable (compare assets by library not path, `ui.js` / `ui.css` / `shinyreact-*` are expected on the port only, check the console for exceptions before trusting anything else, re-check per tab since dependencies arrive at first render).

Skill-only change; `make update-skills` run, `pkg-py/tests/test_skills.py` passes (8 passed). No behavior change, so no `FEATURES.md` diff.

Worth revisiting once #285 lands — most of what `deps-diff.R` flagged in #287 was the unwanted Bootstrap 3.

title: fix(r): wire_tap() pumps the event loop; un-export ShinyReactComponentElement; 01-hello wire test
description:
## Summary

An audit of the R, Python, and JS export surfaces found one export with no purpose in the repo today: `ShinyReactComponentElement`, the custom-element base class that hosts React islands inside server-rendered HTML. That is the inverse of the ui.tsx pattern and nothing subclasses it. Its export lines in `shiny-react/index.ts`, `global.ts`, and `npm.ts` are commented out with a note to re-enable them when partial React app support lands. The class and its unit test stay in the tree; the surface tests, `CLAUDE.md`, and `FEATURES.md` are updated to match.

Adding a `wire_tap()` test to `examples/01-hello` exposed a bug in `wire_tap()` itself: the `expect_*` poll loop slept with `Sys.sleep()`, which never runs the `later` event loop, so chromote never received websocket frames that arrived after the test's last `app$` call. Any debounced input send after a synthetic event was invisible and every expectation on it timed out. The loop now calls `later::run_now()`, `later` is declared in Imports, and a unit test schedules a frame via `later::later()` that fails against the old loop.

`examples/01-hello/tests/testthat/test-wire.R` drives `app.R` in a real browser and asserts the websocket contract: the default `bins` value of 30, the golden 30-bin histogram and caption, and the one-bin payload plus singular caption after moving the slider. The React-owned range input is driven through the native value setter plus an `input` event, since `useShinyInput` registers no Shiny binding for `set_inputs()` to find. It runs from the app via `shinytest2::test_app()` and from the package suite via the installed copy.

## Verification

```r
# from examples/01-hello
NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e 'shinytest2::test_app()'   # 26 pass
```

Locally: vitest 281 passed, R devtools::test 279 passed, pytest 159 passed.

title: ci: release packages by `<lang>/v` tag, and add a release skill
description:
Tag a release, get a published package — taking the shape from py-shiny, with a `<lang>/v` prefix so the three packages stay distinguishable.

| Package | Version source | Tag | Automation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shinyreact` (PyPI) | root `pyproject.toml` | `py/v1.2.3` | `release-py.yaml` |
| `@posit/shinyreact` (npm) | `pkg-js/package.json` | `js/v1.2.3` | `release-js.yaml` |
| `shinyreact` (R) | `pkg-r/DESCRIPTION` | `r/v1.2.3` | none — CRAN is manual |

### `release-py.yaml`

Python releases were unreachable as written: the workflow triggered only on `workflow_dispatch` but was gated by `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/py/v')`, which a manual dispatch can never satisfy. Now:

- triggers on `py/v*` tag pushes
- fails before building if the tag disagrees with `uv version --short`
- publishes via trusted publishing (unchanged), then `gh release create --generate-notes` with the sdist and wheel attached

### `release-js.yaml`

`js-v*` → `js/v*` for consistency; no tags exist yet, so nothing breaks. Adds the same tag-vs-version guard — `npm publish` ships whatever `package.json` says regardless of the tag, so a mismatch would quietly publish a version the tag lies about.

### `release-shinyreact` skill

Repo-internal (not in `SHIPPED_SKILLS`; `make update-skills` leaves the tree clean), with a minimal description so it loads on `/release-shinyreact` rather than on any mention of "release".

The load-bearing part it leads with: **Python and R vendor the built JS bundle**, so `make update-dist update-skills update-examples` must leave a clean tree *before* tagging. CI checks those committed copies on PRs, not at tag time — a stale-bundle release would ship silently.

For R it calls `usethis::use_release_issue()` and works the generated bullets, rather than hand-copying a CRAN checklist that would drift on the first-release-vs-patch difference it can't track. Only two repo-specific notes remain: run `make r-check` too (it fails on NOTEs), and the "tag the release" bullet means `r/v1.2.3`.

### Still needed before a real Python release

PyPI trusted publishing isn't configured yet (the TODO this replaces). Set it up at https://pypi.org/manage/project/shinyreact/settings/publishing/ with workflow `release-py.yaml` and environment `pypi`.

title: docs: tidy-style READMEs; move extras to vignettes and site articles
description:

The latter two use Python/R tabsets. R links in the navbar and Reference table now go to `r/reference/`, matching the Python and JS API links.
- **Makefile:** `uv run --group docs` for quartodoc, and `js-docs` depends on `js-setup`, so `make docs` works on a venv/node_modules synced before those tools were added.

title: docs(r): adopt the tidytemplate pkgdown template
description:
Points the R site at [tidytemplate](https://github.com/tidyverse/tidytemplate), following its README checklist and [shinytest2's config](https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/blob/3c31e83163c037f62abd81f7fa02a467f3e32880/DESCRIPTION#L68) for shape.

- `DESCRIPTION`: `Config/Needs/website: pkgdown, tidyverse/tidytemplate`. `website-r.yaml` already runs `setup-r-dependencies` with `needs: website`, so CI picks it up with no workflow change.
- `_pkgdown.yml`: `template.package: tidytemplate`, `trailing_slash_redirect: true`, and `bslib` colors derived from the hex logo's React cyan — `primary: "#006D80"` (darkened for text contrast), `navbar-background: "#ebfcff"` (lightened 92%, same recipe shinytest2 documents).

Skipped from the checklist: plausible analytics (needs a domain registered with Hadley; shinytest2 doesn't have it either) and `development: mode: auto`, which would move the site to `r/dev/` and break the deploy path in `website-r.yaml`.

### Logo placement

pkgdown 2.2 strips the logo out of the README and re-inserts it as the first child of a `display: flex` `.page-header`, which defeats both the README's `align="right"` and pkgdown's own `float: right` rule — shinytest2's live site has the same left-aligned result. `pkgdown/extra.css` puts it back on the right with `order: 1; margin-left: auto`.

### Also

- Drops `" (R)"` from the R README title, and adds the shinytest2-style linked logo to line 1.
- Both package READMEs' opening paragraph now links out: React → react.dev, `shinyreact` → the site landing page, JavaScript bundle → the JS API docs, and the sibling language → its API docs (the R README pointed at a GitHub tree; the Python README's "R package" wasn't a link at all).
- Adds a Conductor run script that builds and serves the whole site. `npx --yes http-server` so it can't block on an install prompt in a non-interactive shell, and a `PORT ?= 8080` variable so concurrent workspaces don't collide.

### Verification

`make r-docs-render` builds clean; measured in a browser, the logo now spans x 614–734 inside a main of 38–758 (flush right) and the `<h1>` reads `shinyreact`. `make docs-preview PORT=8792` serves 200 with no npm prompt.

description:

title: docs(r): drop stale JSON-driven wording from DESCRIPTION Title
description:
The `app.py` pattern (server-side JSON-spec rendering) was removed in #168, so the R package Title no longer described what the package does.

Also re-triggers the R workflows (`check-r` routine, `website-r`) on `pkg-r/**`, letting the routine job commit any regenerated `man/` output.

title: ci: pr-done gate that passes iff every triggered check passed
description:
Adds a single `pr-done` check, in the spirit of py-shiny's `pr-gate`, adapted to this repo's layout.

py-shiny's gate is a `needs:`-list job inside one workflow. Ours can't be: the checks here are separate path-filtered workflows (`check-r` only runs when `pkg-r/**` changes, etc.), and GitHub treats a required check that never triggered as *pending*, not passed — so a required `check-r` would block every Python-only PR.

`pr-done` runs on every PR, polls the check runs on the head commit ([poseidon/wait-for-status-checks](https://github.com/poseidon/wait-for-status-checks)), and passes iff every check that *did* run passed. A workflow the path filter skipped creates no check run and doesn't count — an R-only or docs-only PR still gets a green gate.

This PR is itself the test case: only `pr-done` and `conventional-commits` trigger on it.

Follow-up (repo settings, not code): add `pr-done` as the only required status check in the `lock-down-main` ruleset. Without a required check, `gh pr merge --auto` merges immediately — which is what happened to #273.

title: feat: documentation website — Quarto landing + quartodoc, pkgdown, TypeDoc (#86)
description:
Closes #86.

## What

One GitHub Pages site at https://posit-dev.github.io/shinyreact/, deployed to `gh-pages` from two workflows (`clean: false`, same approach as shinychat):

| URL | Tool | Source |
|---|---|---|
