title: build: track py-shiny main; use the public ui.page_html()
description:
## What

py-shiny#2475 merged on 2026-09-01, so the `schloerke/issue-2462` branch pin is stale. It also renamed the API on the way in — `ui.PageDocument` became `ui.page_html()`, and the document class is no longer exported.

- **`pyproject.toml`** — the git dep (runtime and `tests-e2e`) now tracks py-shiny `main`. Still a git dep: `ui.page_html()` has not shipped in a release yet (#216).
- **`page_react_html()`** builds with the public `ui.page_html()` and tags the returned document with the directory it was read from:

  ```python
  setattr(doc, SRC_DIR_ATTR, index_path.parent)   # "_shinyreact_src_dir"
  ```

  `ReactApp` reads it with `getattr(ui, SRC_DIR_ATTR, None)` instead of an `isinstance` check.

## Why the tag rather than a subclass

`ReactHtmlDocument` existed only to carry `src_dir` so `ReactApp` could mount the document's directory at `/`. py-shiny exports `page_html()` but not its `PageHtmlDocument` class, so keeping the subclass would mean importing from `shiny.ui._page`. Tagging the attribute drops the class, drops the `_page` → `_app` class import, and leaves `pkg-py/src/` on public py-shiny API only.

Behavior is unchanged: same mount, same `bookmark_store=` `TypeError` for `ui=page_react_html(...)`. The return type is now `htmltools.HTMLTextDocument` — public, and a true supertype of what `page_html()` returns.

## Remaining private import

The three test modules import `DEPS_PLACEHOLDER` from `shiny.ui._page`. On py-shiny `main` it is a module-level constant (it *was* a `PageDocument` class attribute pre-merge), and neither it nor the class is publicly exported. Commented as such at each import.

## Also

- Docs follow the rename: `CLAUDE.md`, `FEATURES.md`, `examples/03-columns-shadcn/README.md`, and two R comments that referenced py-shiny's spelling.
- `pkg-py/README.md` gains one blank line from `make py-format` (ruff formats Python blocks inside Markdown) — unrelated, but the format check wants it.

## Verification

- `make py-check` → 159 passed, pyright 0 errors, format clean
- `make py-test-e2e` → 14 passed

title: feat(r): ship 07-plotly in inst/examples-shiny with a drift guard, and document runGitHub() (#265)
description:
Closes #265.

#265 proposed relocating `examples/` into the packages. We're not doing that — see [the decision comment](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinyreact/issues/265#issuecomment-5612452638). Instead this PR does the two things the issue was actually reaching for.

## 1. Fix the drift, don't relocate

`pkg-r/inst/examples-shiny/01-hello/` was a hand-made copy of `examples/01-hello` added on the #201 branch, so `wire_tap()`'s real-browser test could reach an app from the *installed* package. Nothing kept it in sync.

- `make update-examples` copies `app.R` + `www/` for each name in the Makefile's `R_EXAMPLES` list into `pkg-r/inst/examples-shiny/<name>/`.
- `pkg-r/tests/testthat/test-examples.R` tree-compares the shipped copy against `examples/<name>` and fails with `run \`make update-examples\``.

Same generated-copy + parity-test flow as `make update-skills` / `make update-dist`. I verified the guard fails on a deliberate one-line drift and passes after regenerating.

`07-plotly` ships too now, so #194's R e2e suite has a second package-reachable fixture app.

Relocating would have made one thing strictly worse: `examples/` has to stay canonical for any drift guard to have something to compare against, so `www/ui.js` would live in **three** places (canonical + `pkg-r` + `pkg-py`) instead of one. "Relocate" would really have been "duplicate". `inst/examples-shiny/` stays, but narrowly as the installed-package test fixture — the only thing that actually required it, since R CMD check runs against the installed package and genuinely cannot see `examples/`.

Python needs no equivalent: pytest `testpaths` reaches `examples/` in-repo, and its one out-of-tree reach-through (`pkg-py/tests/playwright/test_wire_frames.py`) is repo-only by construction (`make py-test-e2e`).

## 2. Give users a run command instead

```r
shiny::runGitHub("posit-dev/shinyreact", subdir = "examples/01-hello")
```

Added to `examples/README.md` (new "Running an example" section), `examples/01-hello/README.md`, and `pkg-r/README.md`.

Traps documented, each verified rather than assumed:

- It's `runGitHub` — **capital H**; `shiny::runGithub` does not exist (`exists("runGithub", asNamespace("shiny"))` is `FALSE`).
- `repo` accepts the `"username/repo"` form and `ref` defaults to `"HEAD"` (read from `body(shiny::runGitHub)`). The URL it builds resolves: `https://github.com/posit-dev/shinyreact/archive/HEAD.tar.gz` → 200.
- `01-hello` and `07-plotly` are the only examples with an `app.R`, so they're the two this launches.
- Python has no `runGitHub` equivalent → clone + `shiny run`.
- `03-columns-shadcn`, `04-shadcn`, `09-hmr` gitignore `www/ui.js`, so they need `npm install && npm run build` before `shiny run`.

## Not done

Porting the eight Python-only examples to R. Seven are mechanical; `08-input-handler` and `10-bookmarking` would carry real signal (they cover `shiny.datetime` through `shinyreact.default`, and all of `bookmark.R` — neither has an R example today). `06-data-frame` is hard-blocked: its client hardcodes `ShinyOutput tagName: "shiny-data-frame"`, a py-shiny-only web component with no R counterpart, so the shared `www/` client can't be reused. Worth revisiting after #179 prunes the set; filed nothing yet.

No `07-plotly/README.md` added — it never had one, and `examples/README.md` names its command explicitly.

## Testing

R suite: `[ FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 0 | PASS 271 ]`.

**I could not run the Python suite.** `uv sync` fails resolving the py-shiny git dep — `fatal: couldn't find remote ref refs/tags/schloerke/issue-2462`, the branch pinned in `pyproject.toml`. Pre-existing and unrelated (this PR touches no Python), but it means CI is the first Python signal here, and that pin probably needs its own fix now that py-shiny#2475 has moved.

`FEATURES.md` unchanged: this is repo plumbing plus docs, and the testing helpers (`wire_tap()`) aren't in the tree either.

title: feat: shinyreact_js= switch for npm-tier pages; convert examples/09-hmr (#217)
description:
Closes #217.

Every page entry point injected the IIFE bundle unconditionally, so an app that
bundles `@posit/shinyreact` got **two** runtimes on the page.

## The switch

`shinyreact_js = "server" | "client"`, default `"server"` — who supplies
`shinyreact.js` (and `shinyreact.css`) to the page.

```python
page_react(..., shinyreact_js="server")            # default
page_react_html(path, ..., shinyreact_js="server")
set_react_page(path=None, *, shinyreact_js="server")
ReactApp(server, ..., shinyreact_js="server")
```
```r
page_react(..., shinyreact_js = "server")
page_react_html(path, extra_deps = NULL, shinyreact_js = "server")
```

`"client"` omits **only** those two files. The `#shinyreact-config` tag is
emitted either way, because the npm-tier client hard-errors without it.

Validation lives in one place per language (`_serves_bundle()` /
`serves_bundle()`), so every entry point rejects a typo identically.
`set_react_page()` and `ReactApp()` validate **eagerly** at call time rather
than at first page render, so a typo fails at app startup next to the line that
caused it:

```
ValueError: shinyreact_js='sever' is not valid. Expected one of 'server',
'client'. Use "server" when the shinyreact package should serve shinyreact.js
(the default, and what a no-build app needs), and "client" when your own bundle
imports @posit/shinyreact and therefore ships its own copy.
```

### Why an enum, and why this name

`include_runtime=False` was the first shape. It lost on two counts: if the
bundler tier becomes the norm, a boolean is a permanent double negative at the
call site, and "runtime" is already overloaded in this repo — `pkg-js/vite.config.npm.ts`
externalizes `react/jsx-runtime`. An enum lets the *default* flip later with no
rename and no call-site churn, and leaves room for the decision record's
Option D (server-served ESM).

`shinyreact_js` names the artifact, so it does not promise the narrower thing
`examples/04-shadcn/vite.config.js` already controls with `rollupOptions.external`
(where React comes from). Names considered and dropped: `react_runtime`
(collides with React Server Components / `react-dom/server`), `runtime_source`
("runtime"), `shinyreact_source` (sits next to `src_dir` in the same signature),
`shinyreact_dep` / `include_dep` (a dep is a server-side htmltools object, so
`="client"` is a category error — and `page_react()` attaches four kinds of
dependency, `page_react_html()` already has `extra_deps=`, and R already has an
internal `shinyreact_dep()`).

### What the server deliberately does not do

It never validates the *choice*, because it cannot: whether the client bundles a
copy is a property of the built `ui.js`, known only once it executes — after the
page's script tags are committed. A `package.json`-sniffing heuristic was
considered and rejected: it is wrong on 2 of the 3 examples that have one
(`03-columns-shadcn` and `04-shadcn` have a build step *and* use the global), and
`package.json` is not part of a deployed app, so the same app would render one
way locally and another in production.

## Double-load warning

Instead, the case that fails silently announces itself. From the npm entry:

```
[shinyreact] shinyreact.js is loaded twice on this page: the server served it,
and this app also imports @posit/shinyreact. The app works, but it is
downloading a second copy of React and the hooks for nothing. Pass
shinyreact_js="client" to your page entry point — page_react(),
page_react_html(), set_react_page(), or ReactApp().
```

`console.warn`, not a throw: nothing is broken (the registries are page-scoped,
so both copies share one set of inputs, outputs, and handlers) and killing a
working app over wasted bytes is the wrong trade. It lives in the npm entry
because only that build can observe the collision — deferred classic and module
scripts execute in document order and the page emits the bundle dep first, so
`installGlobal()` runs first and sees nothing.

The reverse mistake (`"client"` with a client that bundles nothing) needs no
help: it throws on the app's first hook call.

## examples/09-hmr → the npm tier

- imports `@posit/shinyreact`; `src/shiny-bridge.{dev,prod}.ts`, the
  `resolve.alias` switch, and the React-externalizing `rollupOptions` are gone
- React is bundled in **both** modes — a development React in dev, which is what
  Fast Refresh requires and what the production-only React inside the IIFE could
  never provide
- `app.py` uses `set_react_page(shinyreact_js="client")`
- until the first npm publish the dep is `file:../../pkg-js` — repo-relative, so
  the lockfile stays portable (`"resolved": "../../pkg-js", "link": true`); build
  `pkg-js` before installing

Acceptance test from #217, on the real example page:

```
shinyreact.js served: False
shinyreact.css served: False
config tag:           True
```

and the built `www/ui.js` contains no `window.shinyreact` reference.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| pytest | 151 passed |
| testthat | 246 passed |
| vitest | 258 passed |
| pyright / tsc | 0 errors |
| R CMD check | 1 pre-existing NOTE (CRAN incoming feasibility) |
| ruff / air / prettier | clean |

New tests: omit-the-bundle for `page_react`, `page_react_html`, both
`set_react_page()` modes, and both `ReactApp` discovered modes; typo rejection
in both languages, cross-referenced by name; two `entry-parity.test.ts` cases
for the warning. That file's `beforeEach` also now deletes `window.shinyreact` —
`installGlobal()` was leaking it across tests, so what a test saw depended on
what ran before it.

Docs: `FEATURES.md` (shared `shinyreact_js` block, four updated signatures, the
third deliberate tier difference), both `examples/09-hmr` docs,
`examples/README.md`, the decision record, and the `#217` justification comments
in `message-registry.ts` / `react-registry.ts` / CLAUDE.md, which all cited the
old flag when explaining why two copies can coexist.

`pkg-py/tests/playwright/test_module_dependency.py` is an unrelated `ruff format`
fixup that `make py-format` produced.

## ⚠️ Overlaps #263

#263 (`examples/11-npm-local`, evidence for #261) touches the same files and
**conflicts semantically in `pkg-js/src/npm.ts`**: it removes
`requireShinyReactConfigTag()`, while this PR keeps it and inserts the
double-load warning immediately above it. The two ideas are compatible — #263's
`page_bare(page_react_dep(...))` page needs no switch, and this PR is what makes
`page_react()` / `set_react_page()` / `ReactApp()` / `page_react_html()` usable at
the npm tier — but they need sequencing, and whichever lands second will have to
resolve `npm.ts`, `entry-parity.test.ts`, `FEATURES.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
`decisions/2026-08-17-js-distribution.md`, and `examples/README.md`.

title: feat(testing): export WireTap / wire_tap() wire-payload test helpers
description:
Research from #201 (see also the design notes added in `docs/`); complements #252's FEATURES.md + jsdom layers with the real-wire tier its layer table reserves for Playwright. Related: #194, #265.

## Summary

- `shinyreact.playwright.WireTap` (Python) and `shinyreact::wire_tap()` (R): assert the JSON payloads that actually crossed the Shiny websocket — the client/server contract — from app-author tests. Test-only dependencies are guarded at runtime: importing `shinyreact.playwright` requires playwright (the package itself doesn't), and `wire_tap()` checks that shinytest2 is installed and that `app$get_logs()` returns a data frame with `location`/`level`/`message` columns (i.e. the AppDriver was created with `options = list(shiny.trace = TRUE)`).
- Per-channel API only — cross-channel frame order (which output lands first, how outputs batch into `values` frames) is reactive-scheduling coincidence, so it is deliberately not exposed. The retrying `expect_output_value` / `expect_message` / `expect_input_value` methods (value matcher = equality, fn matcher = truthy, playwright-style) consume a per-channel cursor over lossless recorded history, giving ordered-subsequence semantics: values arriving between checks cannot be missed, and a matcher that errors on a value's shape is a non-match reported at timeout. `all_output_values` / `all_messages` / `all_input_values` return each channel's full history. The message channel follows `protocol/surface.json` (`{id, data}`).
- Mirrored unit suites (fake page in `pkg-py/tests/test_wire_tap.py`, fake `get_logs()` app in `pkg-r/tests/testthat/test-wire-tap.R`), a Playwright e2e test on `examples/01-hello` proving the histogram binned the `waiting` column, and an R e2e test against a copy of the same app shipped in `pkg-r/inst/examples-shiny/01-hello/` so it works from the installed package (#265 tracks relocating examples there properly). README sections in both packages; design notes in `docs/2026-08-27-verifying-shinyreact-apps.md`; a runnable shinytest2 walkthrough in `spikes/201-wire-verification/`.

## Verification

```r
app <- shinytest2::AppDriver$new(
  system.file("examples-shiny", "01-hello", package = "shinyreact"),
  options = list(shiny.trace = TRUE)
)
tap <- shinyreact::wire_tap(app)
tap$expect_input_value("bins", 30L)
tap$expect_output_value("dist_data", function(d) d$breaks[[1]] == 43)
```

`NOT_CRAN=true` R CMD check: 0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 notes (the e2e test runs inside check); `make py-check` clean; the new Playwright test passes under `make py-test-e2e`.

title: feat: expose an erroring output's message with useShinyOutputError
description:
Closes #257.

## The gap

When a `reactive_output` errored, the client could only learn *that* it errored — `useShinyOutputStatus(id)` returned `"error"` and the message stopped at the output registry. Both stock-app ports in the skills benchmark had to record "error text not reproduced verbatim" as a *forced* divergence.

## The fix

The registry already cached the error and fanned it out to subscribers; nothing exposed it. So this is a new read-only hook over an existing channel:

| | Read-only |
|---|---|
| **Output error** | `useShinyOutputError(id, options?)` → `{message, call, type} \| null` |

- Subscribes to the error channel only (no re-render on value/status), resets on id or namespace change, and syncs a late-mounting subscriber from the cache.
- `null` whenever the output is not in the `"error"` state.
- `[r]` `call` / `type` carry the condition's call and extra classes; `[py]` both are `null`.

**No server-side change in either package.** `reactive_output` is an ordinary Shiny renderer, so the message arrives already sanitized by shiny itself (`shiny.sanitize.errors` / `sanitize_errors`) — the client never has to decide what is safe to show.

## Silent errors, and an R/Python parity fix

R sends `req()` as an error with an **empty message** (vanilla Shiny blanks the output element); py-shiny sends a `null` value for the same `req()`. `setError` with an empty message is now handled as `setValue(null)`, so one React component sees the same thing from either server, and a silent error surfaces no message.

## Tests

- `pkg-js/src/shiny-react/__tests__/use-shiny-output-error.test.tsx` — 5 cases (first delivery, late-mount sync, clearing on a value, silent error, id change).
- `output-registry.test.ts` pins the empty-message → `null` value mapping; `global.test.ts` pins the widened `window.shinyreact` surface.
- `pkg-py/tests/playwright/apps/output-error/` + `test_output_error.py` — e2e: the server's `ValueError` text reaches the client and clears on recovery, and `req()` blanks the value with no error. R has no e2e suite yet (#194).

Green locally: JS 262, Python 146 + pyright clean, R 237, Playwright 12.

## Docs

`FEATURES.md` leaves (hook behavior, the `[r]`-only silent-error shape, `(e2e)` markers), `CLAUDE.md` hook table, both READMEs, and the shipped `shinyreact-build-app` skill (hook table, an error-UI snippet, debugging + modules references), with `make update-skills` and `make update-dist` run.

title: feat: expose an erroring output's message with useShinyOutputError
description:
Adds the `useShinyOutputError(id)` hook: subscribes to an output's error channel and returns the server's (already sanitized) `{message, call, type}`, or `null` when the output is not in the `"error"` state. Silent errors (`req()`, `validate()` with no message) are mapped to a `null` value so R and Python servers look identical to the same React component. Includes unit tests, a Playwright e2e app/test, and docs/skills/FEATURES updates.

Also widens `ErrorsMessageValue` to `call: string[] | null; type?: string[] | null` — py-shiny sends `null` for both.

title: fix: show protocol handshake failures on the page (#213)
description:
Closes #213.

The protocol handshake throws during the first hook mount, so a mismatch left the page blank with the explanation only in the DevTools console.

## What changed

Every fatal handshake path now goes through `throwVisibly()` in `pkg-js/src/shiny-react/config.ts`, which paints a fixed banner and then throws the same message:

- major-version mismatch, either direction (`assertProtocolCompatible`)
- npm build: missing `#shinyreact-config` tag
- npm build: tag with no `protocolVersion`

Fail fast is unchanged — the banner is additive.

Details:

- `<div id="shinyreact-fatal-error" role="alert">` appended to `<body>`, one element reused across repeated failures.
- Plain DOM, no dependency on Shiny being initialized: the failure being reported is precisely that client and server cannot talk to each other.
- Literals (both versions, `#shinyreact-config`, `@posit/shinyreact`) are backticked in the message and render as `<code>` chips. Backticks are stripped from the thrown error and from the console-only warning.
- Written with `textContent`, never `innerHTML`, so a server-supplied version string cannot inject markup.
- #7f1d1d on #fee2e2 (~9.5:1) with a #991b1b bottom rule; chips ~11:1 on white. Never color alone — the full sentence and `role="alert"` carry the meaning.

## What it looks like

```
shinyreact protocol mismatch: the server speaks protocol `999.0` but this JS
client supports `1.0`. Upgrade the older side (the shinyreact R/Python package,
or the client bundle) so the major protocol versions match.
```

(versions rendered as `<code>` chips, dark maroon on a pale red banner across the top)

## Tests

- `pkg-js/src/shiny-react/__tests__/config.test.ts`: both mismatch directions, chip markup, HTML-injection safety, single-element reuse, throw/display parity, backtick stripping. `npx vitest run` → 263 pass.
- `pkg-py/tests/playwright/test_protocol_mismatch.py` + fixture `apps/protocol_mismatch/` (server monkeypatched to claim protocol `999.0`): banner visible with both versions, chips, `role="alert"`, and the app body never rendered. `make py-test-e2e` → 11 pass.
- `make py-check-tests` → 146 pass. `make js-lint` clean. `make update-dist` run.

`FEATURES.md` updated with the new `[js]` subtree.

## Not done

No `Shiny.notifications.show()` / dev-mode error console surface. Shiny's error console is fed by server errors, not client throws, and notifications need Shiny initialized — exactly what is unreliable at the moment the handshake fails. Worth revisiting once the npm tier lands.

title: docs: fix the leaves the third FEATURES.md audit contradicted (#245)
description:
Closes #245.

The third `FEATURES.md` audit, run once the #237–#241 stack and the follow-ups (#246–#249) had merged. Walked all 557 leaves and both reverse passes.

**Result: CONFIRMED 535 · CONTRADICTED 12 · NOT FOUND 0 · UNVERIFIABLE 10.** Every contradiction was in a section rewritten by that stack, exactly as #245 predicted — reading order would have spent the effort on already-correct leaves.

## What the audit found

The worst finding is the one #245 warned would recur: **a leaf had re-absorbed a claim the repo already deleted as false.** `test_shiny_output.py` asserts `not_to_have_class(shiny-bound-output)` and its comment records that a previous comment claiming otherwise was "false for this fixture. Asserting it is how that was discovered." The leaf sat as a child of that very `(e2e)` test. It is now split into the two conditioned claims the suite actually pins.

Two more were verified by execution rather than by reading: `MockShinySession` **has** `onFlushed` and `getOutput`, so discovery installs on it and is inert only because the mock's private `.outputs` is `NULL` — the tree and the R source comment both gave the wrong reason. And the decision record contains **zero** mentions of `reactive_output`, so that leaf's citation pointed at a section that does not exist (`CLAUDE.md` repeated it).

Full per-leaf verdicts, coverage fractions for the eight sweeps, and ~45 unclaimed behaviors are in the audit report on #245.

## Beyond the tree

Three fixes went into code, because the tree was describing something that ought to have been true and wasn't:

- **Two surface guards could pass without checking anything.** The custom-message scans in Python and R had no non-vacuity assertion, so a broken regex yielded an empty set, an empty difference, and a green test. This is the substance behind correcting the "each guard is verified to fail on an unlisted name" leaf: rather than claim failure-injection that does not exist, the leaf now states what is asserted and the guards no longer have a silent-pass mode.
- **`entry-parity.test.ts` claimed to pin two tier differences and pinned one.** Nothing checked that `npm.ts` opts into config-tag strictness, so that call could have been deleted with a green suite.
- **`ReactOutputBinding` bypassed the page-scoped accessor** in all three of its methods, with three non-null assertions. It now takes the accessor injected (importing it would cycle with `react-registry.ts`) and resolves it per call.

## Not in scope

Three page-singletons remain module-scoped (`installed`, `shinyReactInitialized`, and the unguarded `createReactOutputBinding()`). I verified against Shiny's client source that all three are **latent, not active** — `addCustomMessageHandler` silently replaces, `bindOutputs()` skips already-bound elements, and the server latches the duplicate ping. Page-scoping them would add two more sanctioned `window` writes to fix nothing observable, in code that #217 deletes. Recorded on #217 with the evidence; the tree now states the per-copy scoping explicitly so it is visible rather than contradicted.

## Verification

```
JS   227 passed (5 new)
py   115 passed
R    199 passed
make js-lint, make py-check   clean
```

Both new guards were confirmed to fail when deliberately broken (regex mutated; `requireShinyReactConfigTag()` commented out), and the new per-call binding test fails if the registry is captured at construction. `make update-dist` rebuilt the bundle — all three committed copies are byte-identical.

title: feat: ship the Agent Skills inside the installed packages
description: The skills only reached people working in this repo. Ship them so an app author who `pip install shinyreact` / `install.packages("shinyreact")` gets them too, via the two conventions their ecosystems already have: - Python: `shinyreact/.agents/skills//SKILL.md`, where library-skills scans site-packages (`uvx library-skills --claude`). Hatchling includes it with no packaging config. - R: `inst/skills//`, where btw looks (`btw::btw_skill_install_package("shinyreact")`). `.claude/skills/` stays canonical; `make update-skills` copies into both packages, the same committed-copy flow as `make update-dist`, and each package's suite fails on drift. `audit-shinyreact-features` is repo-internal and not shipped. Two things the copies needed: the skills' repo-relative pointers become GitHub URLs, since an installed user has no checkout; and the generated Python copy is excluded from ruff, which formats Python code blocks inside Markdown and would otherwise rewrite it away from its source. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

The description is PORT.md — a FEATURES.md-style behavior tree plus one checklist per feature area, kept current during implementation so other agents and the user can see where the port stands. examples/*/FEATURES.md are the worked examples it points at. title: feat: adopt py-shiny's dependency placeholder in `page_react_html()`
description:
Closes #216. Closes #243.

`page_react_html()` required a `{{ headContent() }}` marker of our own invention. The document now carries py-shiny's own marker instead:

```html
<meta name="shiny-dependency-placeholder" content="">
```

the literal `shiny.ui.PageDocument.DEPS_PLACEHOLDER`. It is an ordinary `<meta>` tag rather than template syntax, so an app's `index.html` stays valid HTML that any tool — a bundler's dev server included — can serve unchanged. One literal, both languages, so one document works on either server.

### #243 dissolves rather than getting fixed

#243 offered three options for a check whose error message claimed `<head>` while the match was document-wide. None of them apply once we stop owning the marker: Python deletes `_HEAD_CONTENT_MARKER`, the substring check, and the `ValueError` outright. `ui.PageDocument` raises when a document has no placeholder — the placeholder is py-shiny's contract, so py-shiny enforces it, and its message names `deps_replace_pattern=` and the default. `ReactHtmlDocument` no longer passes `deps_replace_pattern=` at all.

The one visible consequence: Python's error moves from `page_react_html()` call time to page render (which, under `ReactApp`, is the same request either way). `test_page_react_html_missing_placeholder_errors_at_render` pins it, and says why it isn't R's shape.

R keeps a check. htmltools silently drops attached dependencies when a document contains no `headContent()` — the page comes back with no Shiny on it and nothing upstream complains — so the check has to live somewhere, and it may as well live where it can name the file. It greps for the meta tag and quotes it in the error, so check and message finally agree.

R's rewrite to `{{ headContent() }}` happens **in memory**, on the text already read with `brio`, then goes to `htmlTemplate(text_ = ...)`. So the author's file has no template syntax in it, matching Python, and R stops reading the same file twice per call. R's whole-document `{{ }}` evaluation is unchanged and still the documented divergence (#223).

### #216: `ReactApp` earns its keep

The third checkbox on #216 asked whether it still does, once `ui.PageDocument` exists. It does, and this PR is the evidence: `PageDocument` serves a document you hand it, but *discovering* the document next to the app file and mounting `static_assets={"/": src_dir}` so its sibling `ui.js` resolves are both ours, and the new example needs both.

The git dep on the `schloerke/issue-2462` branch stays until py-shiny#2475 ships in a release — the two `TODO`s in `pyproject.toml` now point at py-shiny#2475 directly rather than at this issue.

### The example

**Nothing exercised `page_react_html()` before this** — no example had an `index.html` at all. `03-columns-shadcn` becomes the one that owns its document: a checked-in `www/index.html` with its own `<html lang>`, viewport, title, and a `Loading…` placeholder that shows before the bundle mounts, served by `ReactApp(server)` on the Core API (`app.py` moves from Express, same server logic).

Two things the README now spells out because they bit during the conversion:

- `<script src="ui.js" defer>` needs the `defer`. The shinyreact bundle lands in `<head>` deferred, and deferred scripts run in document order; a bare script in `<body>` runs *first* and finds no `window.shinyreact`.
- The build stays Vite lib-mode IIFE. A standard ES-module build can't map a bare `react` import to a global, and the client must share the React instance that owns the hooks. Owning the document is orthogonal to that, and the README says so rather than implying `vite dev` now works here.

The honest cost is stated too: a hand-written `<script src="ui.js">` is cached by URL, where `page_react()` versions the bundle by mtime. Own the document when you need control over the HTML; otherwise don't.

### Breaking

A `{{ headContent() }}` document now errors, in both languages, with no transitional accept-both — deliberate, and confirmed as the call. Pre-release, not on CRAN. R has a test pinning the rejection so the break is a stated behavior rather than an accident.

### Adjacent, deliberately not in this PR

- **#148** ("`www/index.html` is a template and that's misleading") is most of the way closed by this: the document is plain HTML now. What's left is a different wart — `set_react_page("www/index.html")` (Express) treats the file as a **body fragment** while `page_react_html()` (Core) treats it as a **full document**. Same filename, two meanings; Express can't reach `PageDocument` because of #82.
- **#158 / #217** are unblocked, not fixed: a dev server can serve a document containing an inert `<meta>` tag, and never could serve one containing `{{ headContent() }}`.

### Checks

`make py-check` — 115 passed. `make r-check` — 199 passed, 0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 notes. `FEATURES.md` and `CLAUDE.md` updated in the same PR, per the tree's own rule. The example was built (`npm run build`) and served through a `TestClient`: one `<html>`, deps inserted at the placeholder, `/ui.js` and `/ui.css` both 200.

title: feat(py): automatic renderer dep discovery for Core mode / late registrations (#220)
description:
Closes #220.

Ports R's post-flush renderer dependency discovery (#203/#221) to Python, so
Core-mode pages (`page_react()`, `page_react_html()`, `ReactApp`) get the
zero-config dependency delivery that only Express's `set_react_page()` had —
and Express apps get it for outputs registered *after* page load.

## How

`pkg-py/src/shinyreact/_dep_discovery.py` mirrors `pkg-r/R/dep-discovery.R`:
the `shinyreact.init` ping (already sent once per session by the JS bundle,
previously a Python no-op) installs an `on_flushed(..., once=False)` hook that

1. diffs `session.output._outputs` for outputs it has not seen,
2. reads each new renderer's `auto_output_ui().tagify().get_dependencies()`,
3. drops deps already sent to this session (keyed `name@version`),
4. registers the rest via `session._process_ui()` and ships them as a
   `shinyreact-deps` custom message — the message type the JS client already
   handles (loads the deps, re-runs `bindAll`).

It no-ops rather than raising on sessions without the pieces it needs
(`None`, no `output._outputs`, no `on_flushed`), and installs at most once per
session — py-shiny has no `session$userData`, so the latch is an attribute.

This does **not** address #160: shinywidgets' `comm_open` arrives on its own
channel and races the dep load. R's htmlwidgets have no such side channel,
which is why the push is sufficient there.

## Tests

- `pkg-py/tests/test_dep_discovery.py` — 7 unit tests mirroring R's
  `test-dep-discovery.R` (push once per new output, late registrations, no
  resends, dep-less outputs, idempotence, no-op sessions, handler wiring).
- `pkg-py/tests/playwright/apps/late_data_frame/` + `test_late_dep_without_a_holder`
  — e2e proof the push is **required**: a `render.data_frame` registered on a
  button click, mounted through a bare `<ShinyOutput>` with no `@render.ui`
  holder, so neither the page-generation harvest nor Shiny's own dynamic-UI
  path can deliver the binding. Stubbing `install_dep_discovery()` out makes
  exactly this test fail.
- `test_dynamic_ui_plotly_dep` → `test_late_dep_with_a_server_side_holder`: its
  "dep absent at page load" DOM assertion is now (correctly) falsified by the
  push, so it asserts absence in the *served HTML* instead — which is what it
  was there to pin. Both dep-delivery tests are renamed after the variable they
  isolate, with a module docstring stating the three delivery paths.

`FEATURES.md` updated: renderer dependency discovery is now shared behavior
with `[py]`/`[r]` detail leaves instead of an R-only subtree with a "#220
pending" note.

title: fix(r): name the app "shinyreact-app" when src_dir is missing (#242)
description:
Closes #242, option 2 from the issue.

`page_react()` resolves `src_dir` with `normalizePath(mustWork = FALSE)`, so a missing relative path stays relative and `basename(dirname("www"))` came out as `"."` — a page titled `.` and an asset dependency served at `/lib/.-0/`.

Keep the permissive resolution — the bundle may legitimately not be built yet, and the `js_file` warning is still the signal — but fall back to `shinyreact-app` when the derived name is empty, `.`, or `..`. Both the `<title>` and the dependency name pick it up.

Python needs no fallback: it resolves against the calling module, so the path is absolute whether or not it exists.

- R test pins the fallback (title + dep name); Python test pins that a missing `src_dir` still titles after the app folder, so the non-parity is asserted rather than silent.
- `FEATURES.md`'s leaf rewritten: shared "a missing `src_dir` does not error" parent, `[r]` fallback and `[py]` no-fallback children.

Not taken: erroring on a missing `src_dir` (option 3) — it breaks the build-on-first-request case.

title: docs: settle the protocol bump rule for additive shapes (#232)
description:
Closes #232.

#240 landed the surface manifest and its guards but deliberately left #232's policy call open. This settles it, without a version bump.

**The rule: additive, ignorable shapes do not bump.** A new message type, handler name, or optional payload member leaves the version alone. The client compares majors only, no peer reads the minor, and a same-major peer must tolerate unknown members and types regardless — so a minor bump would be a number nothing observes. `protocol/surface.json` is the enforced record of what is on the wire; the version records only what an existing peer would *misinterpret*. #221's `shinyreact.init` / `.shinyreact_init` / `shinyreact-deps` additions therefore stand correctly at `1.0`.

**The stale comments.** All three protocol constants enumerated "exactly three boundary shapes" — which is precisely how the scope went stale one PR after it was written. They now point at `surface.json`, which a test in each language keeps honest, and state the bump rule instead of the inventory.

`FEATURES.md`'s leaves describing the disagreement now describe the resolution.

Comment- and prose-only; `PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays `1.0` in all three languages. `pkg-py/tests/test_protocol_surface.py`: 4 passed.

title: test(r): pin output_ui()'s no-outputFunc branch (#234)
description:
Closes #234.

The issue's substance — the false hint claiming `reactive_output()` render functions carry no `outputFunc` — was already fixed in ac0e981 (#238), which took the issue's suggested option (1). `FEATURES.md:505-517` carries the corrected leaves.

What was still missing: nothing asserted the no-`outputFunc` branch itself. Unreachable through `reactive_output()` and untested, it reads as dead code, which is how a future cleanup deletes it and turns a clear abort into a `do.call(NULL, ...)`.

This adds a test that constructs the one render function that does reach the branch — hand-classed `shiny.render.function`, never through `createRenderFunction()` — and pins both `output_ui()`'s abort and `output_ui_or_null()`'s `NULL` skip.

`[ FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 0 | PASS 12 ]` for `test-output-ui.R`.

No behavior change, so no `FEATURES.md` diff.

title: fix: the robustness bugs from the FEATURES.md audit (#223 items 15–23)
description:
Stacked on #240. Closes items **15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 23** of #223.

## JS

| Item | Fix |
|---|---|
| **17** | `useShinyOutputValue()` drops the previous id's value when the id or namespace changes. `outputs.add()` only pushes a value when the new entry already has one, so an id the server had not answered yet kept rendering the **other** output's data as if it were its own. Falls back to the caller's `defaultValue`, and still adopts a cached value immediately so there is no flash of `undefined`. |
| **18** | `MISSING` now **cancels** a pending debounced send. It skipped `setInputValue` but left a queued send alone, so "real value then `MISSING`" inside the debounce window still delivered the real value ~100 ms later — the server holding a value the client had retracted. `ImageOutput` is where this bites: measure 400×300, element goes `display: none`, dimensions revert to `MISSING`, and the server renders a plot for dimensions that no longer apply. |
| **19** | a `priority` change now **warns**, naming the id and both values. Kept as last-writer-wins rather than made an error — see below. |
| **20** | `getReactRegistry()` becomes an accessor in the shape CLAUDE.md prescribes: attach-once (`??=`), module fallback without Shiny, never `undefined`. It read `shiny.reactRegistry` unchecked, yielding `undefined` when init had not run — a crash one call later, far from the cause. |
| **20** | `initializeReactRegistry()` is **idempotent**. It rebuilt both registries on every call, silently discarding every input value and output subscriber on the page; only the init latch made that survivable. |
| **20** | the output container is created on first `add()` instead of in the constructor, so constructing the registry in a DOM-less environment no longer throws — the policy `lifecycle-store.ts` already followed. |
| **21** | manufactured output divs no longer ship `This is the output div for <id>` into every page. |
| **23** | a config tag carrying no `protocolVersion` no longer skips the handshake silently: the IIFE logs, the npm build throws (an independently installed client cannot assume compatibility). |

### Why item 19 warns instead of throwing

`type` throws on a conflict because it changes *server-side semantics* — the wire id becomes `id:type`, routing through a different handler, so picking a winner silently would corrupt what the value means.

`priority` is not like that. It changes *when* Shiny recalculates, so a disagreement costs a coalesced update, not a wrong result. And throwing would break the documented action-button pattern, where a reader mounts `useShinyInput("count", 0)` and a button mounts `useSetShinyInput("count", 0, { priority: "event" })` for the same id — same-id-different-priority is the intended usage there. `debounceMs` is last-writer-wins for the same reason and nobody wants that to throw either.

What was worth fixing is the silence: two mounts fighting over one id produced a winner determined by mount order with no signal at all. The warning fires only on an actual change; setting the same priority again, or setting it first, stays quiet.

## Python

| Item | Fix |
|---|---|
| **15** | `ReactApp` re-checks the mode **per request** instead of latching it at construction, so creating or deleting `www/index.html` during a dev session switches modes with no restart. The UI was already a per-request function; only this check was frozen. |
| **16** | `www/` is mounted whenever the directory exists, and an explicitly passed `static_assets` — **including `None`** — now wins over the auto-mount. The guard was `is None`, so passing `None` auto-mounted anyway. |
| — | `page_react_html()` re-reads the document only when `(st_mtime_ns, st_size)` changes. |
| — | both HTML reads pass `encoding="utf-8"`. The default follows the platform locale while R decodes UTF-8 unconditionally — a real parity gap. |

### On the re-read question

The status quo was worse than it looked: under `ReactApp` the UI is a per-request function, so `page_react_html()` was doing a full `read_text()` on every page render. Now it stats each call and reads only when the signature moves — dev edits still appear on refresh, an unchanged document is read once.

No dev-mode flag, deliberately: a flag means two code paths, and one `stat` per page render is nothing against a page assembly plus websocket handshake. `st_mtime_ns` + `st_size` is the heuristic build tools use; it misses a same-nanosecond same-size edit, which needs a machine writing twice inside one filesystem timestamp tick. Unlocked on purpose — concurrent requests may both read and both store, costing one redundant read and unable to produce a wrong answer.

## One audit finding rejected

The audit reported that `ReactApp` "re-emits the missing-`ui.js` warning on **every** request". The `warn()` call does repeat, but Python's default warning filter dedupes by `(message, category, module, lineno)`, so exactly one warning surfaces. Measured: three calls → one warning. No caching layer for something the stdlib already handles.

## Tests

27 added across the three suites, **each verified to fail without its fix** — the id-change reset, the `MISSING` cancellation, the priority warning, registry idempotence, container laziness, the handshake, the per-request mode, the `static_assets` guard, the read cache, and the UTF-8 decode.

Two existing JS test files needed explicit registry resets: they had been using `initializeReactRegistry()`'s **non**-idempotence as their isolation mechanism, which is precisely the bug being fixed. Worth knowing as a general hazard — a suite can encode a bug as the thing that makes it pass.

Items **12** and **14** were split into #242 and #243: both are decisions rather than bugs, so they no longer sit in the #223 omnibus.

Suites: **JS 221 · R 190 · Python 107 · e2e 9.**

title: test: fail when the protocol surface grows without being declared
description:
Stacked on #239. The enforcement half of #232 — the policy decision itself stays open.

## Why

The surface grew without anyone noticing: #221 added the `shinyreact.init` handler (plus its `.shinyreact_init` ping) and the `shinyreact-deps` custom message while `PROTOCOL_VERSION` stayed `1.0`.

Worth stating plainly, because I had it wrong earlier: **`protocol/README.md` already has a versioning policy, and it is stricter than I assumed.** It says a *minor bump* covers "additive, ignorable changes: a new optional payload member, **a new message type**". By that rule #221 should have been `1.1`. So this was not a missing policy — it was an unenforced one, which is worse, because the document reads as authoritative while nothing checks it.

## What this adds

`protocol/surface.json` enumerates the whole boundary — custom message types, input-handler names, input ids, DOM ids — **beside the protocol version**. That adjacency is the point: adding a name means editing the file where the version lives.

Three guards, one per language, each reading the most authoritative source available:

| Suite | Source of truth |
|---|---|
| Python | shiny's `input_handlers` registry after `import shinyreact`, so a new `@input_handlers.add` appears whether or not anyone updates the test; plus a source scan for `send_custom_message` types |
| R | the same registry (`shiny:::inputHandlers`) after loading the package; plus a scan of `pkg-r/R/*.R` for `sendCustomMessage` types |
| JS | a scan of `pkg-js/src` for `addCustomMessageHandler` / `setInputValue` / `getElementById` literals |

The JS side scans source rather than asserting at runtime deliberately: a message type is only observable when Shiny is present *and* a message arrives, which is exactly the situation a unit test misses. The literal at the registration site is the thing that matters.

## Verified to fail, not just to pass

A guard that passes is worthless unless it also fails. Each was checked against a planted name:

- `[r]` a `"shinyreact.bogus"` handler in `.onLoad()` → `FAIL 1 | PASS 4`
- `[py]` a `"shinyreact.bogus"` handler in `_input_handler.py` → 1 failed, 3 passed
- `[js]` a `"shinyreact-bogus-new-type"` message in `dep-discovery.ts` → 1 of 6 failed

The JS scan also asserts it walked more than ten files, so a broken directory walk fails loudly instead of making every other assertion vacuous.

## What this deliberately does not decide

Whether #221's additions warrant `1.1`, and whether additive changes need a bump at all given the client compares only major versions (making a minor bump documentation rather than enforcement). That call is yours and stays in #232 — deferred, as you said, since nothing is released yet. `protocol/README.md` now records the mechanism *and* the open question, with the #221 discrepancy stated rather than smoothed over.

Suites: **R 185 → 190 · Python 99 → 103 · JS 197 → 203.** pyright and `tsc --noEmit` clean.

title: fix(js): install dependency discovery from the npm entry too
description:
Stacked on #238. Closes #233.

## The bug

`installDepDiscovery()` was called from `src/index.ts` (IIFE) and not from `src/npm.ts`. Consequences for an `@posit/shinyreact` consumer:

1. no `shinyreact-deps` handler, so dependencies the server pushes are never rendered and `bindAll` is never re-run;
2. no `.shinyreact_init` ping — and that ping is what bootstraps discovery *server-side*, so on an R server discovery was never installed for the session at all.

The feature #221 shipped was therefore absent end to end for the bundler tier. A `<ShinyOutput>` rendering plotly or a data frame just never bound, with no error. Verified in the artifacts before the fix:

```
$ grep -c 'shinyreact-deps' pkg-js/dist/shinyreact.js pkg-js/dist-npm/index.js
1    # IIFE
0    # npm
```

## Why calling it from both entries is safe

The concern with adding an import-time side effect to the npm entry is that it is otherwise side-effect-light — a consumer doing SSR or importing hooks in a node test should not get DOM work on `import`. `installDepDiscovery()` already satisfies that, and now says so explicitly:

- no `document` → immediate no-op (SSR, node tests);
- no Shiny yet → one event listener, nothing more;
- called twice → no-op (new idempotence latch).

## Latent hole fixed along the way

The waiting path used `document.addEventListener("shiny:connected", start, { once: true })`. If that event fired before `window.Shiny` was readable, the one-shot listener was consumed, `start()` returned early, and discovery never installed for the life of the page. It now stays subscribed until Shiny is actually there, then unsubscribes. (Found by the second `FEATURES.md` audit; the same shape exists in `lifecycle-store.ts` and is listed in #223.)

## The drift guard

`pkg-js/src/__tests__/entry-parity.test.ts` imports each entry module for real and asserts its observable side effects:

- both install the `shinyreact-deps` handler;
- both send `.shinyreact_init:shinyreact.init`;
- **only** the IIFE installs `window.shinyreact`, and **only** the npm build treats a missing config tag as fatal — the two deliberate tier differences, pinned so flipping either is a decision rather than an accident.

Nothing previously asserted what an entry point *does*, which is exactly why this diverged unnoticed. Confirmed the test fails with the fix reverted (2 of 4 fail).

`decisions/2026-08-17-js-distribution.md` gains a section stating the rule: "single source" does not make the two builds equivalent, because entry modules are where side effects live. Client behavior belongs in both; tier distinctions are deliberate, few, and test-pinned.

Suites: **JS 197** (193 → 197), **R 185**, **Python 99**; `tsc --noEmit` clean. Bundles rebuilt.

title: test: close the audit's test holes; document R's whole-document templating
description:
Stacked on #237. The straightforward half of the audit follow-up: tests for behavior nothing pinned, plus documentation for the one behavior we decided not to change.

Counts: **R 173 → 185 · Python 94 → 99 · JS 186 → 193.** pyright and `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Test holes closed

Each of these was named by an audit as a leaf no test pinned.

- **`shiny-bound-output` is now asserted**, not just described in a comment. It appeared only as prose in `test_shiny_output.py`, so nothing would have caught an element that rendered but never bound.
- `[r]` **the bundle script's `defer` attribute and absent `type`.** Python pinned its script attributes while R pinned only `src` — which is exactly how #182 (wrong attributes in R) survived as long as it did.
- **The stylesheet's unconditional attachment** and **the bundle-version fallback divergence** (`"0.1.0"` vs `packageVersion()`), asserted in *both* languages so the divergence stays deliberate.
- `[py]` **`set_react_page()`'s explicit-missing-path `FileNotFoundError`.** `test_set_react_page.py` contained no `pytest.raises` at all.
- **`page_react()` emits no body HTML**, and **`page_bare()` emits no config tag** — the second is what makes `page_bare()` the escape hatch.
- **The export sets**: `__all__` (8 names) and `NAMESPACE` (6), so an accidental addition or removal is a test failure rather than a surprise.
- `[js]` **the 15-member `window.shinyreact` surface.** The object literal in `global.ts` and the `Window` interface beside it would otherwise drift together and still typecheck. Also pins that `React`/`ReactDOM` are the real modules, since two Reacts on a page breaks hooks.
- `[js]` **`ShinyReactComponentElement`'s connect/disconnect lifecycle**, including that `unbindAll` is called **without** `includeSelf`. Pinned as today's behavior deliberately: the asymmetry with `ShinyOutput`'s carefully-reasoned `includeSelf: true` is unexplained (#223), so this makes changing it a visible decision instead of silent drift.
- `[js]` **`debounceMs`'s numeric default of 100.**

## Documentation

**#223 finding 2 — documented, not changed.** `?page_react_html` now states that `htmltools::htmlTemplate()` evaluates **every** `{{ ... }}` in the document as R code — anywhere, `<head>` or `<body>`, with the global environment as parent — not just the `{{ headContent() }}` marker. **`httpx` added to the `dev` dependency group.** `starlette.testclient` (used by `tests/test_app.py`) requires it, so `make py-check-tests` was failing at *collection* — not reporting a test failure — and the workaround was `uv run --with httpx`. title: fix(js): ship the stylesheet in the npm build
description: The IIFE bundle imports shinyreact.css as a side effect; src/npm.ts imported no CSS and package.json exposed no stylesheet, so @posit/shinyreact consumers got none of it. The only rule in that file is @keyframes spin, which ImageOutput's placeholder spinner animates with — so the spinner sat still for every bundler-tier app. The entry now imports the CSS so the lib build emits it (dist-npm/style.css), reachable as `import "@posit/shinyreact/styles"`. Vite does not inject a CSS import into a lib-mode ESM bundle — verified: dist-npm/index.js has no reference to style.css — so consumers are not forced to take it, and SSR/node consumers are unaffected. Found by the FEATURES.md audit (#223, finding 4). --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

title: fix(js): register message handlers on the singleton, not window.Shiny
description: useShinyMessageHandler() called `shiny.messageRegistry.addHandler(...)`, but `window.Shiny.messageRegistry` is only set by initializeMessageRegistry(), which is a silent no-op when Shiny is not yet present and never retries. If shinyreact's init ran before Shiny loaded, the property stayed undefined and the hook threw a TypeError once Shiny did initialize — messages were unusable, not merely unregistered. The hook now uses the module singleton, whose addHandler installs Shiny's dispatcher lazily, so it works whenever Shiny arrives. init() also publishes the registry on window.Shiny at the moment it installs the dispatcher, so the debugging surface is populated on that path too. message-registry.ts had zero tests. Adds five: lazy single-dispatcher registration, fan-out to every handler for an id, removal dropping the id, unknown ids ignored, and the late-Shiny path that was broken. Found by the FEATURES.md audit (#223, finding 6). --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

title: fix(js): remove the output's own div at cleanup, not any same-id element
description: scheduleCleanup() looked the div up with a document-global getElementById(outputId). Output ids are author-chosen, so an app can legitimately have an element with the same id in its own markup — and getElementById returns the first match in document order, which is likely to be the app's node, not the one inside our hidden container. Cleanup could delete part of the app's UI. The entry now holds a reference to the div it created and removes that node. Simpler than scoping a selector, and it sidesteps id-escaping entirely (CSS.escape is also absent from the jsdom the tests run in). Test: an app-owned element with a colliding id survives cleanup while the registry's own div is removed. Found by the FEATURES.md audit (#223, finding 5). --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

title: fix(js): run the protocol handshake before the restore-applied check
description: applyRestoredValues() returned early on a truthy `_restore["-applied"]` before reaching assertProtocolCompatible(), so a pre-set or forged window.shinyreact._restore silently disabled both bookmark restore and the wire-protocol version check — no warning, and a version mismatch would then surface as undebuggable payload corruption instead of the error it exists to raise. The handshake is a property of the page, not of the restore payload, so it now runs first. Idempotence is unchanged: an already-applied sentinel still preserves its snapshot. Two tests: a matching protocol still preserves the snapshot, and a mismatched one throws even when the sentinel says applied. Found by the FEATURES.md audit (#223, finding 3). --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

title: fix(r): declare the utils dependency
description: bookmark.R calls utils::getFromNamespace() (three times) and dep.R calls utils::packageVersion(), but utils appeared in neither DESCRIPTION nor NAMESPACE. It works today because utils is attached in a default R session; R CMD check flags it, and a stripped session would not. Found by the FEATURES.md audit (#223, finding 7). --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

title: fix(r): emit the #shinyreact-config tag in <head>, not <body>
description:
`shinyreact_dep_page()` returned a bare `tagList`, so under `page_react()` the config tag rendered inline in `<body>`. Python emits it via `head_content()`, and R's own `page_react_html()` path (`config_head_dep()`) already put it in the head — so R disagreed with Python *and* with itself, for a tag both packages document as head-injected.

Wrapping it in `tags$head()` is the direct counterpart of Python's `head_content()`. Behavior for the client is unchanged (it locates the tag by id), so this is placement parity, not a functional fix.

Verified before and after:

```r
htmltools::renderTags(page_react())   # before: $html has it, $head does not
```

Two tests pin the placement — one on `shinyreact_dep_page()`, one end-to-end through `page_react()` — asserting the tag is in the head *and* absent from the body. `extract_config()` now renders through `renderTags()` and reads both head and body, since `as.character()` alone returns only body HTML and would silently stop finding a hoisted tag.

Found by the `FEATURES.md` audit (#223, finding 1).

title: feat(r): output_ui() extraction + automatic renderer dep discovery
description:
Closes #203. Closes #146. Closes #138.

## Summary

R apps can now use traditional Shiny renderers (e.g. `plotly::renderPlotly()`) through `<ShinyOutput>` with **zero dependency wiring** — the server discovers each output's binding JS/CSS from its render function and pushes it to the client automatically.

**The primitive (#203):** `output_ui(render_fn, id)` builds the UI a render function's matching `*Output()` would produce, via the `outputFunc`/`outputArgs` attribute contract shiny's own `knit_print`/Express paths use (`shiny:::useRenderFunction`'s core, minus its domain-registration and `hasExecuted` side effects). The render expression is never evaluated — `outputFunc` is a pure UI constructor, so even `renderImage({})` extracts fine. This is the R counterpart of Python's `Renderer.auto_output_ui()`.

**Automatic discovery (#146):** Python Express harvests deps at page-generation time, but R renders the UI before `server()` runs, so R pushes instead. The shinyreact input handlers install a per-session `onFlushed` hook (idempotent; a `.shinyreact_init` client ping covers zero-input apps) that diffs `names(private$.outputs)` on **every** flush — a name `setdiff`, microseconds when idle — so module servers mounted after startup are covered too. New outputs' deps (deduped by name@version) go out as one `shinyreact-deps` custom message; the JS bundle awaits `Shiny.renderDependenciesAsync()` then re-runs `bindAll()` (safe: already-bound elements are skipped). The shiny client replays stored values on late bind, and R htmlwidgets carry their runtime deps (e.g. plotly-main) with the value, so only binding JS needs pre-delivery — R has no `comm_open` side channel, which is why this works where Python's #160 attempt stalled. Python Core port tracked in #220.

**Example (#138):** `examples/07-plotly/app.R` runs `plotly::renderPlotly()` over the same `www/` client as the Python app; the `ShinyOutput` className now carries both servers' binding classes (only the running server's binding JS loads, so the other set is inert).

Design record: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-r-output-ui-extraction-design.md` (includes rejected routes: explicit `deps=` arg, `MockShinySession` pre-run, AST scan).

## Verification

Browser-verified end to end (R has no e2e suite yet, #194): `R -e 'shiny::runApp("examples/07-plotly")'` → page loads with only jquery/shiny/shinyreact scripts → after first flush the client fetches `htmlwidgets.js` + `plotly-binding`, the output binds, plotly-main arrives with the widget value, and the chart renders; slider drives point count with a clean console. Python `examples/07-plotly/app.py` re-verified unchanged over the new bundle.

Local checks: R CMD check `Status: OK` (130 testthat, incl. new `test-output-ui.R` / `test-dep-discovery.R`), `make py-check` (74), `make py-test-e2e` (9), vitest (166), `tsc --noEmit` clean.
