title: feat: @posit/shinyreact dual build, wire-protocol doc, publish workflow
description:
Part of stack #209 (on top of #214 ← #208 ← #198). Implements steps 2 and 3 of `decisions/2026-08-17-js-distribution.md`. Refs #172, #28.

## Summary

**The wire protocol is now a versioned artifact.** `protocol/README.md` specifies everything that crosses the client/server boundary — the `#shinyreact-config` payload and its one escaping rule, the `shinyReactMessage` shape, the input-handler suffixes, handshake semantics, and the major/minor versioning policy. Its version *is* `protocolVersion`; the three per-language constants are pinned equal by parity tests, and a shared fixture (`protocol/fixtures/config-restore.json`, stress-testing quotes, `</script>`, U+2028/29, `__proto__` keys, float precision, null) is round-tripped by all three test suites.

**`pkg-js` builds two outputs from one source.** The existing IIFE (React inlined, `window.shinyreact`, ships inside the server packages) is untouched; a new ESM build (`vite.config.npm.ts` + `tsconfig.npm.json` for declarations) externalizes `react`/`react-dom` as peer dependencies. `package.json` becomes the publishable `@posit/shinyreact` (exports map, `files: ["dist-npm"]`, `dist-npm/` gitignored). One `npm run build` produces both, so the two tiers can never speak different protocol versions.

**Strict config for the npm tier.** The npm entry opts in via `requireShinyReactConfigTag()`: a page without the `#shinyreact-config` tag throws ("upgrade the shinyreact Python/R package") instead of silently degrading — an independently-installed client meeting a pre-protocol server is exactly the skew the handshake exists for. The IIFE keeps tolerating absence: it ships inside the server package and cannot skew, and `page_bare()` pages legitimately lack the tag.

**Publish workflow**: `release-js.yaml` publishes with provenance on `js-v*` tags or manual dispatch. Needs the `NPM_TOKEN` repository secret before first use.

**Deliberately out of scope**: converting `examples/09-hmr` to consume `@posit/shinyreact`. That needs a server-side switch for npm-tier pages to omit the IIFE bundle (otherwise two runtimes both register the `shinyReactMessage` handler) — a small API design question worth its own PR. Tracked in the decision record's updated status.

## Verification

- JS: 178 tests (new: shared-fixture round-trip, strict-mode throw on missing tag), `tsc --noEmit` clean, both builds produce output (`dist/shinyreact.js`; `dist-npm/index.js` ~27 kB ESM + `types/npm.d.ts`).
- Python 91 / R 143 tests pass including their fixture round-trips.
- `make update-dist` synced the rebuilt IIFE into both server packages.

title: feat!: Python page_react_html() accepts full documents via shinyreact.ReactApp
description:
Part of stack #209 (on top of #208 ← #198). Closes the R/Python `page_react_html` divergence left in #208. Built on posit-dev/py-shiny#2475 (`ui.PageDocument`), consumed as a **git dependency** on the PR branch until it releases — the swap to a release pin is tracked in #216.

## Summary

**New export `shinyreact.ReactApp`** (named to avoid confusion with `shiny.App`, which also works): a `shiny.App` for the ui.tsx pattern where the app file is just the server —

```python
from shinyreact import ReactApp

app = ReactApp(server, bookmark_store="url")
```

With no `ui=`, the UI is discovered next to the calling module the same way `set_react_page()` discovers it: `www/index.html` present → `page_react_html()` with the document's directory auto-mounted at `/`; otherwise → `page_react()` (`www/ui.js` / `www/ui.css`, served by the dependency itself). The discovered UI is a function of the request, so it re-renders per request and **bookmark restore works with zero wiring**. `ui=` (keyword-only) overrides discovery and behaves like `shiny.App`'s `ui` — except a direct `page_react_html()` result still gets its directory auto-mounted. Discovery reads the *immediate* calling frame (the `page_react_dep()` convention), so helpers wrapping `ReactApp(...)` must pass `ui=` explicitly.

Note the deliberate signature break from `shiny.App(ui, server)`: `ReactApp(server, *, ui=None)` is server-first because the UI is normally absent.

**Python `page_react_html()` now matches R**: it requires a complete HTML document containing a `{{ headContent() }}` marker (the kind a Vite build emits) and the body-fragment mode is removed. The same literal marker works in both languages — R evaluates it via `htmltools::htmlTemplate()`, Python passes it as `deps_replace_pattern` to `shiny.ui.PageDocument` (py-shiny#2475), which prefixes Shiny's own dependencies; shinyreact only adds its bundle and the `#shinyreact-config` tag as `extra_deps`. The user's document stays the only `<html>`, and no py-shiny private API is touched. You rarely call it directly — `ReactApp` discovers it.

## Verification

- 93 Python tests pass (new `test_app.py`: index.html discovery serves the single-`<html>` document + auto-mounted assets, ui.js discovery serves via the dependency route with the folder-name title, discovered UI renders the bookmark restore payload from a query string, explicit-`ui=` document/plain/UI-function paths), pyright and ruff clean, all 9 Playwright e2e tests pass — all against the git-dep py-shiny build.
- Template tests mirror the R test names per the parity policy.

## Follow-ups

- #216: swap the git dep for a release pin once py-shiny#2475 ships; re-evaluate how much of `ReactApp` py-shiny can absorb.

title: feat: add page_react() and template-mode page_react_html()
description:
Closes #205. Part of stack #209 (on top of #198 ← #197). Follows the two-mode design discussed for replacing the halfway index.html fragment.

## Summary

**Mode 1 — `page_react()` (Python + R, new export).** Zero-configuration server-composed page: no HTML file at all. Discovers `www/ui.js` and `www/ui.css` (named for the ui.tsx pattern per #205 — the source entry `ui.tsx` compiles to `www/ui.js`, paired with `ui.css`; the client entry is the *ui*, the server file is the *app*, and #204's rename discussion can flip the default later), serves them as an mtime-versioned `HTMLDependency` — so edits cache-bust, unlike raw `<script src>` tags in a hand-written HTML file. Title defaults to the app folder's name; extra `HTMLDependency` args pass through. The server emits no body HTML — the client appends its own mount container to `<body>`.

**Express follows:** `set_react_page()`'s `path` is now optional. With no args it uses `www/index.html` when present (existing behavior, so every current example keeps working), else falls back to `page_react()` discovery. Renderer-dependency harvesting works in both modes (extracted into `_harvest_renderer_deps()`).

**Mode 2 — R `page_react_html()` accepts a real document.** The file must be a complete HTML document containing a `{{ headContent() }}` marker (the kind a Vite build emits); it renders through `htmltools::htmlTemplate(document_ = TRUE)` with the shinyreact bundle and the `#shinyreact-config` tag injected at the marker via the new `config_head_dep()` (an href-less dependency carrying only head HTML). Fragment input now errors with a message pointing at the marker or at `page_react()`. Assets the document references live in `www/` and are served statically.

**Python `page_react_html()` is deliberately unchanged** (fragment mode): `shiny.App` has no way to accept a pre-rendered document with extra dependencies — `HTMLTextDocument` is only used internally for `ui=Path` with no injection hook (verified empirically: `App(ui=HTMLTextDocument(...))` fails on `get_dependencies`). The docstring documents the divergence and points users at `page_react()`. Closing this needs an upstream py-shiny change.

**Build-step examples converted to the free names.** `03-columns-shadcn`, `04-shadcn`, and `09-hmr` now build to `www/ui.js` (+ `www/ui.css`), drop their `www/index.html` fragments, and mount by appending to `<body>` — their `set_react_page()` calls need zero arguments. Verified by building all three and driving 04-shadcn in a browser (full UI boots off the discovered mtime-versioned dep routes). With #207 merged, the no-build examples (01, 02, 05–08, 10) are converted too: `www/app.js` → `www/ui.js` (+ css → `ui.css`), index.html fragments deleted, body-append mounts. `examples/01-hello`'s Core app drops its `static_assets=` mount (assets serve via the dependency), and its `app-core.py`/`app.R` use `page_react()`. Terminology docs (README, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, catalog, pkg READMEs) now name the no-build role `ui.js` and the Vite entry `ui.jsx`/`ui.tsx`. `page_react_dep()`'s defaults follow suit (`ui.js`/`ui.css`, formerly `main.js`/`main.css`).

## Verification

- Python: 84 tests (new: `page_react` defaults/title/css-skip/missing-js-warn/extra-deps/cwd-fallback; `set_react_page` index-precedence and discovery-fallback), pyright, ruff.
- R: 140 tests (new: template rendering with single `<html>`, config payload extraction, marker-missing error, `page_react` suite mirroring Python), `R CMD check` 0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 notes. Tests render through a `createWebDependency`-mimicking helper (`helper-render.R`) since standalone `renderDocument` can't href file-based deps.

title: feat: #shinyreact-config tag + protocol handshake, decide JS distribution
description:
Refs #172. **Stacked on #197** (base is `schloerke/rename-pkg-js`; retarget to `main` once #197 merges).

## Summary

Implements step 1 of the JS-distribution decision and checks in the decision record itself (`decisions/2026-08-17-js-distribution.md`: hybrid npm distribution — publish `@posit/shinyreact` as a real ESM runtime while keeping the IIFE HTMLDependency as the zero-build tier, with a wire-protocol handshake instead of lockstep releases).

**The `#shinyreact-config` script tag.** Page entry points (Python `_dep_page()`, R `shinyreact_dep_page()`) now always emit `<script type="application/json" id="shinyreact-config">{"protocolVersion":"1.0","restore":{...}}</script>`. This replaces the inline JS that pre-seeded `window.shinyreact._restore` — the one structural dependency on the global existing before the bundle runs — with inert JSON that any future ESM client can read too. Because the payload is never parsed as JavaScript, the two-layer JS-string-literal escaping (and the U+2028/U+2029 handling from #183) collapses to a single rule: every `<` is emitted as the JSON escape `\u003c`.

**Protocol handshake.** `PROTOCOL_VERSION = "1.0"` is declared in all three languages (`pkg-js/src/shiny-react/config.ts`, `pkg-py/src/shinyreact/_protocol.py`, `pkg-r/R/protocol.R`); each language has a parity test pinning the three strings equal. The JS client asserts the major version at boot and throws naming both versions on mismatch — this is what lets a future npm-installed client and a pip/CRAN server release independently.

**No legacy channel.** The config tag is the *only* restore delivery channel — the pre-config inline-script `window.shinyreact._restore` global is not read at all (the repo is pre-release; nothing shipped depends on it). `window.shinyreact._restore` remains only as a write-only `-applied`/`-values` DevTools sentinel, and `installGlobal()` is now a plain assignment since nothing writes the namespace before the bundle runs.

## Verification

- Python: 74 unit tests, pyright, ruff, and all 9 Playwright e2e tests pass (the e2e bookmark tests exercise the new tag end-to-end through a real browser).
- R: 122 testthat tests pass; test helpers moved to `helper-config.R` and mirrored against the Python test names per the parity policy.
- JS: 177 vitest tests pass (new `config.test.ts` plus config-tag cases in `use-shiny-restore.test.tsx`), `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- `make update-dist` rebuilt and synced the bundle to both language packages.

Reproduce: run a bookmarkable app (`examples/10-bookmarking`), view source — the head now contains the `#shinyreact-config` JSON tag instead of a `window.shinyreact._restore = JSON.parse(...)` script, and restored inputs behave identically.

title: chore: rename js/ to pkg-js/
description:
Closes #196. Refs #172.

## Summary

Purely mechanical rename of `js/` to `pkg-js/` so the JS package sits alongside `pkg-py/` and `pkg-r/` in the `pkg-*` sibling convention, ahead of publishing it as `@posit/shinyreact` (decided in `decisions/2026-08-17-js-distribution.md`, pending on its own branch).

- `git mv js pkg-js` — all files detected as 100% renames, including the committed `dist/` assets.
- Path references updated in live files only: `Makefile` (`PATH_PKG_JS`, the single source for all `js-*` targets), `.gitignore` (`!pkg-js/dist/`), `.pre-commit-config.yaml` excludes, `.github/workflows/check-js.yaml` trigger paths and `working-directory`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `docs/posit-conf-2026-goals.md`, and `examples/09-hmr/src/shiny-bridge.dev.ts` (relative import of the vendored source).
- Historical records under `docs/superpowers/` intentionally left untouched.
- Make target names (`js-setup`, `js-build`, …) are unchanged — only the directory moved.

## Verification

- `make js-lint` passes (tsc --noEmit).
- `make js-test` passes (166 tests, 12 files).
- `make update-dist` produces zero diffs — `pkg-js/dist/`, `pkg-py/src/shinyreact/www/`, and `pkg-r/inst/lib/shiny/` remain byte-identical, so the check-js "no uncommitted changes" job will pass.
- `grep -rn 'js/(src|dist)' --exclude-dir=docs` finds no remaining references outside historical docs.

title: docs(readme): add a "Prior and related work" section (#202)
description:
Closes #202.

Adds a `Prior and related work` section at the bottom of the root `README.md`, cataloging the existing React + Shiny efforts so readers can see where this repo sits.

Grouped by *shape* rather than by language, since that's the axis that actually distinguishes them:

- **Whole-frontend-in-React.** The same shape as the `ui.tsx` pattern, hand-rolled per app: [glin/shiny-react-example](https://github.com/glin/shiny-react-example), [filipakkad/react-shiny-template](https://github.com/filipakkad/react-shiny-template).
- **React components embedded in a traditional Shiny UI.** The inverted relationship, where Shiny owns the page and React renders individual widgets: [reactR](https://github.com/react-R/reactR) (plus Alan Dipert's rstudio::conf(2019) talk and the *Outstanding User Interfaces with Shiny* chapter), [Appsilon/shiny.react](https://github.com/Appsilon/shiny.react) + [shiny.fluent](https://github.com/Appsilon/shiny.fluent), [posit-dev/shiny-bindings](https://github.com/posit-dev/shiny-bindings), [pvictor/shinyReactWidgets](https://github.com/pvictor/shinyReactWidgets).
- **Broader catalogs.** [awesome-shiny-extensions](https://github.com/nanxstats/awesome-shiny-extensions).

Notes on sourcing:

- Activity/maintenance status was checked via the GitHub API (`pushed_at`), not inferred from search-result summaries.
- `posit-dev/shiny-react` does not exist as a repo. The `@posit/shiny-react` package this repo vendors is published from [wch/shiny-react](https://github.com/wch/shiny-react). That project is the closest prior work of all (we vendor it at `js/src/shiny-react/`), but it is not listed in this section; the README already names `@posit/shiny-react` in the hooks table and Architecture section. Worth a follow-up if we want it explicitly credited here with a link.

Docs-only change; no code or tests touched.

title: fix(examples): mount www/ in Core-mode apps
description: Stacked on #207 (base `schloerke/example1-oldfaithful-hello`). Split out of that PR to keep the two ideas separate: #207 rewrites the 01-hello example, this fixes a real bug it happened to surface. ## The bug `page_react_html()` reads `index.html` but does not serve the files `index.html` *references*. Shiny Express mounts the app directory's `www/` at `/` automatically: ```python # shiny/express/_run.py www_dir = file.parent / "www" if www_dir.is_dir(): app_opts["static_assets"] = {"/": www_dir} ``` Core's `App()` has no equivalent — `static_assets` defaults to `None`. So every Core app in this repo served `/` fine and then 404'd on its own scripts and stylesheets. This is not a path-resolution issue (`page_react_html()` found `index.html` correctly all along), which is why it presented as "the page loads but nothing renders." ## What was broken Both Core-mode examples, and only those: - **`examples/01-hello/app-core.py`** — 404 on `/app.js` and `/main.css`. - **`examples/10-bookmarking/app.py`** — same cause, worse symptom: its entire client bundle 404'd, so it rendered a **completely blank page**. Both now pass `static_assets={"/": Path(__file__).parent / "www"}`. I swept all ten examples to confirm the blast radius. Eight are Express (`set_react_page()`) and unaffected. The remaining 404s are unrelated and expected: `03-columns-shadcn` / `04-shadcn` need `npm run build` (their bundles are gitignored) and `09-hmr` gets `www/app.js` from the Vite dev server. Proof those are *not* this bug: `www/index.html` lives inside the mounted directory, and `curl /index.html` returns 200 on both — the mount is live, the bundles just aren't built. ## Docs The trap is invisible until you run the app, so it's documented where a Core user will actually meet it: - a **"Serving the client's files"** section in `page_react_html()`'s docstring, with the working snippet - the Core snippet in **`pkg-py/README.md`**, which previously showed `App(page_react_html(...), server)` — i.e. the broken form R needs no counterpart: `shiny::runApp()` serves `www/` next to `app.R` automatically. That is exactly why 01-hello's `app.R` worked all along and masked the Python-side gap. ## Tests None added — this is docs-and-examples only, with no package behavior change (`page_react_html()` is untouched apart from its docstring), so there is nothing new to assert. Worth considering as follow-ups, happy to file either: 1. **A CI smoke test over `examples/`** — boot each app, assert `/` and every `src`/`href` in its `index.html` returns 200. This is how 10-bookmarking's blank page would have been caught instead of sitting broken. 2. **A warning from `page_react_html()`** when the resolved `index.html`'s directory isn't among the app's static mounts. That is a real behavior change and would need its own tests. ## Verification - `app-core.py`: `/`, `/app.js`, `/main.css` all 200, and the full slider → histogram round trip drives correctly in a browser. - `10-bookmarking`: renders again, and bookmark restore still hydrates — `?_inputs_&txt="hi"&num=7` populates the inputs and the server echoes `text='hi' num=7`. - Console clean apart from `favicon.ico`. - `make py-check-tests` (74 passed), `make py-check-types` clean, `ruff` clean. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

title: docs(01-hello): rebuild example as Shiny's Old Faithful 01_hello
description: Rebuilds `examples/01-hello` as Shiny's canonical [`01_hello`](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/main/inst/examples-shiny/01_hello/app.R) Old Faithful app, `ui.tsx`-first. It replaces the previous name-input/click-counter latency demo. ## Why this app `01_hello` is the app every Shiny user has seen, which makes it the clearest possible place to show what changes under the `ui.tsx` pattern. Traditional Shiny renders the histogram **on the server** — `renderPlot({ hist(...) })` ships a PNG and the browser is a passive ``. Here the server never produces a picture: - **Server** — one `reactive_output` returning `{breaks, counts}` as plain JSON, plus a caption. That's the whole server: no plotting library, no image encoding, no `plotOutput` placeholder. - **Client** — `www/app.js` reads that JSON with `useShinyOutputValue` and draws the bars as SVG ``s. Because the chart is real DOM the client owns, it can be styled or made interactive without another round trip. The slider goes the other way: `useShinyInput("bins", 30)` pushes to Shiny, which recomputes the counts. Still no JSX, no bundler, no `package.json`. ## Notable bits - **`faithful.py`** — waiting times plus a stdlib-only equal-width binner, shared by `app.py` and `app-core.py`. Keeps the Python side dependency-free (no numpy/matplotlib), which matters for the example that exists to be minimal. - **`faithful.csv`** — base R's `faithful` exported so Python needs no data dependency. `app.R` uses the built-in dataset and `hist(..., plot = FALSE)`. - **`I()` in `app.R`** — without it, `bins = 1` serializes `counts` as a scalar instead of a length-1 JSON array and the client crashes. Found by clicking; worth knowing about generally when a `reactive_output` returns vectors. - **R returns `NULL` before the first `bins` message** — Python raises a silent exception instead. `req()` also works, but its silent error still reaches the client and shows up as a console error, which is a poor look for the flagship example. - **`useShinyOutputStatus`** — the chart stays mounted while the server recomputes and only dims, per the flicker guidance in `CLAUDE.md`. Dragging the slider never tears the SVG down. ## Relationship to #206 Second commit carries #206's change forward onto the rewritten example: `www/index.html` is two lines and `app.js` appends its own mount div to ``, preparing 01-hello for the upcoming `page_react()` mode where the server emits no body HTML. #206 has been closed as superseded. Note it was stacked on #198 (`schloerke/npm-distribution`) while this branches off `main` — if #198 needs the body-mount change on its own branch, it will have to be reapplied there. ## Stacked follow-up: #210 Rewriting this example surfaced a pre-existing bug — Core-mode apps never served their own `www/`, so `app-core.py` loaded `/` and then 404'd on `app.js` and `main.css`. That fix lives in **#210**, stacked on this branch, since it's a separate idea: it touches `10-bookmarking` and the package docs, not this example's content. **That means `app-core.py` is still broken on this branch alone** — it works once #210 lands. `app.py` (Express) and `app.R` are unaffected and work here. ## Verification Booted all three server entries and drove them in a browser: - R and Python produce **identical** counts at bins 1/2/7/30/50 (`sum == 272` throughout), and the `bins = 1` edge case renders. - `document.getElementById("root")` is `null`, with the mount div a direct `` child. - Console clean apart from `favicon.ico`. (The `app-core.py` round trip was verified with #210 applied on top.) `make py-check-tests` passes (74); `make py-check-types` clean; `air format`, `ruff`, and `prettier` applied. Note when trying it locally: `www/app.js` is served statically with no cache busting, so a hard refresh is needed after pulling.

title: refactor(examples): mount 01-hello by appending to <body>
description:
Stacked on #198 (base `schloerke/npm-distribution`).

## Summary

`examples/01-hello` no longer ships a `#root` div. `www/index.html` is now two lines (stylesheet + deferred script) and `app.js` creates its own mount container with `document.body.appendChild(document.createElement("div"))` — safe because the script is deferred, so `<body>` is fully parsed when it runs.

This prepares 01-hello for the upcoming `page_react()` page mode, where the server emits no body HTML at all and the client owns its mount point.

## Verification

Ran the app and drove it in a browser: no `#root` element in the DOM, the mount container hangs directly off `<body>`, typing a name updates both cards, and clicking brings client and server cards to the same count. (Note when trying it locally: `www/app.js` is served statically with no cache busting, so a hard refresh is needed after pulling this change.)

title: test: close the R/Python test-coverage gaps (#185)
description:
Closes #185. The remaining e2e item is split out as #194 (a sub-issue of #185).

R was at 17 `test_that` blocks / 42 assertions across 6 files against Python's ~53 tests. The `page_react_dep()` items landed with #189 and #191; this closes the rest.

## R additions

**`reactive_output()`** was tested only for S3 class identity — the whole file was 4 lines. Now covers pass-through for every JSON shape (object, integer, string, array, `NULL`) driven through `shiny::testServer()`, recomputation on input change, and the absence of any UI placeholder or html dependency — the R analogue of Python's `auto_output_ui() is None` / no `extra_deps`.

**Non-mocked bookmark restore** (`test-bookmark-restore-context.R`). All three existing R bookmark tests mock `.restore_input_values()`, so the fragile part — the `shiny:::hasCurrentRestoreContext()` / `getCurrentRestoreContext()` / `RestoreInputSet$asList()` path pinned to shiny >= 1.13.0 internals — was never exercised, and a shiny release changing those internals would break R silently. These drive a real `RestoreContext` via `shiny:::withRestoreContext()`:

- values read back from a real context
- values **not** marked used (mirrors Python's `_pending == set()` assertion — this is the property that keeps the app's own `restoreInput()` calls working in the same render)
- empty context → `list()`
- `restore_script_tag()` and `shinyreact_dep_page()` wrapping
- end-to-end emission through `page_react_html()`, with and without a bookmark

**`page_bare()` / `page_react_html()`** — previously asserted only the absence of `id="root"` and an error message. Now: title rendered exactly once, no shinyreact dependency, `HTMLDependency` arguments included, HTML byte-verbatim (trailing newline + CRLF), the working directory named in the not-found error, and relative-path resolution.

## Ported back to Python

**`test_input_handler_dispatch.py`** — real dispatch through the `:shinyreact.default` / `:shinyreact.asis` wire suffix via `AppSession._manage_inputs`, the counterpart to R's `shiny:::applyInputHandler` test. Python previously only looked handlers up in the registry, never exercising the suffix split, the id de-suffixing, module-prefix preservation, or `force=True`.

(The other reverse-port item — asserting *non*-transformation of nested structures through Python's no-op handler — landed in #191 alongside the R-side contract change it pins.)

## Counts

R: **30 → 105** passing assertions. Python: **61 → 74** tests.

(An earlier revision of these PR bodies quoted a 42 baseline for R. That was wrong — 42 is the count *after* #189 adds the `page_react_dep()` tests. Measured per branch against `origin/main`: 30 → 30 (#188) → 42 (#189) → 64 (#190) → 72 (#191) → 105 (#192).)

## Not included

**The R Playwright e2e suite** — now tracked as **#194**, a sub-issue of #185. The blocker there is fixture infrastructure (an R app runner alongside the Python one), not test cases, so it is a different kind of change from this one.

title: fix: converge the remaining R/Python API divergences (#184)
description:
Closes #184.

Works the #184 checklist. Several items asked for a *decision* rather than a fix ("worth converging deliberately rather than just matching"), so each call and its reasoning is recorded in **`decisions/2026-08-13-r-python-parity.md`**. The guiding rule: the same React component talking to either server should get the same data and produce the same page; divergence is acceptable only where matching would make the API worse in its own idiom.

## Converged

**`page_react_dep()` argument shape.** Took the better half of each. Python gains `src_dir=` and `name=` — the issue is right that R's explicit `src_dir` is the better design, because Python's frame inspection reads the *immediate* calling frame, so a library author wrapping the call silently resolves against the wrapper's directory. Inference stays the default (it is what makes the one-line app case pleasant) but is now opt-out. Both default to `main.js` / `main.css`, and **neither the script nor the stylesheet is attached unless the file exists** — Python previously emitted a 404-ing link for bundles shipping no CSS, R attached none at all; existence-gating is what either default was reaching for, and a tag pointing at a file that is not there is never useful for the JS either.

A missing `js_file` additionally **warns**. It is the entry point, so a gated dependency with no script is empty — it loads nothing and, unlike the 404 it replaces, leaves nothing in the console to diagnose. The warning keeps the "build the dep before the bundle exists" dev flow working (the `"0"` version fallback is unchanged) while making that silence audible. `src_dir` stays required in R (no `__file__` to infer from).

**`send_message()` namespacing (R).** Aborts when `session$ns` is missing instead of falling back to an un-namespaced type that no module-scoped handler matches. Every real Shiny session namespaces — `ShinySession$ns()` is `NS(NULL, id)` at top level — so the fallback only ever fired for a malformed session, where an error is the useful outcome. The test that asserted the old tolerance is replaced by one asserting the error, plus one covering the real top-level-identity case.

**Bookmark-restore error handling (R).** Dropped the blanket `tryCatch(error = function(e) list())`. Verified `hasCurrentRestoreContext()` returns `FALSE` (it does not error) outside a request, so the guard already covers the expected-empty cases; real breakage in the pinned `shiny:::` internals now surfaces.

**`shinyreact.default` input handler (R).** `[]` now yields `list()` not `NULL`, and `[[1, 2], [3, 4]]` keeps its nesting instead of flattening to `c(1, 2, 3, 4)`. Both were accidents of inheriting shiny's default coercion. The handler is now simpler as well as more correct — one "is this a genuine array of scalars?" test replaces the record-detection special case. Full contract tabulated in `CLAUDE.md`:

| JSON sent | R | Python |
|---|---|---|
| `[{name, size}, ...]` | list of records | list of dicts |
| `[0, 100]` | `c(0, 100)` | `[0, 100]` |
| `[]` | `list()` | `[]` |
| `[[1, 2], [3, 4]]` | nesting preserved | nesting preserved |

**`page_react_html()` file read (R).** Reads bytes verbatim via `readChar()` instead of `readLines()` + `paste(collapse = "\n")`, which dropped a trailing newline and normalized CRLF.

## Documented as deliberate, no code change

- **Relative-path resolution.** R has no per-caller `__file__`, and the alternatives (`sys.function()` walking, `srcref` inspection) are fragile. Under `runApp()` the working directory *is* the app directory, so the default works in both languages. The not-found error now names the working directory so a wrong CWD is diagnosable rather than mysterious.
- **Renderer `HTMLDependency` discovery.** `set_react_page()` is Shiny **Express** only, and Express has no R equivalent — the harvesting exists because Express hands the page function the renderers. Python's own Core-mode `page_react_html()` is equally dependency-blind, so R matches Python-Core exactly, which is the right comparison. Revisit only with a concrete failing app.
- **Scalar-array flattening.** An atomic vector is what R code wants and it matches shiny's own coercion; `type = "shinyreact.asis"` is the documented opt-out.

Verified: `make py-check` 67 tests green (format + pyright + tests); `make r-check-tests` 72 assertions green; `make r-check-package` clean apart from the pre-existing `:::` NOTE.

## `R CMD check` is now clean, and enforced

Two follow-ups from review:

- The last two `:::` uses (`shiny:::hasCurrentRestoreContext` / `shiny:::getCurrentRestoreContext`) now go through `shiny___*` wrappers using `utils::getFromNamespace()`, matching the convention #190 introduced for `shiny___to_json()`. `.restore_input_values()` composes them, so the file's "every internal use is confined to a named wrapper" claim holds literally. **`R CMD check`: 1 NOTE → 0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes.**
- `make r-check-package` now runs with `error_on = "note"`, so it stays clean. Verified both directions: clean tree exits 0; reintroducing one `shiny:::` call fails with `Error: R CMD check found NOTEs` (exit 2).

Landed here rather than on #190 because this branch already rewrites `.restore_input_values()` (dropping the blanket `tryCatch`), so doing it a branch lower would conflict on rebase for no benefit.

Test files still use `shiny:::` on purpose — they construct real `RestoreContext` / `RestoreInputSet` objects and dispatch through `applyInputHandler` to exercise the actual runtime path. `R CMD check` does not scan tests, and `getFromNamespace` indirection there would only obscure what is being poked.

**One gap:** this gates the `make` path only. The CI R-CMD-check matrix comes from `rstudio/shiny-workflows`, which calls `r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2` without exposing its `error-on` input (default `"warning"`), so CI still passes on a NOTE. I did not add a separate job blind — CI-only NOTEs (CRAN incoming feasibility, future file timestamps) would likely make it flaky-red. Happy to add one with an allowlist, or to request the input upstream.

title: fix(r): escape U+2028/U+2029 in the bookmark restore script (#183)
description:
Closes #183.

## The bug

`jsonlite::toJSON()` emits U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) and U+2029 (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR) as raw UTF-8. Both are legal inside a JSON string but are **line terminators in JavaScript**, so they are illegal inside a JS string literal. An R app whose bookmarked input value contained one emitted a `<script>` block the browser could not parse — breaking bookmark restore and anything else depending on `window.shinyreact._restore`.

Python gets this for free from `json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True)`. R now escapes both code points explicitly after `toJSON()`.

## Two more bugs found in the same pass

- **`digits = NA`.** `jsonlite::toJSON()` defaults to `digits = 4`, silently rounding bookmarked doubles — `3.14159265358979` came back as `3.1416`. Python's `json.dumps` is exact. This one is arguably worse than the reported bug, since it corrupts values without any visible failure.
- **Layer 2 uses `jsonlite::unbox()`** instead of `auto_unbox = TRUE`, stating the scalar contract for the payload string explicitly rather than relying on the heuristic — the loose end flagged at the bottom of the issue.

## Serializer: shiny's internal `toJSON()`

Per review — shiny has no public *to*-JSON helper (`safeFromJSON` is the only from-direction one), but it does have an internal `toJSON()`. It does **not** solve this bug: it is jsonlite underneath, jsonlite has no `ensure_ascii` equivalent, and U+2028 still passes through raw (verified). The escaping below is still what fixes #183 — confirmed by deleting just those two `gsub` lines and watching 4 assertions fail.

It is worth adopting anyway, and now is, behind a `shiny___to_json()` wrapper (named per review so the name itself flags the namespace reach, and reaching it via `utils::getFromNamespace()` rather than `:::`). It is the serializer Shiny uses for every other value it sends the client, so restored inputs now go over the wire identically to normal output values, and two of its defaults matter here:

- `digits = I(16)` — supersedes my explicit `digits = NA`, fixing the same rounding.
- `null = "null"` / `na = "null"` — jsonlite emits a `NULL` element as `{}`; Python's `json.dumps` emits `null`. One more R/Python divergence closed, with a test.

Cost: a second touchpoint on shiny internals. The file header previously claimed a single one, so it now lists both wrappers instead. `R CMD check` is back to the one pre-existing `:::` NOTE (the restore-context internals).

## Tests

New `test-bookmark-escaping.R` ports Python's `_extract_restore_payload()` round-trip helper to R and mirrors its value-safety coverage: line separators, numeric precision, quotes/newlines/tabs, `</script>` injection, and `__proto__` / `constructor` keys.

Confirmed the new tests fail without the fix (5 failures: the 4 escaping assertions + numeric precision).

Also adds the matching **Python** test pinning the `ensure_ascii` reliance — it was documented in a comment at `_bookmark.py:70-72` but nothing tested it, which is why R could diverge unnoticed.

Verified: `make r-check-tests` 42 → 64 assertions; `make py-check` green.

title: fix(r): emit script type="module" from page_react_dep() (#182)
description:
Closes #182.

## The bug

`page_react_dep()` built its `HTMLDependency` script entry differently per language:

| | script attributes |
|---|---|
| Python (`_page.py:111`) | `{"src": js_file, "type": "module"}` |
| R (`page.R:63`) | `list(src = js_file, defer = "")` |

An ESM bundle — the default output of a Vite `build.lib` config — loads fine from Python but throws on its first `import` when served from R, because the tag lacks `type="module"`.

## The decision

Match Python. `type="module"` is implicitly deferred, so `defer` is dropped rather than kept alongside. This does change behavior for an R user shipping a *classic* script; the docs now point that case at building the `htmlDependency()` directly.

## Tests

`page_react_dep()` had **zero** R tests despite being exported — exactly the gap that let this diverge. New `test-page-react-dep.R` mirrors Python's coverage in `pkg-py/tests/test_dep.py`: return type + `src`, mtime versioning, missing-JS `"0"` fallback, custom filenames + `name` override, and the script attributes (asserted both on the dependency object and in the rendered tag).

Verified: `make r-check-tests` 30 → 42 passing assertions; `make r-check-package` clean apart from the pre-existing `:::` NOTE.

title: fix(py): emit a single <title> from page_bare() (#186)
description:
Closes #186.

`page_bare(title=)` injected `tags.title(title)` as head content *and* forwarded `title=title` to `page_bootstrap()`, which emits its own `<title>` — two `<title>` elements in `<head>`.

Let `page_bootstrap()` own the title, matching the R implementation (`pkg-r/R/page.R:11`).

The existing test passed because it only asserted the string appeared *somewhere*; it now asserts exactly one occurrence:

```python
assert re.findall(r"<title>.*?</title>", rendered) == ["<title>My Title</title>"]
```

Verified: `make py-check` green (format, pyright, 63 tests).

title: docs: fix stale API references and consolidate historical plans
description:
Refs #182, #183, #184, #185, #186 — filed from the same audit, not fixed here.

## Summary

Documentation-only cleanup from an audit of `CLAUDE.md`, `DESIGN.md`, and the four READMEs against the code. Three independent commits:

**Stale API references.** `DESIGN.md` documented `useShinyMessageHandler` as `(id, messageType, handler)`; the real signature is `(messageType, handler, opts?)` (`js/src/shiny-react/use-shiny.ts:471`). The `page_react_dep()` docstring in `pkg-py/src/shinyreact/_page.py` still imported `page_react`, removed in #168.

**`docs/posit-conf-2026-goals.md` trimmed (−50/+8).** The file was relocated into `docs/` in #159 but its content was never refreshed past the April/May 2026 state — it described the R package as an unimplemented placeholder, referenced the `examples/ui-tsx/` and `examples/app-py/` trees, and built its goals on `output_react()`, `render_react`, `Spec`/`Element`, and `page_react()`, all removed in #168. I kept the Vision section, which is still the posit::conf narrative and isn't duplicated by `DESIGN.md`, and deleted the "Current state (May 2026)" section and gap-analysis table outright — both were entirely stale and both duplicate what `CLAUDE.md` now designates the issue tracker for. The R parity goal is rewritten to describe what actually ships, linking #182–#185.

**`docs/plans/` folded into `docs/superpowers/{plans,specs}`.** Four files predated that convention; split on the existing `*-design.md` → `specs/` rule. Pure renames, no references to the old path existed.

Deliberately *not* changed: `DESIGN.md` Tenet 4's language about dynamic dependency injection. It reads more absolute than the shipped `set_react_page()` dep discovery, but those deps are inspected at page build and injected on init rather than pushed at runtime, so the tenet holds.

## Verification

git log --stat origin/main..HEAD

The one non-doc file touched is a docstring line in `_page.py` — no runtime behavior changes, so the existing suite is the check. Rendered `docs/posit-conf-2026-goals.md` should read top-to-bottom with no dangling references to removed APIs; `grep -rn "docs/plans" .` should return nothing.

title: feat: helper packages RFC, MUI prototype, and scaffolding skill
description:
## Summary

Adds three coupled artifacts establishing the conventions for `shinyreact` downstream helper packages (the second one, after `shinyshadcn`).

- **RFC at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-12-downstream-helper-packages-rfc-design.md`** — defines what a "well-formed" helper package looks like (JS bundle shape, namespacing, Python API, asset injection, package layout). Covers categories 1, 2, 3, and 5 (styled libraries, headless primitives, copy-paste, specialized). Leaves theming, slots, controlled-vs-pushed inputs, and per-category divergences as open questions that the prototype answers concretely.
- **MUI prototype at `downstream-prototypes/shinymui/`** — 5-component validation of the RFC conventions: Button (action input + icon slot), TextField (controlled string), Slider (controlled numeric), Card (children composition), DataGrid (specialized, server-pushed via `useShinyOutputValue`). 6 factory tests, 4.3 MB bundle. Findings from the prototype are folded back into the RFC's open-questions section (§5) and a new bundle-size baseline subsection (§6).
- **`scaffold-shinyreact-helper` Claude skill at `.claude/skills/scaffold-shinyreact-helper/`** — fully self-contained (`SKILL.md` + 14 `.tpl` files) so it does not depend on shinymui's continued presence. Scaffolds a new helper-package prototype with one stub component wired end-to-end. Validated by scaffolding a transient `shinymantine` package that built, linted, tested, and served HTTP 200 (transient scaffold deleted; two SKILL.md fallback bugs caught during validation were patched in-flight).

Two implementation plans accompany the work under `docs/superpowers/plans/`. The follow-on umbrella issue (per RFC §8) will enumerate per-package child issues (`shinymui`, `shinyradix`, etc.).

## Verification

### shinymui prototype

```bash
cd downstream-prototypes/shinymui
(cd js && npm install && npm run build)
cp js/dist/shinymui.js pkg-py/src/shinymui/www/shinymui.js
uv pip install -e pkg-py
uv run python -m pytest pkg-py/tests/test_factories.py -v   # expect 6 passed
uv run shiny run --reload example/app.py                    # composite example
```

The composite example exercises every component: TextField updates a greeting, Slider filters the DataGrid in real time, Button increments a click counter, Card wraps the controls.

### scaffold-shinyreact-helper skill

Invoke via the Skill tool with inputs (short name, upstream npm package, prefix, stub component, target directory). The skill renders 14 templates with substitutions, runs `npm install`, builds the bundle, runs lint + the stub factory test, and runs a programmatic HTTP smoke test.

title: feat: shadcn/ui for shinyreact (47 components, Python + R) + Claude skills to wrap any UI library
description:
## What this adds

A new top-level `ui-frameworks/` area. Two things ship here, and the second is the larger goal:

1. **`ui-frameworks/shadcn`**, a shadcn/ui component library driven entirely from a Shiny server through shinyreact. 47 components, each with a Python helper (`pkg-py/shadcn/`) and an R helper (`pkg-r/shadcn.R`), usable from `app.py` and `app.R` with no install (`sys.path.insert` or `source()`).
2. **A reusable, framework-generic method for doing this for any React UI library**, captured as two Claude Code skills (`scaffold-framework`, `scaffold-component`) plus the codegen they drive. shadcn is the proving ground, not the endpoint. The skills are written to wrap MUI, Mantine, or anything else next, and `ui-frameworks/mui/` is already scaffolded as the first npm-library target.

The point it proves: shinyreact stays zero-component plumbing, a real third-party React design system can be wrapped on top of it once and driven from both languages off one wire format, and the wrapping itself is now a repeatable skill rather than a one-off. This is both the existence proof and the engine for the next library.

It began as the 12-component foundation (was PR #161, now closed) and grew to the full set here. `ui-frameworks` is a strict ancestor of this branch, so nothing from #161 is lost. One PR rather than a stack because the repo squash-merges, and stacked PRs do not survive a squashed base cleanly.

## Reviewing 20k lines without reading 20k lines

Most of the diff is generated or vendored. Skip:

- `js/package-lock.json` (~4k lines, lockfile)
- `www/shadcn.js` and `www/style.css` (build output, regenerates from source)
- `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` (generated docs)
- The top half of each `js/src/components/*.jsx`, which is shadcn's own source with TypeScript stripped and otherwise unchanged

What is actually worth your time:

1. One component per pattern, not all 47. The patterns are: `button.jsx` (input), `dialog.jsx` (Radix portal overlay), `dropdown-menu.jsx` (data-driven compound menu), `tabs.jsx` (metadata prop plus positional children), `sonner.jsx` (server push via message handler). Every other component is a variation on one of these five.
2. `js/src/index.jsx`, the 47-entry registry.
3. `js/src/styles.css`, the Bootstrap compatibility layer. This is the file most likely to bite, explained below.
4. `pkg-py/shadcn/__init__.py` and `pkg-r/shadcn.R` for the helper conventions.
5. `.claude/skills/` (the two scaffold skills) and `js/scripts/*.mjs` (the codegen they drive). This is the reusable method, described below, and the most important thing to evaluate if you care about the next library more than this one.

Read the cumulative diff, not the 28 commits. Those commits are working history (parallel-agent batches, two gallery redesigns, a cva removal and re-adoption) and squash down to one commit on merge. The per-milestone story with dates is in `ui-frameworks/CHANGELOG.md`.

## The bridge pattern

Each component file carries shadcn's source on top and a small shinyreact bridge below it. The bridge reads `element.props` sent by the server, maps them onto the React component, and connects Shiny state with the hooks. It is named `ShinyFoo` to avoid colliding with the shadcn `Foo` in the same file, then re-exported clean as `export { ShinyFoo as Foo }`. `index.jsx` registers all 47 under `shadcn:Name`.

Every shadcn component sorts into one of eight roles (Display, Container, Input, Action, Overlay, Collection, Hybrid, Push), so there were no unknown shapes left to design for by the end.

## Decisions that earned their place

Each of these exists because something concrete did not work otherwise.

- **`react-dom` is bundled, `react`/`react-dom/client` are not.** `window.shinyreact.ReactDOM` only exposes `react-dom/client`, which has no `createPortal`. Every Radix overlay needs `createPortal`, so `react-dom` is bundled (about 2 kB gzipped) while the rest stays shared with the host.
- **`styles.css` carries a Bootstrap compatibility layer.** Shiny loads Bootstrap unlayered, so it outranks Tailwind's layered utilities on everything it touches: card titles rendered at 28px, inputs at 16px, and Bootstrap's `.grid` overrode `grid-cols-2`. The fix is a compat layer scoped to `.shinyreact-output` that resets typography, re-asserts the grid columns, and uses `@source inline(...)` to force-generate utilities that only appear in app files (Tailwind scans `js/src`, not the apps). This is the subtle one.
- **`class-variance-authority` is kept, not inlined.** Using shadcn's real `cva(...)` keeps default and compound variants faithful to upstream and is the least-edit path. An earlier attempt to hand-inline it was reverted.
- **`className` passes through end to end.** Bridges merge a caller class last via `cn(variants(), className)`, so cva sets defaults and tailwind-merge lets the caller win. Python takes `class_`, R takes `class`.
- **Optional args are keyword-only.** Required positional, optional keyword-only (`def f(req, *, opt=…)`; R `function(req, ..., opt=…)` with `check_dots_empty()` on leaves). Positional misuse errors, and new optionals stay backward compatible.
- **Host hooks are an external module, not a local shim.** Bridges `import { useShinyInput } from "shinyreact"`; the bundler maps that to `window.shinyreact` and tree-shakes the unused hooks, exactly as `react` is handled. This replaced a hand-maintained `hooks.js` that eagerly destructured the global. See the dedicated note below for current state and next step.

## Host hooks: how they are consumed (current and next step)

Worth calling out on its own because it sets a pattern any downstream bundle should follow.

**Before.** `js/src/hooks.js` did `export const { useShinyInput, ... } = window.shinyreact`. That eagerly destructured a runtime global at module-eval time and kept a hand-maintained list of hook names that had to track core by hand. It reinvented, in a local file, what the bundler already does for React.

**Current (this PR).** `"shinyreact"` is declared a bundler external in `vite.config.js` (`external: ["react", "react-dom/client", "shinyreact"]`, `globals.shinyreact = "window.shinyreact"`), so a bridge writes `import { useShinyInput } from "shinyreact"` and the build rewrites it to a property access on the global, tree-shaking the hooks a file does not use. This is identical to how `react` and `react-dom/client` are already externalized, so there is one mental model for every host-provided dependency. Runtime behavior is unchanged by construction: same global, same property, lazy access instead of eager destructure. `js/src/shinyreact.d.ts` supplies ambient `declare module "shinyreact"` types for all eight hooks so authors get editor IntelliSense.

**Next step.** `shinyreact.d.ts` is an interim copy. Those hook type declarations should be owned and shipped by the core shinyreact package (it is fully TypeScript and owns the API), so every downstream framework imports the same contract instead of re-declaring it. That is a follow-up in core, not in this PR.

## The reusable engine: skills for any UI library

The 47 components were not hand-transcribed. They came out of a method that is the same for any React library, written down so it can be rerun. This is the part meant to outlive shadcn.

- **`/scaffold-framework`** bootstraps a brand-new integration under `ui-frameworks/` from scratch. It handles both framework models: copy-paste (shadcn, where you check in the source) and npm library (MUI, Mantine, where bridges import from the installed package). `ui-frameworks/mui/` is the scaffolded placeholder for the npm path, ready for its first component.
- **`/scaffold-component`** adds one component to an existing framework, and is explicitly framework-generic (shadcn is only the running example). Its core is an 8-type taxonomy (Display, Container, Input, Action, Overlay, Collection, Hybrid, Push) that fixes the hook choice and bridge shape per type. Wrapping a new component reduces to picking a type and filling a small bridge.
- The two codegen scripts the skill drives, `prep-component.mjs` and `finalize-component.mjs`, do the mechanical work: prep strips a source to a bridge-ready stub (TypeScript removed, `"use client"` dropped, exports neutralized, imports fixed, `@shiny` annotation appended); a human fills only the bridge; finalize reads the annotation and writes the registry entry plus the Python and R helpers. `download-components.sh` fetches sources into a gitignored staging dir.

What this means for review: the skills and the taxonomy are the durable artifact. shadcn demonstrates they cover all eight component shapes across Python and R; the next library should be mostly skill-driven rather than written by hand.

## Parity and verification

The wire format is identical across Python and R (same as core shinyreact). Parity was checked on the components most likely to diverge (DropdownMenu, Table, Tabs, Sonner, Calendar) and on the className and keyword-only changes. Both servers boot and serialize all 47 sections of the Component Explorer.

```bash
cd ui-frameworks/shadcn/js && npm ci && npm run build
uv run shiny run ui-frameworks/shadcn/examples/shinyreact-shadcn/app.py
#   shiny::runApp("ui-frameworks/shadcn/examples/shinyreact-shadcn/app.R")
```

CI note: `check-js`, `check-py`, and `check-r` are path-filtered to `js/**`, `pkg-py/**`, `pkg-r/**`, so none run on this PR. Only `verify-conventional-commits` does. Local checks pass instead: `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` on the Python module and examples, a clean import of all helpers, `pkg-r/shadcn.R` parses, and the bundle builds matching the committed `www/shadcn.js`.

## Known limitations and follow-ups (out of scope here)

- `ui-frameworks/` gets no CI coverage under the current path filters. A follow-up should add globs or a dedicated workflow.
- R single-column tables auto-unbox to a scalar and break the JS `.map`; wrap with `I()` to force an array (multi-column is fine).
- Deferred components: `sidebar` (very large), `form` (react-hook-form coupling), `combobox` (uses `@base-ui`, not Radix, so it will not follow this pattern).
- `ui-frameworks/` is a prototype area, deliberately outside the shipped `pkg-py` and `pkg-r` wheels. Nothing here is published or imported by the core packages.

title: feat(js): input setters accept functional updaters
fix: auto-discover module renderer HTMLDependencies in set_react_page (#87)
description:
Closes #87. Follow-up tracked in #160.

## Summary
`set_react_page()` (the `ui.tsx` pattern entry) previously injected downstream `HTMLDependency` objects into `<head>` only for the renderers Shiny Express passes to the page function as positional args. Renderers defined inside `@module.server` were invisible, so their JS/CSS never loaded and the component failed to mount in the browser (e.g. `shinywidgets`' `ipywidget-output-binding`, needed by a module-level `render_plotly`).

This PR makes `_react_page_fn` also harvest dependencies from every renderer registered on the active session (`get_current_session().output._outputs`), resolving each via `.tagify()` so late-binding deps surface. At the Express UI/tagify pass the stub session already holds every synchronously-mounted renderer — top-level and module — so their dependencies now reach `<head>` automatically, with no `extra_deps` boilerplate. The existing `*args` walk is retained (Shiny de-duplicates by name+version, so overlap is harmless).

Coverage delivered: top-level renderers (unchanged); `@module.server` renderers (the #87 bug, now auto-discovered); and `@render.ui` / `insert_ui` dynamic UI (delivered natively by Shiny, verified by a new e2e test). Not in scope: dependencies for renderers registered *after* page load (e.g. a `render_plotly` created in a `@reactive.effect` with a React-supplied placeholder) — investigated thoroughly, no clean automatic fix found (the shinywidgets `comm_open` message is dropped before the late-loaded dependency registers its handler), deferred to #160 with full findings. R's `page_react_html()` has no renderer auto-discovery at all — tracked in #146.

## Verification

Adds two design memos under `decisions/`, split by idea after early

- **`decisions/2026-05-20-class-based-ui-components.md`** — the accepted
  direction. UI components become classes (`__init__` stores args,

title: feat(examples): hot reload (React Fast Refresh) for the ui.tsx pattern
description:
## Summary

Adds `examples/ui-tsx/09-hmr/` — a worked `ui.tsx`-pattern example that gives app authors **true React Fast Refresh** while Shiny serves the page (edit a component, it hot-swaps in place keeping state — no full reload, no `vite build` wait). Entirely in the JS/build layer: **no Python or R API changes**, so it works for both backends.

Of the three cases in #132: the `app.py` and no-build `www/app.js` paths already reload (now documented); this delivers the hard one — partial refresh for the bundled `ui.tsx` path.

### How it works
- Shiny serves the page + reactive WebSocket as usual. A Vite **dev server** serves the React modules with Fast Refresh.
- A serve-only Vite plugin writes the statically-served `www/app.js` as a stub (Fast Refresh preamble + dynamic import of `@vite/client` and the entry from the dev server); `vite build` overwrites it with the real IIFE bundle. `index.html` (`<script type="module" src="app.js">`) never changes between modes.
- **Key constraint:** `window.shinyreact.React` is a *production* React, which can't drive `react-refresh`. So in dev the example bundles its own dev React + the vendored `shiny-react` hooks; the prod build externalizes both to `window.shinyreact`. A `shiny-bridge` alias swaps dev/prod so `App.tsx`'s imports never change.
- Component (`src/App.tsx`, the refresh boundary) is split from the mount (`src/ui.tsx`, `createRoot` only) — required for Fast Refresh.

Design spec and plan are under `docs/superpowers/`. Deferred follow-ups (a dev `shinyreact.dev.js` bundle; a shipped dev helper/CLI) are recorded in `docs/todos.md`.

## Test Plan
- [x] `npm test` (dev-stub generator unit tests) — 3/3 pass
- [x] Prod path: `npm run build` + `shiny run` — page renders, Shiny round-trip works (count → server-doubled), IIFE loads as a module
- [x] Dev path: `npm run dev` + `shiny run` — editing `App.tsx` hot-swaps the component while preserving `count` (verified a planted `window` marker survives, i.e. no full reload); dev stub is cleaned up on shutdown

Addresses #132.

title: feat: route untyped useShinyInput values through a built-in shinyreact.default handler (#124)
description:
## Summary

Fixes #124. Array-of-objects `useShinyInput` values (e.g. a file input sending `[{name, size, type}, ...]`) arrived on the **R** server as a flat *named character vector* — keys repeating once per element — instead of a list of records, so the natural port of the Python code (`for (f in input$x) f$size`) errored with `$ operator is invalid for atomic vectors`.

The flattening is done by Shiny's *default* no-type input handler (`unlist(val, recursive = TRUE)`); R actually parses the inbound JSON cleanly (`simplifyVector = FALSE`). A `:type`-suffixed value intercepts **before** that flattening.

So this PR makes shinyreact's JS hooks default every untyped input's wire id to a `:shinyreact.default` suffix, and registers two server-side handlers in **both R and Python**:

- **`shinyreact.default`** — the global default. **R:** smart handler that preserves arrays-of-objects as a clean list of records, while still flattening scalar arrays (`[0,100]` → `c(0,100)`) exactly as Shiny's default does. **Python:** no-op (Python already deserializes to a list of dicts). The *only* behavior change vs. Shiny's default is the records case — the bug.
- **`shinyreact.asis`** — opt-in pure pass-through via `type="shinyreact.asis"`, for nested structures you want returned completely untouched. Identity in both languages.

Result: the same React component is portable across R and Python, and `for (f in input$x) f$size` (R) matches `for f in input.x(): f["size"]` (Python). An explicit `type=` (e.g. `shiny.datetime`) still overrides the default.

Design + plan: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-04-shinyreact-default-input-handler-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-04-shinyreact-default-input-handler.md`.

## Changes

- **JS** (`js/src/shiny-react/input-registry.ts`): default the wire suffix to `:shinyreact.default` when no explicit `type`; conflict-error message now reflects the real wire id. Built bundles rebuilt (`js/dist`, `pkg-py/.../www`, `pkg-r/inst/lib/shiny`).
- **R** (`pkg-r/R/input-handler.R`, `pkg-r/R/zzz.R`): `default_input_handler` / `asis_input_handler`, registered in `.onLoad`.
- **Python** (`pkg-py/src/shinyreact/_input_handler.py`, `__init__.py`): both handlers registered at import.
- **Example**: `examples/app-r/02-inputs` `output$fileout` simplified to iterate clean records (no JS change needed — that's the zero-config demo).
- **Docs**: CLAUDE.md "Common patterns" subsection, `docs/features.md`, `docs/todos.md`.

## Test Plan

- [x] JS: `make js-lint` + `vitest` — 183/183 pass (new default-suffix + override assertions)
- [x] R: `make r-check` — `R CMD check` 0 errors / 0 warnings / 1 pre-existing NOTE; new `test-input-handler.R` (13 assertions) exercises the real `shiny:::applyInputHandler` dispatch path
- [x] Python: `make py-check` — 357 pass incl. new `test_input_handler.py` (registration, no-op behavior, idempotency)
- [ ] Manual: upload multiple files in `examples/app-r/02-inputs` and confirm the file-output card lists each file with no R error

## Notes / out of scope

A first-class API for *app authors* to register their own per-id input handlers (validate/coerce/deny) and `ignore_init`-at-the-input-layer remain open — see the trimmed entry in `docs/todos.md`.

title: fix: seed static React mounts inserted after page load (#120)
description:
Closes #120

## Summary
`Node.tagify()` emits a `.shinyreact-static` mount whose React spec was seeded only once, at `DOMContentLoaded` — so a mount delivered *after* load (a `@render.ui` returning a `Node`, or `insertUI`) rendered nothing. This adds a standing `MutationObserver` (`js/src/inline-spec.tsx`) that seeds `.shinyreact-static` mounts as they are inserted. `seedInlineSpecs(root?)` is now scoped to the freshly-inserted subtree, the `seedMount` `hasRoot` guard keeps every pass idempotent, the `DOMContentLoaded` pass is retained as a zero-cost fast path for load-time chrome, and `seedInlineSpecs` is exposed on `window.shinyreact` as a manual escape hatch.

Static mounts stay distinct from outputs — no convergence with `output_ui` (an output needs an id + a WebSocket value; a static mount has neither). The `MutationObserver` was chosen over every alternative because none works or is clean: no non-monkeypatch Shiny hook exists; `shiny:bound` fires on binding elements and a static mount is not one (in the canonical `@render.ui`→`Node` case the inserted content has no binding, so it never fires); `shiny:value` is cancelable, fires *before* the default render, and never fires for `insertUI` of binding-free content; wrapping `Shiny.bindAll` monkeypatches another library's internals. The observer reacts to the actual DOM mutation, so it is correctly timed by construction and uniform across `@render.ui`, `insertUI`, and even non-Shiny insertions. This is a deliberate, documented deviation from the issue's "no standing observer unless shown necessary" — shown necessary, with the rationale recorded on the issue and in the nesting spec §4.

The JS bundle is shared by both packages, so `make update-dist` rebuilt `pkg-py/src/shinyreact/www/` and `pkg-r/inst/lib/shiny/`; no server-side change was needed (dependencies already ride along on `Node.tagify()`'s `TagList`, so Shiny's `renderContent` injects them).

## Verification
New Playwright e2e `pkg-py/tests/playwright/test_post_load_insert.py` proves the fix and is the regression guard: a `@render.ui` returning `Node("Badge", ...)` is clicked into the DOM after load. Before the fix the `.shinyreact-static` mount attached but rendered nothing; after the fix the badge renders.

- e2e: `make py-test-e2e` (or `uv run pytest pkg-py/tests/playwright/test_post_load_insert.py --browser chromium -o addopts=`)
- JS units (scoped-root, root-self, post-load insertion, nested insertion): `cd js && npx vitest run src/__tests__/inline-spec.test.tsx`

title: refactor: script-safe JSON helper for inline-spec embedding (#125)
description:
Closes #125

## Summary
Replaces the blanket `<` -> `<` gsub/replace hack — used to embed a `Node`'s serialized spec into an inline `<script type="application/json">` for the static-mount delivery path — with a deliberate, documented, script-safe JSON helper shared in spirit across R and Python. Python adds `script_safe_json()` in `pkg-py/src/shinyreact/_spec.py` (now called by `Node.tagify()`); R adds the internal `.script_safe_json()` in `pkg-r/R/wire.R` (now called by `as.tags.shinyreact_node()`). Both escape the full script-dangerous set to lossless `\uXXXX` JSON escapes — `<`, `>`, `&` (neutralizes `</script>`, `<!--`, `-->`, `<![CDATA[` breakouts) plus U+2028/U+2029 (valid in JSON but illegal unescaped in a JS string literal). The two implementations carry matching escape tables and cross-reference each other in comments to stay in lockstep. No JS change is needed: `seedInlineSpecs()`'s `JSON.parse` natively decodes the `\uXXXX` escapes back to their characters, so embedding round-trips losslessly.

One intentional cross-language difference: `jsonlite::toJSON` escapes `/` as `\/` by default (pre-existing, unrelated to script-safety), so R and Python were never byte-identical for `/`-containing payloads. The R round-trip test therefore asserts the contract (escaped `<`/`>`, lossless `fromJSON`) rather than byte-equality.

## Verification
- Python: `make py-check-tests` (353 pass), `make py-check-types` (0 errors), `make py-format` clean.
- R: full `testthat` suite passes; `make r-check-fixtures` reports the shared wire fixtures in sync; `air format` clean.
- New tests on both sides assert `</script>`, `<!--`, and U+2028/U+2029 payloads are escaped and round-trip safely. Example (Python): `script_safe_json({"x": "</script>"})` returns `'{"x": "</script>"}'`, which `json.loads` (and the client's `JSON.parse`) decode back to the original.

title: fix(js): seed inline static specs at DOMContentLoaded (#123)
description:
Fixes #123

## Summary
`test_static_node_in_chrome` flaked on CI because the static-mount seeding raced React's render against component registration — not because the mount was missing from the DOM (the issue's suspected cause). A static `.shinyreact-static` mount renders a component registered by a *separate* `defer` bundle. `installInlineSpecSeeding()` ran at `readyState === "interactive"` and seeded immediately, before that sibling bundle executed. React 19's concurrent render usually flushed after registration (pass), but on a loaded CI box it occasionally flushed first, hit an unknown component, threw in `renderNode`, and left the mount's React root poisoned — every later seed pass skips it via `hasRoot()`, so the badge never appears. Neither fix proposed in the issue would work on its own: waiting can't recover a permanently-thrown render, and re-seeding is a no-op against a poisoned root.

The fix seeds on `DOMContentLoaded` instead of mid-parse. `DOMContentLoaded` fires only after every parse-time `defer`/module script has executed, so all sibling registrations have landed before any static mount renders. A `load` listener is a safety net, `readyState === "complete"` still seeds immediately, and the deliberate throw on genuinely-unknown components is preserved (a typo is still unregistered at `DOMContentLoaded`). Late-after-load insertion (#120) remains out of scope.

## Verification
New unit tests in `js/src/__tests__/inline-spec.test.tsx` lock each ingredient of the race — the two headline tests were RED before the fix (one asserting seeding is deferred, one reproducing the exact `Unknown component "Badge"` throw) and are GREEN after. Full JS suite: 179/179 pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean. The previously-flaky `test_static_node_in_chrome` e2e passed 8/8 consecutive runs. Bundle rebuilt via `make update-dist` into `pkg-py/src/shinyreact/www/` and `pkg-r/inst/lib/shiny/`.

## What

Sync the docs (`pkg-py/README.md` + `CLAUDE.md`) with the shipped API. Three docs-only fixes:

### 1. `Spec`/`Element` no longer exist in Python (README + CLAUDE.md)
Both files referenced `shinyreact.Spec(root=..., elements={...})` and `shinyreact.Element(...)`, which **don't exist in the Python package** — only `Node` is exported. `Spec`/`Element` exist solely as TypeScript wire types (`js/src/spec.ts`).

- CLAUDE.md terminology + Python-package sections → reference `Node`

### 2. `Node.to_spec()` never existed (CLAUDE.md + README)
Replaced the bogus `Node.to_spec()` claim with the real API: `.serialize()` → `(wire_tree, deps)`, `.to_dict()` → wire tree, `.tagify()` → static mount. Downstream render example in both files → `value.to_node().to_dict()` (no `Spec` layer exists).

### 3. R package is no longer a placeholder (CLAUDE.md)
CLAUDE.md called `pkg-r/` "not yet implemented", but it ships a full API (`node`, `output_react`, `render_react`, `reactive_output`, `page_react*`, `send_message`), testthat tests, man pages, and bundled JS.

- Added an `### R package` subsection documenting the exports and the R-idiom differences from Python (children via `...`, `render_react`/`reactive_output` as functions not decorators, `page_react_html()` ≈ Python's `set_react_page()`), and noted the cross-language wire format is verified by `make r-check-fixtures`

## Why

Docs-only. The README `app.py` example as written would `AttributeError` on `shinyreact.Spec`, and CLAUDE.md misdescribed both the `Node` API and the (now-implemented) R package.
