title: feat(r): implement the shinyreact R package (#91)
description:
Promotes `pkg-r/` from a placeholder (built JS/CSS only) to a working `shinyreact` R package that mirrors the Python API and conforms to the current **discriminated-union wire format** (#119, "layer all the way down"). Closes #91.

Built spec → plan → subagent-driven TDD; after `origin/main` merged #119 mid-stream, the data model was reworked from the original flat-map design to the nested tree (a second spec + plan + TDD pass). Designs/plans live under `docs/superpowers/{specs,plans}/`.

## What ships

**Two patterns (parity with Python):**
- **`app.R` pattern** — UI described as R objects: `node("Component", ..., props=)` trees, rendered by `render_reactive()` and `ui_output()`.
- **`ui.tsx` pattern** — static React client served via `page_react_html()`; server returns raw JSON-serializable values for `useShinyOutputValue()`.

**Data model + serializer (`node.R`, `wire.R`):**
- `node()` is a plain **S3** object (`shinyreact_node`) — no `Spec`/`Element`/`to_spec`, no S7.
- Internal `as_wire()` S3 walker converts a `node()` / htmltools `tags$*` / `HTML()` / string / number tree into the `{type: "react"|"tag"|"text"|"html", ...}` wire tree, translating HTML attrs (`class`→`className`, …) and harvesting `HTMLDependency` objects. Scalars are `jsonlite::unbox()`-wrapped so Shiny serializes them as JSON scalars.
- `node()` embeds directly in page chrome too, via `as.tags.shinyreact_node()` → a `.shinyreact-static` mount + inline JSON the JS bundle hydrates.

**Rest of the surface:**
- `render_reactive()` (+ internal S3 `should_walk` deciding walk-vs-passthrough; warns on render-time deps), `ui_output()`, `send_message()` (module-namespaced `shinyReactMessage`), `page_bare`/`page_react`/`page_react_html`/`page_react_dep`.
- **Bookmark restore** (`restore_script_tag()`): reads R Shiny's restore context non-destructively via accepted `shiny:::` internals (`getCurrentRestoreContext` + `RestoreInputSet$asList()`); emits `window.shinyreact._restore`. `shiny` floor pinned to the verified `>= 1.13.0`.
- mtime-based dep versioning with a `packageVersion()` fallback.

**Cross-language parity:** committed fixtures (`pkg-py/tests/fixtures/wire_format/`) are the source of truth; Python asserts it produces them and R asserts it reproduces them semantically — covering the wire tree (react/tag/text/html, sibling-list root, attr translation, number→string coercion) **and** the attr map (`.ATTR_MAP` ⇔ `_ATTR_MAP`). `make r-check-fixtures` keeps the R copies in sync.

**CI:** enabled `check-r.yaml` (the package now has a `DESCRIPTION`) — `routine` (air format + tidy) and `R-CMD-check` (`--as-cran`).

**Examples:** `examples/app-r/{01-hello-world,02-inputs,04-messages}` and `examples/ui-tsx-r/01-hello` (reuse the language-agnostic JS/CSS verbatim); `01-hello-world` shows interleaved htmltools content inside a `node()`.

**Docs:** `docs/features.md` R section, root + `pkg-r/` READMEs, `_pkgdown.yml`; the original R spec carries a superseded note pointing at the rework spec.

## Verified live

Drove the example apps in a headless browser: the `node()` tree renders, the input→server round-trip works (e.g. `toupper()` echo), `send_message` toasts arrive, and the `02-inputs` file-input response renders correctly (fixed an R/Python deserialization gotcha — `input$filein` arrives as a flat named vector, not a list of dicts).

## Follow-ups filed

- #123 — flaky `test_static_node_in_chrome` e2e (static-mount seeding race; pre-existing, JS-side).
- #124 — `useShinyInput` array-of-objects arrives as a flat named vector on the R server (ergonomics).
- #125 — inline-spec `<script>` escaping is a blanket `gsub`/`replace` hack (R + Python).
- #27 — documented v1 limitation: bookmark `auto_unbox` shape divergence for single-value multi-value inputs.

## Out of scope (per design)

CRAN submission, `ImageOutput`/`render.plot`, Playwright e2e against R examples.

## Test plan

- [x] `make r-check` — 0 errors | 0 warnings | 1 note (accepted `shiny:::` note)
- [x] R unit tests — **89 passing** across 10 files (`devtools::test()`)
- [x] `make r-check-fixtures` — R/Python fixtures in sync (wire tree + attr map)
- [x] Python suite — **350 passing**
- [x] All 4 example apps build into `shiny.appobj` and were smoke-tested live in a browser
- [x] CI green on PR (`check-r`, `check-py`, Conventional Commits)

title: ci(e2e): mirror Playwright image to GHCR as lazy pull-through cache
description:
## What

Replaces the `actions/cache` + `docker save`/`load` approach in `setup-playwright-remote` with a **lazy pull-through cache backed by GHCR**:

- Pull `ghcr.io/<owner>/<repo>/playwright:v<version>-noble` first — co-located with the runner, no Azure/MCR round-trip and no `docker load` of a multi-GB tar.
- On a miss, fall back to MCR (keeping the existing 5-attempt retry loop for MCR's intermittent "request is blocked"), then tag + push to GHCR for the next run.
- Drops ~85 lines of cache machinery.

The image is always tagged to the MCR name locally, so the unchanged "Start Playwright server" step works as-is. Version resolution and everything from server-start onward are untouched.

## Why

On a fresh ephemeral runner the Playwright image (~2 GB) must arrive every run. The old `actions/cache` hit still cost ~1 min because `docker load` of the uncompressed tar is itself slow. GHCR is co-located with the runners, so a hit is a fast pull.

## Trade-offs

- **First run per Playwright version:** still slow (MCR pull + GHCR push, one-time).
- **Every run after:** fast GHCR pull.
- Concurrent first-runs on a fresh version are harmless (same digest).

## Caveat

The `py-test-e2e` job now needs `permissions: packages: write` so `GITHUB_TOKEN` can push to GHCR (added in this PR). This first CI run will be a GHCR miss → MCR fallback + push; subsequent runs exercise the fast path.

title: feat: layer all the way down — nest htmltools and the React spec at arbitrary depth (#88)
description:
## Summary Closes #88. Closes #98. Lets htmltools content (`Tag`, `TagList`, `HTML`, strings) and shinyreact's React data model (`Node`) interleave at **arbitrary depth in one tree**, in both directions. - **New wire format — a recursive discriminated-union tree.** Replaces the flat `{root, elements}` map. Each node carries a closed `type` ∈ `react | tag | text | html` plus a separate `name` (component name for `react`, DOM tag name for `tag`). This removes the synthetic key-map and its reconciliation churn, and dissolves the `` collision (tag name lives at `name`, attributes in `props`). - **One `process_ui`-shaped walker** (`_walk` / `serialize_ui` in `_spec.py`) converts any mixed `TagChild` subtree into `(wire_tree, harvested HTMLDependencies)`. Attribute translation (`class`→`className`, `for`→`htmlFor`, …; `data-*`/`aria-*` passthrough). `HTML(...)` → opaque `html` node; deps are pulled out as a side-list. - **`Node` is now a `Tagifiable`.** A static `Node` embedded in page chrome renders to an **id-less** `
`; the JS bundle's `seedInlineSpecs()` renders it at load. Reactive `Node`s returned from `@reactive_output` are walked and delivered over the WebSocket. The two paths are cleanly separated (`.shinyreact-static` no-id vs `.shinyreact-output` id-bound). Inline JSON escapes `<` as `<` to prevent `` breakout. - **`reactive_output.transform`** walks `Node`/`Tag`/`TagList`/`Tagifiable` content; bare `str`/`int`/`dict`/`list`/`None` pass through as JSON (so `useShinyOutputValue` outputs are unaffected). Warns when a render-time tree carries `HTMLDependency` objects that can't reach `` post-render. - **JS renderer** dispatches on `type` (registered component / intrinsic tag / text / raw html), throws on unknown component names, and honors an explicit `key` in props. - **Breaking (pre-1.0):** the flat `shinyreact.Spec` / `shinyreact.Element` classes and `Node.to_spec()` are removed; `Node` is the spec surface. Independent of #69; re-parenting `Node` onto `UiReact(UiComponent, AllowsChildren)` is tracked as a follow-up in `docs/todos.md`. Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-29-htmltools-spec-nesting-design.md`. New example: `examples/app-py/14-nesting`. ## Test Plan - [x] `make py-check` — ruff format + pyright (0 errors) + 90 pytest - [x] `cd js && npx vitest run` — 159 JS tests - [x] `make py-test-e2e` — 7 Playwright tests, incl. new `test_nesting.py` covering both the static-chrome inline-seed path and the reactive interleaved tree in a real browser - [x] `make update-dist` produces a clean working tree (committed bundles in sync)

title: fix(accordion): reject non-accordion_panel children with TypeError (#106)
description:
## Summary

Resolves #106. `accordion.tagify()` previously accessed `.title`, `.children`, `._value`, and `.icon` on every child, but `self.children: list[TagChild]` allows arbitrary values. Non-panel children (e.g. a bare string in the Express `with`-block displayhook path) produced a confusing `AttributeError` at render time, far from the call site that added the bad child.

This PR validates at three entry points and raises a clear `TypeError("accordion children must be accordion_panel instances, got <type>")`:

1. **`__init__`** — positional args (Core form).
2. **`append()`** — Express `with`-block displayhook path + direct calls. Preserves `Self` return type.
3. **`tagify()`** — defense in depth, catches direct `children` mutation.

A shared private `_check_panel(child)` helper keeps the message synchronized across all three sites. Removes four `# type: ignore[union-attr]` suppressions in each `tagify()`; one inline `cast("list[accordion_panel]", self.children)` replaces them on the comprehension iterable.

Applied identically to **`shinyui.accordion`** and **`shinyuiclassonly.accordion`** — both packages carried the same bug.

## Test Plan

- [x] `make py-check` clean (ruff, pyright 0 errors, 333 tests pass)
- [x] 6 new tests per package (12 total) covering: Core positional `__init__`, direct `append`, Express `with`-block displayhook path, `tagify` defense-in-depth, error-message type-name specificity, happy-path regression guard
- [x] All four `# type: ignore[union-attr]` suppressions removed from `tagify()` in both `_accordion.py` files (verified by grep)

## Design and plan

- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-26-accordion-child-validation-design.md`
- Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-26-accordion-child-validation.md`

title: fix: CtxTag.__exit__ propagates self to enclosing parent (#107)
description:
## Summary

- Fixes #107. `CtxTag.__exit__` now mirrors `AllowsChildren.__exit__`: on normal exit it calls `dispatch_to_active_parent(self)` so `with CtxTag(...)` nested inside an enclosing parent (an `AllowsChildren` component or another `CtxTag`) composes into the surrounding tree instead of silently orphaning itself and its children.
- Applied identically to `shinyui` and `shinyuiclassonly` (the two packages each ship a `CtxTag`).
- Adds 3 regression tests per package: dispatch into an `AllowsChildren` parent, dispatch into an enclosing `CtxTag`, and the `exc[0] is None` guard (no dispatch when the body raises).

### Why not inherit from `AllowsChildren`?

`AllowsChildren` is a mixin for the shinyui component classes (`card`, `accordion`, …) that are *not* `htmltools.Tag`s — its `children: list[TagChild]` and `__init__(*children, **kwargs)` would clash with `Tag`'s `TagList`-typed `children` and `(_name, *args, ...)` constructor, and with `Tag.append`'s child coercion that the displayhook shim depends on. Duplicating the four-line `__exit__` body is the cleaner fix; extracting a shared `_WithBlockChildCollector` mixin would be over-engineering for ~6 lines.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest pkg-py/tests/shinyui/test_ctx_stack.py pkg-py/tests/shinyuiclassonly/test_ctx_stack.py` — all 23 tests pass (6 new + 17 existing)
- [x] New tests verified to fail on `main` (without the `_ctx_tag.py` change): 4 of the 6 new tests fail pre-fix; the 2 exception-guard tests pass either way (they verify behavior only relevant once the fix is in)
- [x] `make py-check-tests` — 317 passing, 4 pre-existing failures (unrelated; same set fails on `main`)

title: fix: bump htmltools to >=0.7.0 and adapt to stricter Tagifiable protocol
description:
## Summary

- `make py-check` was failing on pyright after htmltools 0.7 split `Tag.tagify()` into a separate `TagifiedTag` return type and started enforcing the Tagifiable protocol at runtime (a child's `.tagify()` must return a fully-tagified value).
- Bump `htmltools>=0.7.0` and widen abstract `UiComponent.tagify` to return `Tagified` in both `shinyui` and `shinyuiclassonly`. Every component impl now chains `.tagify()` on its shiny.ui builder so children are resolved.
- `shinyui.render_plot.auto_output_ui` must keep returning `Tag` (covariance with `shiny.render.plot`), so it delegates directly to `shiny.ui.output_plot` rather than going through the wrapper class.
- Two tests updated to assert on `TagifiedTag` instead of `Tag`.

See #117 for discussion of the htmltools>=0.7 floor and downstream implications.

title: feat: shinyuiclassonly — class hierarchy without session machinery
description:
## Summary

Adds a sibling Python package `shinyuiclassonly` that ports the **class hierarchy** of `shinyui` while stripping all session-bound machinery. Plus two paired examples and CLAUDE.md updates.

The motivation is to let the team evaluate the class-per-component idea on two independent axes:

- **Structural** (the class hierarchy itself) — demonstrated by `shinyuiclassonly`.
- **Ergonomic** (session-bound `.value()` / `.update()` / `.click_value()` accessors) — demonstrated by `shinyui` only.

Reading `examples/16` against `examples/14` shows what disappears when the session-bound accessors are removed; reading `examples/16` against today's `ui.card()` shows what the class hierarchy alone buys you.

### What ships

- New package `pkg-py/src/shinyuiclassonly/` — 14 modules: `UiComponent`, `UiInput`/`UiOutput`/`UiLayout` role markers, `AllowsChildren` mixin, parent-tag context stack, `CtxTag`, and eight concrete components (`card`, `accordion`, `accordion_panel`, `input_slider`, `input_select`, `input_action_button`, `output_code`, `output_plot`, `render_plot`).
- Parallel test suite at `pkg-py/tests/shinyuiclassonly/` — 91 tests, no session fixtures.
- Two example apps: `examples/app-py/16-shinyuiclassonly-core/` (positional) and `examples/app-py/17-shinyuiclassonly-express/` (`with`-block), mirroring examples 14 / 15.
- CLAUDE.md updated with a "Sibling packages" section explaining when to use `shinyui` vs `shinyuiclassonly`.
- Design spec at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-19-shinyuiclassonly-design.md`, plan at `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-19-shinyuiclassonly.md`, decision notes at `decisions/2026-05-19-class-based-ui-type-system.md`.

### What's deliberately dropped vs `shinyui`

- No `_session` capture in `UiComponent.__init__`
- No `HasInputValue` mixin (no per-session id→instance registry, no input-handler `__init_subclass__` registration, no bookmark serializer)
- No `Updatable` ABC, no `.update()` methods on components
- No `reactive_calc_method`, no `.value()` / `.open_panels()` / `.full_screen_value()` / `.click_value()` accessors
- `render_plot` keeps `auto_output_ui()` (returns the `output_plot` instance, not `.tagify()`'d) but drops the derived-input accessors

Server code in the examples reads inputs via `input.<id>()` and pushes updates via `shiny.ui.update_*` — exactly like today.

## Test plan

- [x] `make py-check` clean (ruff format/lint, pyright, pytest)
- [x] 314 tests pass total — 91 new in `shinyuiclassonly/`, no regressions in `shinyreact/` or `shinyui/`
- [x] No `from shinyui` imports inside `pkg-py/src/shinyuiclassonly/` or the new examples
- [x] No session symbols leak into `shinyuiclassonly/` (verified via grep for `_session`, `HasInputValue`, `Updatable`, `reactive_calc_method`, `lookup_component`)
- [ ] Manual browser smoke run of `examples/app-py/16-shinyuiclassonly-core/app.py` and `examples/app-py/17-shinyuiclassonly-express/app.py` — sliders, accordion open/close, plot click/brush, action buttons

## Notes for reviewers

- The PR is large (~5,400 line insertions) but the per-file content is mostly mechanical: each concrete component is ~50–100 lines mirroring `shinyui`'s sibling minus the stripped machinery. The structure-only intent makes line-by-line review against `pkg-py/src/shinyui/` straightforward.
- `decisions/2026-05-19-class-based-ui-type-system.md` is the entry point if you want the "why bother" argument before the diff.
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-19-shinyuiclassonly-design.md` is the spec; it documents the "kept vs. dropped" table that drives every file in the new package.

title: feat: tag-as-context-manager for shinyui (#70)
description:
## Summary

Stage A of issue #70: makes `shinyui` `AllowsChildren` components (`card`, `accordion`, `accordion_panel`) and a new `shinyui.CtxTag` (a thin `htmltools.Tag` subclass) usable as Python context managers. The same shinyui class can now be composed both positionally (Shiny Core) and via `with`-blocks (Shiny Express / Jupyter / Quarto / REPL), producing identical UI trees.

```python
# Both produce the same DOM:
card(accordion(accordion_panel("A", input_slider("n", "N", 1, 10, 5)), id="acc"), id="m")

with card(id="m"):
    with accordion(id="acc"):
        with accordion_panel("A"):
            input_slider("n", "N", 1, 10, 5)
```

Bare strings (and any other `TagChild`) inside a `with`-block are coerced and captured too — `wrap_displayhook_handler` handles the type matrix:

```python
with card(id="m") as c:
    "Section title"              # plain string — captured as a text child
    input_slider("n", "N", 1, 10, 5)
    with accordion_panel("A"):
        "Panel intro paragraph"  # captured into the panel, not the card
        output_code("diag")

# c.children == ["Section title", <input_slider>, <accordion_panel "A">]
# panel.children == ["Panel intro paragraph", <output_code "diag">]
```

`None` and `...` are filtered out (per htmltools semantics); everything else routes to the nearest active parent.

**Mechanism:** lazily-installed `sys.displayhook` shim + per-task `contextvars.ContextVar` parent stack. `__enter__` pushes self; `__exit__` pops via `Token.reset` and auto-dispatches the just-closed component to the next outer parent on normal exit (this is what makes nested `with` blocks compose — `with X as y:` headers never trigger displayhook on their own). `wrap_displayhook_handler` from htmltools handles type coercion for strings, Tags, Tagifiables, etc.

**Scope:** Stage A prototype lives in `pkg-py/src/shinyui/`. Stage B (out of scope) ports `__enter__`/`__exit__` onto `htmltools.Tag` itself in py-htmltools. Co-exists cleanly with Shiny Express's `RecallContextManager` (function-call layer) — different surfaces, no interference.

Spec: [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-15-tag-context-manager-design.md`](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-15-tag-context-manager-design.md)
Plan: [`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-15-tag-context-manager.md`](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-15-tag-context-manager.md)
Issue: #70 (umbrella #68)

## Test plan

- [x] `make py-check` passes (ruff format + ruff lint + pyright + pytest: 144/144 shinyui tests, 219/219 across pkg-py).
- [x] `make js-lint` passes (no JS changes).
- [x] `pkg-py/tests/shinyui/test_ctx_stack.py` — stack push/pop, displayhook routing, fall-through, CtxTag (3), per-task isolation (asyncio), `@expressify` snapshot equivalence with positional form.
- [x] `pkg-py/tests/shinyui/test_allows_children.py` — collects via displayhook, nested `with`, sequential `with`, bare strings, `None`/Ellipsis filtering, exception-in-body still pops stack, pre-constructed component as CM (direct + `@expressify`), with-block appends to existing positional children (direct + `@expressify`), re-entering same instance keeps appending.
- [x] `examples/app-py/15-shinyui-with-blocks/app.py` starts cleanly in `shiny run` (smoke-tested) and mirrors `14-unified-ui-prototype/`'s tree in `with`-block form.
- [x] Autouse `_reset_ctx_stack` fixture in `pkg-py/tests/shinyui/conftest.py` isolates the contextvar between tests.

## Notes

- `UiComponent.__exit__` was a no-op while `__enter__` already delegated to `AllowsChildren.__enter__` via isinstance. This PR mirrors the delegation on `__exit__` (latent bug that would have caused stack leaks once `__enter__` became stateful).
- Spec was updated mid-implementation to document the `__exit__`-time auto-dispatch (Stage A discovered that without it, nested `with` blocks would silently drop the inner component).

title: feat: shinyui prototype — class-per-component UI hierarchy (#69)
description:
Closes #69 (Stage A only). Builds the class-per-component prototype the
umbrella spec (#68) called for, in a new sibling package `shinyui` next
to `shinyreact`. Design and plan live under `docs/superpowers/`.

## Summary

- **New package `pkg-py/src/shinyui/`** depends only on `shiny + htmltools`
  (no `shinyreact` import), so the eventual Stage B port into `py-shiny`
  is a near-mechanical copy.
- **Hierarchy:** three semantic role bases (`UiInput` / `UiOutput` /
  `UiLayout`) plus three orthogonal mixins (`HasInputValue`, `Updatable`,
  `AllowsChildren`). Replaces the umbrella's straddler model — a card
  with a full-screen toggle reads cleanly as `UiLayout + HasInputValue`
  instead of awkwardly inheriting from `UiInput`.
- **Eight concrete classes** in snake_case (matching `shiny.render.data_frame`):
  `input_slider`, `input_select`, `input_action_button`, `output_code`,
  `output_plot`, `card`, `accordion`, `accordion_panel`. The class IS the
  call site — no parallel factory functions.
- **Single source of session truth** on `UiComponent`: `_session` captured
  at `__init__`, `_require_session(for_op=...)` resolves at call time with
  a fallback, `_read_input(suffix)` powers every accessor.
- **Server-side read accessors** as `@reactive_calc_method`-wrapped
  methods (mirrors `@render.data_frame`'s `df.cell_selection()` pattern):
  `slider.value()`, `card.full_screen_value()`, `accordion.open_panels()`,
  `plot.click_value()`, `btn.clicked()`, etc.
- **Typed `.update()`** per class — no `session=` kwarg; init captures,
  call-time falls back. `UiInputActionButton` demonstrates
  `__init_subclass__` handler-registration on `HasInputValue` (most
  classes leave the default `None` handler, so the hook is a no-op for them).
- **Express/Core overloads** on container classes (`card`, `accordion`,
  `accordion_panel`): Express overload first (no positional children, for
  `with X(...) as x:` blocks), Core overload second (positional children
  for inline construction).
- **126 tests** across 16 test files: per-class snapshots vs `shiny.ui.*`,
  cross-cutting MRO / handler-registration / update-resolution /
  read-accessor / `AllowsChildren` behaviour, bookmark id→instance
  round-trip, public exports.
- **Working end-to-end Express demo** at `examples/app-py/14-unified-ui-prototype/`
  exercising every class. Real matplotlib scatter driven by slider/select/seed
  reads; Open all / Close all buttons fire `accordion.update()`; plot
  click/brush populate the diagnostics panel.
- Spec & plan checked in under `docs/superpowers/specs/` and
  `docs/superpowers/plans/`.

## Notable design refinements

1. `UiAccordion` ships **no** custom input handler — shiny's accordion
   binding pushes a plain JSON list, so the accessor coerces list→tuple
   at read time.
2. `UiInputSelect.update()` delegates to `shiny.ui.update_select` rather
   than hand-rolling the payload — reuses shiny's choice-rendering pipeline.
3. `UiAccordionPanel.tagify()` returns `AccordionPanel` (not `Tag`) so
   the outer accordion's `isinstance(panel, AccordionPanel)` check passes.
   Documented inline.
4. `UiCard.full_screen_value()` reads `input.<id>_full_screen` (the
   actual wire suffix shiny pushes), not `input.<id>()` as the spec
   originally indicated. Browser-side `update()` wiring for full-screen
   remains Stage B work.
5. `_deep_tagify` helper that I'd added briefly was removed — single
   `.tagify()` on the outer tag iterates Tagifiable→Tagifiable chains
   inside htmltools' walker, so it's enough. Accordion still pre-tagifies
   panels because of the isinstance check.
6. `reactive_calc_method` cache is keyed by `(instance, session)` —
   without that, module-level components reused across sessions hit
   `DestroyedReactiveError` on session #2 and the browser went grey.

## Test plan

- [x] `make py-check` is green (126 tests, ruff clean, pyright 0 errors)
- [x] Snapshot tests confirm `tagify()` matches `shiny.ui.*` markup byte-for-byte
- [x] Bookmark id→instance registration works under a mocked session
- [x] `.update()` outside a session raises with class name + method name in message
- [x] Read accessors raise outside a session
- [x] `with card(...): ...` returns `self`; `with input_slider(...):` raises `TypeError`
- [x] `__init_subclass__` auto-registers `UiInputActionButton`'s `shinyui.action` handler
- [x] Express example app renders end-to-end (verified in browser via Playwright):
  inputs drive the scatter plot, Open/Close buttons fire `accordion.update()`,
  plot click/brush populate the diagnostics panel

## Out of scope (intentionally deferred)

- Stage B port into `py-shiny` (separate issue when this prototype is accepted)
- Tag-as-context-manager / parent-tag stack (umbrella sub-issue 3)
- Browser-side JS for `card.update(full_screen=True)` to actually flip the card

title: feat(js): `type=` option on useShinyInput / useSetShinyInput (#97)

## Summary

Resolves #97. Adds an optional `type?: string` to `useShinyInput` and `useSetShinyInput` that routes values through Shiny's server-side input handlers via the `id:type` wire convention:

```ts
const [when, setWhen] = useShinyInput<number>("when", 0, { type: "shiny.datetime" });
// server: input.when() is a datetime.datetime, not a number
```

- `InputRegistryEntry` gains a private `type` field + `updateType()` method. First-writer-wins: the first mount finalizes the policy; later mounts disagreeing throw. Validation rejects empty/whitespace/`:` strings at hook mount.
- Read hooks (`useShinyInputValue`, `useShinyOutputValue`, `useShinyOutputStatus`) are untouched — input handlers fire on the write path only.
- Example: `examples/ui-tsx/08-input-handler/` demonstrates the `shiny.datetime` round trip.
- Playwright e2e proves the suffix survives the wire and the handler runs.

Design doc: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-13-input-handler-type-design.md`. Implementation plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-13-input-handler-type.md`.

title: fix(js): ShinyOutput honors ShinyModuleProvider namespace (#90)
description:
Closes #90.

## Summary

- `ShinyOutput` was the lone consumer of `id` that did not apply the namespace from `ShinyModuleProvider`. Hooks (`useShinyInput`, `useShinyOutputValue`, …) all do, so a module like `<ShinyModuleProvider namespace="a"><ShinyOutput id="scatter"/></ShinyModuleProvider>` rendered `<div id="scatter">` while the server emitted values for `a-scatter` — the binding could not connect, and sibling providers produced duplicate DOM ids.
- The component now reads the context via `useShinyModuleNamespace()` and applies it through `applyNamespace()`, mirroring the hook contract. A new optional `namespace?: string | null` prop follows the same precedence: explicit > context, `null` opts out.
- `bindAll` / `unbindAll` now key on the resolved namespaced id, and the error log reports it — matches what hits the DOM.
- **`ImageOutput` realigned to the same contract.** It used `??` for namespace precedence, which conflates `null` with `undefined` — `namespace={null}` silently fell through to the context instead of opting out. Switched to `!== undefined` so all three APIs (hooks, `ShinyOutput`, `ImageOutput`) agree.

## Test plan

- [x] 7 new unit tests in `js/src/__tests__/shiny-output.test.tsx` covering: bare id (no context), context applied, sibling providers produce distinct DOM ids, explicit prop overrides context, `namespace={null}` suppresses context, re-bind on namespace change, error log uses the namespaced id.
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 150/150 pass.
- [x] `make js-lint` — clean.
- [x] `make py-test-e2e` — 5/5 pass (no regression in existing fixtures).
- [x] `make py-check` — 75/75 pass.
- [x] CI green.

title: fix(py): cache-bust shinyreact.js via mtime version (#84)
description:
## Summary

- **#84 (fix):** Browsers cached `shinyreact.js` across rebuilds because the `HTMLDependency` was pinned at `version="0.1.0"`. Stamp the version with the bundle's mtime so `make update-dist` cache-busts automatically. Introduces `_file_mtime_int(path)` and reuses it in `page_react_dep` for consistency.
- **#82 (won't-fix):** The originally proposed stat-cache for `www/index.html` is reverted — it didn't actually work. Shiny Express's `_run.py` invokes the `page_fn` once at app startup and caches the rendered bytes as `app_ui`; subsequent HTTP requests serve the cached bytes verbatim. A re-read inside the closure is unreachable on those requests. The only knob today that flips Express into a per-request `app_ui` is `app_opts(bookmark_store=...)`, which would force the bookmarking subsystem on every `set_react_page` user — too invasive for an unrelated reason. An inline comment near the read in `_build_react_page_fn` points to #82 and lays out the upstream constraint for a future maintainer. Issue #82 is closed as "won't fix" — the only real fix lives upstream in py-shiny.

Closes #84. Closes #82 (won't fix).

title: feat(bookmark): restore inputs from URL/server bookmarks
description:
Closes #27.

## Summary

Implements bookmark restoration for shinyreact. URL-encoded (`?_inputs_&...`) and server-stored (`?_state_id_=...`) bookmarks both flow through the same mechanism: a head `<script>` set on `window.shinyreact._restore`, then batch-applied to the input registry by the bundle on init. `useShinyInput`'s existing registry-first lookup picks up the restored value as the initial render value — no hook changes.

Both shinyreact patterns are covered:
- **`app.py`** (`page_react`)
- **`ui.tsx`** (`set_react_page`)

`ui_output()` is intentionally unchanged — bookmark restoration is page-level, not per-output.

## Architecture

**Python** (`pkg-py/src/shinyreact/`):
- `_bookmark.py` (new) — `_read_restore_input_values()` reads `RestoreContext.input.as_dict()` without consuming pending state; `_restore_script_tag()` returns a head-injected `<script>` (`htmltools.head_content`) carrying the values, with `</` escaped so it cannot terminate the surrounding tag.
- `_output.py` — `_dep()` unchanged; new `_dep_page()` wraps it with the optional restore script.
- `_page.py` — `page_react` and `_build_react_page_fn` switch to `_dep_page()`. `page_bare` and `ui_output` are unchanged.

**JS** (`js/src/`):
- `shiny-react/bookmark.ts` (new) — `applyRestoredValues(registry)` reads `window.shinyreact._restore`, batch-seeds entries via `registry.add()` (no Shiny call), replaces the global with `{ "-applied": true, "-values": <appliedMap> }`. Idempotent.
- `shiny-react/use-shiny.ts` — wired into `ensureShinyReactInitialized()` between `initializeReactRegistry()` and `createReactOutputBinding()`.
- `index.ts` — `window.shinyreact = Object.assign(window.shinyreact || {}, { ... })` so the bundle preserves any `_restore` set by the head script.

The defer-vs-non-defer distinction (head script is non-defer, bundle is `defer`) guarantees the global is set before the bundle's IIFE runs.

## Sentinel keys: `-applied` / `-values`

Post-init, `window.shinyreact._restore` becomes `{ "-applied": true, "-values": <appliedMap> }`. The leading `-` cannot be a Shiny input id, so the metadata keys cannot collide. `-values` is debugging metadata for DevTools; `_restore` itself is documented internal.

## Security

Bookmarked input values appear in the rendered HTML page source. URL mode: already in the URL, no added exposure. Server-stored mode: URL hides values, but the script tag re-exposes them — anything that can read the HTML (browser extensions, logging proxies, view-source) can read these values. Apps must not place credentials, tokens, or PII into bookmarked inputs. Comment is co-located at the emission site, the apply site, and the example README.

## Tests

| Layer | Count |
|---|---|
| Python unit tests (`pkg-py/tests/test_bookmark_restore.py`) | 18 |
| JS unit tests (`use-shiny-restore.test.tsx`) | 9 |
| Playwright integration (`pkg-py/tests/playwright/`) | 2 + 1 skipped |
| Live curl smoke against `examples/app-py/13-bookmarking/` | ✓ |

`make py-check` runs the Python suite (excluding Playwright). New `make py-test-e2e` target runs the integration suite separately — `pytest-playwright` leaves the asyncio loop in a state that confused unit tests collected after it.

## Public example

`examples/app-py/13-bookmarking/` — text/number/checkbox inputs + bookmark button. Try:

```
shiny run examples/app-py/13-bookmarking/app.py
```

Edit inputs, click **Bookmark**, copy the URL into a new tab — inputs initialise from the URL.

## Spec / plan

- Spec: \`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-08-bookmarking-restoration-design.md\`
- Plan: \`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-08-bookmarking-restoration.md\`

## Out of scope (explicit)

- **No save side helper** (\`useShinyBookmark()\` etc.). Apps still trigger \`session.bookmark()\` themselves.
- **No custom-value channel** (\`RestoreContext.values\`).
- **No \`ui.tsx\` example** — design covers it; example deferred unless docs need it.
- **Server-mode Playwright round-trip** is skipped pending a fixture that supports per-test \`bookmark_store=\` override.

## Test plan

- [x] \`make py-check\` (71 tests)
- [x] \`make js-lint && cd js && npx vitest run\` (137 tests)
- [x] \`make py-test-e2e\` (2 + 1 skipped)
- [x] Open the example, change inputs, click Bookmark, paste URL into a new tab — inputs match

title: fix: handle bindAll/unbindAll errors in ShinyOutput
description:
## Summary

Resolves #56 (policy) and closes #60 (implementation). `ShinyOutput`'s effect now wraps `Shiny.bindAll`/`unbindAll` in `try/catch` (sync) and `.catch()` (async), so a binding failure logs to `console.error` with structured context and the component stays mounted — a single broken output no longer takes down siblings or the surrounding tree.

description:
Closes #76.

The `GIT_VERSION` marker files in `pkg-py/src/shinyreact/www/` and `pkg-r/inst/lib/shiny/` were never read by anything, caused merge conflicts on every dist-touching PR, and blocked self-verifying CI (rebuilding always rewrote the SHA so a `git status` check would always fail).

Path triggers were extended to the package dist directories so direct edits there also fire the workflow.

title: feat(hooks)!: Jotai-style hook decomposition (#49)
description:
## Summary

Implements [#49](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinyreact/issues/49) and refines the API surface to a single-responsibility, Jotai/Recoil-style decomposition. See the [proposal comment on #49](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinyreact/issues/49#issuecomment-4407762606) for the design discussion.

|  | Full | Read-only | Write-only |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Input** | `useShinyInput(id, default)` → `[value, setValue]` | `useShinyInputValue(id)` → `value` | **`useSetShinyInput(id, default)`** → `setValue` (NEW) |
| **Output** | — | **`useShinyOutputValue(id, default?)`** → `value` (NEW) | — |
| **Output status** | | **`useShinyOutputStatus(id)`** → `OutputStatus` (NEW) | |

`useShinyOutput` is **removed**. Each hook now does exactly one thing — no compound returns.

## Migration

```jsx
// before
const [v, recalculating] = useShinyOutput(id, default);

// after — each call site picks what it actually needs
const v = useShinyOutputValue(id, default);
// and/or
const status = useShinyOutputStatus(id);
const recalculating = status === "recalculating";
```

Callers that only destructured `[value]` go from `const [v] = useShinyOutput(...)` → `const v = useShinyOutputValue(...)`.

The removal is intentional. An interim version of this PR changed `useShinyOutput`'s tuple from `[value, boolean]` to `[value, OutputStatus string]`, but every status string is truthy — so `if (recalculating)` checks kept compiling and stayed permanently true (real instance caught in `examples/app-py/06-dashboard/dashboard.js`). The hard removal forces a conscious choice at every call site.

Migrated in this PR:
- All 19 example files (ui-tsx + app-py)
- Internal `ImageOutput.tsx`
- Live docs (CLAUDE.md, README.md, DESIGN.md, features.md, app-py-vs-ui-tsx.md, todos.md, timeline.md)

## Underlying mechanics

- `InputRegistry.subscribe()` with a pending-subscribers map — consumers attach to existing entries or queue and resume when the producer registers. Mount-order safe.
- `OutputRegistryEntry` lifecycle state machine: `pending` → `ready` → `recalculating` → `error`, with idempotent `setStatus`, dedicated error fan-out, and `setValue` clearing prior error subscribers. `renderError` no longer poisons the value channel with a `__error` sentinel.
- The `useShinyOutputValue` and `useShinyOutputStatus` hooks subscribe via the same `OutputRegistry.add(setValue, setStatus, setError)` triple, but pass a stable noop for channels they don't observe — so a value-only consumer doesn't re-render when status changes, and vice versa.

## Example showcase: `examples/app-py/06-dashboard`

Three polish fixes on the dashboard demo, all enabled by this PR:

1. **Period-switch flicker eliminated.** Pre-fix, every period change destroyed and re-mounted the chart and table DOM (54 mutations per click → brief skeleton flash). Now the chart card stays mounted; `status === "recalculating"` adds a `.recalculating { opacity: 0.6 }` cue. Mutations dropped from **54 → 16**, and the 16 are React reconciling a genuinely smaller dataset (15 → 7 bars).
2. **Top Products + Category Performance now react to date changes.** Previously the table and category bars were derived from a static 20-row aggregate with no date dimension; the date filter did nothing for two of three cards. Replaced the static aggregate with a long-format `transactions` fact table (365 days × 20 products = 7,300 rows) and an aggregation pipeline in `filter_data`. Top product reshuffles between periods (Novel → Laptop Stand → Novel across 30/90/365 day windows).
3. **Bar-chart bottom alignment.** The previous `.bar-col` flex layout depended on label rendered height — varied 13/14px due to per-glyph ascender differences. Now labels are absolutely positioned and bar bottoms sit at a fixed offset; spread went from 2px → 0px.

## CLAUDE.md additions

Three new "Common patterns" subsections capturing lessons from this work:

- **Hook decomposition** — the table above plus guidance on picking the narrowest hook.
- **Avoiding flicker on input changes** — the wrong vs. right pattern, drawn from the dashboard fix.
- **Server pattern: fact table + shared `@reactive.calc` + per-output aggregations** — three-step recipe drawn from the data.py rewrite.

title: fix: ShinyOutput renders without wrapper div (#61)
description:
Closes #61.

## Summary
- Removed the `<div ref={ref}>` wrapper from `ShinyOutput` so the rendered element is a *direct* child of its parent. Flex `gap`, grid layouts, and `> *` selectors now work as the caller expects.
- `ref` goes onto the rendered element itself; `tagName` defaults to `"div"`.

## Binding scope (intentionally asymmetric)
- **`bindAll(el.parentElement)`** — Shiny's output bindings call `$(scope).find(selector)`, which is descendants-only. Binding `el` directly would silently no-op for non-custom-element outputs (e.g. `plotly-output`, htmlwidgets). Passing the parent guarantees our element is found. Re-binding is safe: Shiny skips already-bound siblings.
- **`unbindAll(el, true)`** — `unbindAll(parent)` would clobber sibling outputs. `includeSelf=true` scopes the unbind to just this element.

The component-level docblock explains this asymmetry so the next reader doesn't "simplify" it.

## Test plan

  - `renders without a wrapper element`
  - `preserves CSS layout for direct children (flexbox/grid)`
  - `binds with the parent as scope so descendants-only find() locates the element`
  - `unbinds only the element itself (includeSelf=true), not the whole parent`

title: refactor: share Shiny lifecycle state via a single external store
description:
Closes #39

## Summary

`useShinyInitialized()` and `useShinyBusy()` previously each ran their own `useState` + `useEffect`, so every consumer installed its own DOM listeners and held its own copy of state that is really runtime-global. On a page with many Shiny-integrated components this meant N duplicate `shiny:busy` / `shiny:idle` listeners and N redundant state writes per event.

This PR introduces a small singleton at `js/src/shiny-react/lifecycle-store.ts` and rewrites both hooks as one-line `useSyncExternalStore` reads. Public hook signatures are unchanged.

Key design decisions:

- **Lazy-and-permanent subscription.** DOM listeners install on the first `subscribe` call and never tear down. The state belongs to the page, not to any one React tree, so there is nothing to clean up on unmount and nothing to re-subscribe under StrictMode.
- **Disjoint snapshots.** Each hook subscribes through `useSyncExternalStore` with its own primitive selector (`getInitializedSnapshot` / `getBusySnapshot`). `useShinyInitialized` consumers do not re-render on `busy`/`idle` and vice versa.
- **Seeds `busy` from the DOM.** On first mount we read `document.documentElement.classList.contains("shiny-busy")` so a consumer that mounts mid-request sees the correct value instead of a stale `false`.
- **Scope is documented.** A header comment in `lifecycle-store.ts` explicitly limits this pattern to runtime-global state and warns against folding the id-scoped hooks (`useShinyInput` / `useShinyOutput` / `useShinyMessageHandler`) into the store — those already share state through their own id-keyed registries.

A test-only `__resetLifecycleStoreForTests` helper lets the existing test files exercise the singleton cleanly between cases.

## Verification

`make js-lint` is clean and `cd js && npx vitest run` reports `Test Files 10 passed (10) / Tests 83 passed (83)`. `make update-dist` rebuilt the JS bundle and copied it into `pkg-py/` and `pkg-r/`.

The two updated test files cover the new behavior:

- `use-shiny-initialized.test.tsx` adds a "consumer mounts after init returns true on first render" case.
- `use-shiny-busy.test.tsx` adds a "seeds \`busy=true\` from \`.shiny-busy\`" case and a "shares one DOM subscription across many consumers" case that asserts exactly one `addEventListener` call per event regardless of consumer count.

title: feat: replace ReactApp with Express-only set_page()
description:
## Summary

Replace the `ReactApp` Shiny Core class with `set_page()`, a Shiny Express helper that configures the app to serve a static `www/index.html` alongside reactive computation.

This was previously bundled with `ShinyOutput` support — that piece is split into #67 (stacked on this PR).

## Why Express-only?

The old `ReactApp` (formerly `SpaApp`) pattern used a Shiny Core server function. Renderers are created inside that function per-session — they don't exist at app construction time. This made it impossible to automatically discover what dependencies the page needs, forcing users into manual wiring:

```python
# Before: manual deps, private imports
from shiny.ui._html_deps_py_shiny import data_frame_deps
app = ReactApp(server, deps=[data_frame_deps()])
```

In Express, renderers are declared at the top level and exist before the page is assembled. This unlocks automatic dependency discovery — every renderer has `auto_output_ui()` which returns a Tag with its required HTMLDependencies. We just iterate them and inject the deps into the page.

## Result

A much simpler app file with zero-config dependencies:

```python
from shiny.express import input, render
from shinyreact import reactive_output, set_page

set_page()

@reactive_output
def greeting():
    return f"Showing {input.row_count()} rows"

@render.data_frame
def my_table():
    return df
```

`set_page()` uses Express's `page_opts(page_fn=...)` to provide a custom page function that reads `www/index.html`, collects deps from all renderers, and assembles the final page. No manual dependency wiring needed.

## What falls out

- **Zero-config dependencies.** `@render.data_frame`, `@render_plotly`, and anything else with `auto_output_ui()` just works — their JS/CSS is loaded automatically.
- **No server function boilerplate.** The `def server(input, output, session)` wrapper disappears.

## What breaks

- `ReactApp` is removed. The class file (`_react_app.py`) and tests are deleted.

## Open questions

- Does the Express-only direction concern you?
- Naming: `set_page()`?

## Test plan

- [x] `make py-check` — 46 tests pass, 0 type errors
- [x] `pkg-py/tests/test_set_page.py` covers: dep injection, renderer dep auto-discovery, reading `www/index.html`, custom path
- [ ] Verify a real Express app boots end-to-end (will be exercised in #67's examples)

title: feat: add ShinyOutput component for embedding traditional output bindings
description:
## Summary

Add `<ShinyOutput>` — a React component that renders an opaque container and runs `Shiny.bindAll`/`Shiny.unbindAll` on mount/unmount, letting existing Shiny output bindings (`@render.data_frame`, `@render_plotly`, htmlwidgets-style outputs, etc.) be embedded inside a `ui.tsx` React app.

Stacked on #53 (Express-only `set_react_page()`). Examples 06/07 use both pieces, but `ShinyOutput` itself works in any shinyreact context.

Closes #58, #62, #63, #66.

## Motivation

Today shinyreact's `ui.tsx` pattern only supports `@reactive_output` — server sends pure JSON, React renders. That's the right default but means existing Shiny output bindings can't be reused without rewriting them as React components — a significant adoption barrier.

`<ShinyOutput>` is the escape hatch:

```js
h(ShinyOutput, { id: "my_table", tagName: "shiny-data-frame" })
h(ShinyOutput, { id: "scatter", className: "shiny-ipywidget-output shiny-report-size" })
```

The `tagName` prop handles custom elements (like `<shiny-data-frame>`) where the binding is registered on the element itself rather than discovered by CSS class.

## What's included

- `js/src/shiny-output.tsx` — the component (~30 lines, `bindAll`/`unbindAll` on mount/unmount, re-binds on `id`/`tagName` change)
- `js/src/__tests__/shiny-output.test.tsx` — unit tests (rendering, lifecycle, no-op when Shiny absent, re-bind on prop change)
- Exposed on `window.shinyreact.ShinyOutput`
- **Example 06 (`@render.data_frame`)** — `shiny-data-frame` web component embedded in a `ui.tsx` Express app
- **Example 07 (`@render_plotly`)** — plotly via `shinywidgets` embedded in a `ui.tsx` Express app
- `pyproject.toml`: adds `shinywidgets` and `plotly` as dev deps for example 07
- `docs/features.md` / `docs/todos.md` / `docs/app-py-vs-ui-tsx.md` — JS bridge hooks row, example rows, "two output paradigms within a `ui.tsx` app" section

## Terminology

This branch also locks in the team-final naming for the two patterns. **`SPA` and `traditional` are gone** as labels; the canonical pair anchors on the entry filenames the author edits:

- **`app.py`** (or **`app.py`/`app.R`** when cross-language matters) — UI defined as Python or R objects in the Shiny app file via `page_react()` + `Spec`/`Element`/`Node`.
- **`ui.tsx`** — UI defined in a React client codebase whose entry conventionally lives in `ui.tsx`. `ui.tsx` is the *idiomatic canonical name* — examples may use simpler variants like `www/app.js` (no-build) or `src/App.jsx` (Vite + JSX). Treat `ui.tsx` as a *role label* for the React entry, not a strict file requirement.

Naming inspired by [Shiny's "Build your entire UI with HTML"](https://shiny.posit.co/r/articles/build/html-ui/) (UI object vs HTML UI), reframed around the canonical entry filenames the team actually edits. The phrase "traditional Shiny" (vanilla Shiny, no shinyreact) remains acceptable — only the *pattern label* changes.

Directories renamed: `examples/spa/` → `examples/ui-tsx/`; `examples/traditional/` → `examples/app-py/`. Doc renamed: `docs/spa-vs-traditional.md` → `docs/app-py-vs-ui-tsx.md`. Internal helper: `_build_spa_page_fn` → `_build_react_page_fn`.

## Issues closed

- **#58** — `useEffect` deps now track `[id, tagName]` so prop changes properly unbind/rebind; tests added for both transitions and remount.
- **#62** — `cast(Tag, TagList(...))` in `_page.py` is annotated with a comment explaining the `page_opts` type signature mismatch (`Tag` vs `TagList`); kept as-is since `TagList` works at runtime.
- **#63** — `inspect.stack()` replaced with `sys._getframe(1)` (cheaper, immune to wrapper depth); early `FileNotFoundError` added in `_build_react_page_fn`.
- **#66** — rationale; `ShinyOutput` ships, examples 06/07 demonstrate both renderers, and `docs/app-py-vs-ui-tsx.md` documents the two output paradigms within a `ui.tsx` app.

## Open questions

- Do we provide subclasses for known/popular bindings (e.g. `<DataFrameOutput>`, `<PlotlyOutput>`)?
- Do we need a language-specific subclass for `HtmlWidget`? Python's shinywidgets makes this "just work" — R may need more hand-holding (DOM classes etc.).
- Should `ShinyOutput` warn / error when used with a renderer it could trivially replace (e.g. `@render.text`)?

## Test plan

- [x] `make py-check` — 50 tests pass, 0 type errors, ruff clean
- [x] `cd js && npx vitest run` — 80 tests pass
- [x] JS lint clean
- [x] All 7 `ui.tsx` example apps reach `set_react_page()` cleanly under `uv run --group examples`
- [x] Verify example 06 renders a sortable data frame in browser (verified via Playwright — sortable header active, server-side `Showing 5 rows` greeting reflects slider)
- [x] Verify example 07 renders an interactive plotly scatter in browser (verified via Playwright — full plotly toolbar, 50 scattered points, server-side `Showing 50 random points` greeting)

description:
## Summary

- Replaces `js_file`/`css_file` string params on `page_react()` with HTMLDependency support via `*args` (Shiny hoists them to `<head>` automatically)
- Adds `page_react_dep()` helper that builds an HTMLDependency from local file paths with mtime-based cache-busting

## Design

Spec at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-15-page-react-htmldep-design.md`.

Key insight from brainstorming: Shiny's HTMLDependency is a `MetadataNode` subclass that gets hoisted to `<head>` automatically regardless of where it appears in the tag tree. So no separate `deps` kwarg is needed — passing them as `*args` is sufficient and self-documenting.

Vite lib-mode IIFE; React externalized to `window.shinyjson` so the bundle reuses the page's React instance. - **16-shadcn** — full port of [`wch/shiny-react/examples/5-shadcn`](https://github.com/wch/shiny-react/tree/main/examples/5-shadcn): TextInputCard, ButtonEventCard, PlotCard (matplotlib via `@render.plot` + ``), plus a client-side **PlotlyCard** rendering the same data with `plotly.js` and a **PlotlyInfoCard** demonstrating that `useShinyInput`'s "set a value" and "read the local state" modes are the same hook. Continuous hover, click-anywhere, drag-to-select-and-zoom, Esc/double-click reset gestures. ### Fixes - **`fix: ImageOutput sends initial dimensions before first image arrives`**. The `MISSING` sentinel commit (`0deddb4` on main) introduced a chicken-and-egg bug: `` only renders after `imgData` arrives, but `imgData` only arrives after the server sees dimensions, which only get sent by the `ResizeObserver` on the `` element. Pre-existing — examples 5 and 16 were both broken before this PR. - **`fix: refresh both shinyjson packages in update-dist`**. `make update-dist` only refreshed the new package's `www/`, so `shinyjsonold` would silently drift on the next JS rebuild. - **`fix: define process.env.NODE_ENV for Vite lib build`**. Lib mode doesn't auto-replace it; without the define the bundled React jsx-runtime hits a `ReferenceError: process is not defined`. ### Documentation - README files for every example (1–16 plus `hello-shinyjson`). Each is short and consistent: what's demonstrated, where the bridge primitives live, the run command, and a pointer to the modern equivalent where one exists. - `docs/STATUS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` updated to describe the parallel packages. ## Test plan - [x] `make py-check` passes (49 tests, 0 pyright errors, ruff clean). - [x] `make js-test` passes (67 JS tests). - [ ] `import shinyjson, shinyjsonold` both succeed; `shinyjson.__all__ == ['SpaApp', 'render_json', 'send_json']`. - [ ] `uv run shiny run examples/13-spa-hello/app.py` — type a name + click; client and server cards both update (server with a websocket-roundtrip lag). - [ ] `uv run shiny run examples/14-columns-new-spa/app.py` — items move between columns via ←/→ buttons. - [ ] `cd examples/15-columns-shadcn && npm install && npm run build && cd ../.. && uv run shiny run examples/15-columns-shadcn/app.py` — same drag demo with shadcn Card/Button. - [ ] `cd examples/16-shadcn && npm install && npm run build && cd ../.. && uv run shiny run examples/16-shadcn/app.py` — text input round-trips, "Send Event" button triggers server timestamp, **both** plot cards render (matplotlib PNG + plotly.js scatter), the interaction info card updates continuously on hover/click/select, and Esc + double-click reset the zoomed view. - [ ] All legacy examples (1–12 + hello-shinyjson) still run with `shinyjsonold` and behave as before.

title: docs: add playwright testing architecture decision
description:
## Summary

Adds an architectural decision document exploring how to add Playwright-based end-to-end testing to shinyjson. Evaluates four approaches for implementing TypeScript-first test controllers (similar to `shiny.playwright.controllers`) that can be consumed by Python and R:

1. **Node.js Bridge (RPC)** — rejected due to two-process coordination overhead
2. **Shell Out to TS Test Runner** — rejected due to inability to interleave server + browser assertions
3. **Browser-Native Assertion Library** — rejected due to flaky test risk from reimplementing Playwright's expect
4. **Code Generation from TS to Python/R** — recommended: real Playwright expect in every language, single process at runtime, native pytest/testthat integration

Key finding: Playwright's `expect()` and actionability checks run in the host process (Node.js/Python), not in the browser, which eliminates in-browser assertion approaches.

Open questions remain around the code-gen mechanism (schema-driven vs AST parsing vs manual conventions) and R Playwright bindings.

## Verification

Review the decision document at `decisions/2026-03-17-playwright-testing-architecture.md`.

title: fix: write the bookmark URL to the address bar instead of a Bootstrap modal
description:
Fixes [posit-dev/shinyreact#326](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinyreact/issues/326).

Shiny's default `onBookmarked` / `on_bookmarked` action shows the URL in a Bootstrap modal. `page_react()` loads no Bootstrap, so `session$doBookmark()` / `session.bookmark()` threw `$(...).modal is not a function` and the URL was never shown or updated.

The per-session `shinyreact.init` handler (R and Python) now registers a default `onBookmarked` callback that writes the URL to the address bar (`updateQueryString()` / `update_query_string()`).

Shiny only runs its own default when no callback is registered, and runs every callback otherwise. So this callback only acts while it is the only one. If the app registers its own `onBookmarked()`, the app's callback alone decides what happens, just as it would replace Shiny's default. Counting callbacks reads a private field in both languages (`private$bookmarkedCallbacks` / `_on_bookmarked_callbacks`), since neither has a public way to count them.

This also applies to a `page_react_html()` document that loads Bootstrap itself, so those apps get the address-bar behavior instead of the modal too.

Checked by hand with the issue's R repro and a Python `ReactApp(bookmark_store="url")` app: clicking Bookmark updates the URL with no error.

title: feat(js): add useShinyConnected(); hear Shiny's jQuery lifecycle events
description:
Fixes [posit-dev/shinyreact#328](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinyreact/issues/328).

Root cause: Shiny fires `shiny:connected`, `shiny:disconnected`, `shiny:busy`, and `shiny:idle` with jQuery's `trigger()`. That only calls jQuery handlers; `document.addEventListener()` never sees them. The lifecycle store listened with `addEventListener()`, so:

- there was no way to see a disconnect (the issue), and
- `useShinyBusy()` never updated in a real browser either. Its unit tests passed because they send native events.

Changes:

- A small `onShinyEvent()` helper listens through `window.jQuery(document).on()` when jQuery is on the page, and falls back to `addEventListener()` otherwise. jQuery handlers also get native events, so the jsdom tests still work.
- The lifecycle store and the dependency-discovery `shiny:connected` wait both use it.
- New `useShinyConnected()` hook: `false` until the socket opens, `false` again on disconnect, `true` again if Shiny reconnects. It seeds from `Shiny.shinyapp.isConnected()` for late mounts. `useShinyInitialized()` is unchanged (it stays `true`).
- The hook is exported on `window.shinyreact` and the npm entry, and taught in the `shinyreact-build-app` skill.

Checked by hand in a browser with an R app: "Busy" now shows during a slow request, and stopping the R process flips the hook to `false`.

title: fix(js): ImageOutput shows errors and uses the renderer's alt text
description: Fixes [posit-dev/shinyreact#327](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinyreact/issues/327). - When the render function errors, `` now hides the last image and shows the error message, like a regular `plotOutput()`. The message div gets the same classes Shiny's `renderError()` adds (`shiny-output-error`, `shiny-output-error-`), so Shiny's own CSS styles it. The image comes back when a value arrives again. - The `` `alt` now comes from `renderPlot(alt =)` / `@render.plot(alt=)` instead of a hardcoded `""`. R sends a one-class error `type` as a plain string rather than an array, so the class list handles both shapes, the same way Shiny's `asArray()` does. Silent errors (`req()`) still show the loading placeholder, since they arrive as a `null` value, not an error.

title: fix(js): type useShinyOutputValue() as T | null | undefined; export styles.css
description:
Fixes [posit-dev/shinyreact#329](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinyreact/issues/329).

A server `NULL` / `None` reaches the client as `null`, but `useShinyOutputValue()` was typed `T | undefined`. Code that checked `x !== undefined` passed the type checker and then crashed at runtime. The return type is now `T | null | undefined`.

Also from the issue: the stylesheet is now exported as `@posit-dev/shinyreact/styles.css` too. With the `.css` name, TypeScript matches a `*.css` module declaration (for example `vite/client`), so no `declare module` is needed. The old `./styles` export stays.

Note: the type change may make existing TypeScript callers handle `null`. That is the point, but it can show up as new type errors on upgrade.
